title: Checker owns expression operand checks: lvalues, address-of, members, callees, argument counts, builtin arity and operand types
description: Have the checker call TypeResolver::typed on every evaluated expression and report Rejected typer errors, then make the typer (not lowering) the owner of: 'expression is not assignable', 'address of a bit-field/temporary/vector element/register variable', 'unknown member', 'member of incomplete or non-record', 'non-function callee', 'call argument count', 'vector index is not an integer', 'noninteger pointer offset', 'incompatible pointer subtraction', 'non-numeric unary plus', 'sizeof of incomplete type', 'typeof applied to a bit-field', 'predefined name outside a function', 'bit cast to void/array', va/overflow/atomic/classify/shuffle/addressof builtin arity and operand checks (atomic.rs, expression.rs), asm 'asm input tied to a non-output', and the operand checks in numeric.rs (vector/complex operator, non-numeric operand, InvalidOperands/InvalidOperand) and ctype/arith.rs. title: Share the initializer current-object walk with the checker; move initializer checks and braced-element conversions into it
description: initializer.rs's current-object walk (fill/designate/resume, GNU ranges, string arrays, whole-subobject initialization) exists only in lowering, so the checker cannot know the target type of an element inside braces. Factor the walk so the checker runs it over types (inferred_array_length already mirrors part of it as Walk/walk_fill/walk_place) and records per element its target QualType and conversion (reusing the conversion table from the conversions child). Scalar {} / excess scalar elements / empty unknown-length arrays accepted per clang+gcc; inferred length of vector arrays fixed.

title: Checker classifies assignment/argument/return/scalar-initializer/cast conversions; lowering consumes the recorded conversion
description: The static-assertion checker (assertion.rs) becomes the conversion pass. At simple assignment, prototyped call arguments (and default argument promotion for varargs), return (checker tracks the enclosing function's return type), top-level scalar Initializer::Expr and explicit casts it types the operand with TypeResolver::typed, computes null-pointer-constant-ness, and calls CTypes::classify_conversion. Errors become SemaErrors from analyze (so plain 'parse' rejects what --dump-ir rejects today). The result (CastKind + optional warning) is recorded per NodeId in a TypeResolver table; lowering's convert_expr at those sites reads it and emits the cast and warning from it (warning order unchanged, since lowering still emits). A missing record is Internal, not a re-classification. Not covered: conversions inside braced initializer lists (needs the shared current-object walk, see initializer child), atomic/builtin argument conversions, usual arithmetic/promotion conversions (cannot fail on arithmetic operands).
acceptance_criteria: classify_conversion is not called from lowering at the Assign/Arg/Vararg/Return/Explicit sites; ill-formed conversions there are reported by analyze; gate green.

title: Expression typer: variably modified types (VLA casts, compound literals, statement-expression VLA locals)
description: After cc94.4.4 the typer answers every expression lowering evaluates across the gate; the 33 remaining misses are all speculative (typeof/sizeof) operands with a variably modified type: typeof(++i, (int (*)[++i])0), sizeof(*(int (*)[n])p), sizeof(*(int (*)[next()])p), sizeof(*({ n = 20; int (*p)[n] = ...; p; })). TypeResolver::derive needs an extent BindingId in TypeResolver::extents, which lowering creates when it evaluates the size. C evaluates these operands (6.5.3.4p2 sizeof of a VLA; gcc typeof of a VM type), so the fix is not a typing rule but deciding how cc94.4.3 lowers them for real instead of speculatively (e.g. the typer allocates the extent binding and lowering evaluates into it).
close_reason: Typer answers VM operands with provisional vla<T, *> extents (not memoized). sizeof keeps a VLA operand when it has effects; typeof of a VM expression is evaluated where extents are captured; __auto_type reserves extent bindings. 0 speculative misses across the gate; fixes dropped ++i / dangling extent ids in typeof VM declarations (vla-15/16).

title: Expression typer: vector operations, __func__, statement-expression locals, folded null pointer constants
description: After cc94.4.2 the typer leaves ~600 expression nodes unanswered across the gate (from ~29k). Remaining: (1) vector types: unary -/~ on vectors, v[i] lanes, .lo/.hi/.xyzw swizzles, __builtin_shufflevector, vector binary ops; (2) __func__/__FUNCTION__/__PRETTY_FUNCTION__ (char[N] needs the current function name on TypeResolver); (3) statement expressions whose result names a block-scope declaration, typed only after lowering declares it; (4) pointer ?: where null-ness depends on lowering's folding: (void *)(0, 0), (void *)(1 - 1), (void *)'\\0' (typer's integer_zero answers only literals and enumerators). Measure with a temporary SLATE_TYPER_LOG file append in Lowerer::expr when typed() fails.
close_reason: Typer answers vector lanes/swizzles/shufflevector/unary/compound assign, __func__ family, statement-expression locals, and null pointer constants via a shared C 6.6p6 ICE-zero predicate (also fixing too-strict lowering). Lowering-side misses across the gate: 0; remaining speculative misses are VM types (cc94.4.5).

title: Expression typer: calls, builtins and remaining kinds
description: Typer returns Unimplemented for Call (~7.5k unanswered nodes in gcc-torture, the largest gap), builtins (function_like_builtin, derived signatures, atomics, choose_expr, constant_p, source_location), VaArg, OffsetOf, SizeOf*/AlignOf*, TypesCompatible, BitCast, ConvertVector, LabelAddress, Unary Real/Imag, pointer and void ?: (needs null-pointer-constant detection without lowering), predefined __func__, and StatementExpression (needs block-scope declarations typed without lowering). title: Expression typer core: Typed per NodeId, cross-checked against lowering, speculative callers ask it first
description: TypeResolver::typed (sema/typer.rs) memoizes Typed{c, lvalue, bits} per NodeId; Lowerer::expr/place return Internal when it disagrees; speculative_type, unevaluated and unevaluated_type ask it first. Covers literals, identifiers, casts, compound literals, unary, binary, assignment, inc/dec, comma, index, member, _Generic, arithmetic/record ?:.

title: Checker and lowering share one TypeResolver; checker walk becomes the typing pass lowering reads
description: The assertion checker and the Lowerer each build a TypeResolver (separate CTypes arenas), so no per-NodeId QualType table can pass between them. Build the TypeResolver once in Sema, run the checker walk over it, and hand it to lowering, so the checker walk becomes the typing pass lowering reads. The checker and lowering already type expressions with the same typer (cc94.4); lowering's cross-check returns Internal on disagreement.
notes: Tried 2026-09-28 (reverted): Sema built one TypeResolver, ran the checker on it, reset entities, memoized aliases by declarator NodeId and tag failures by TagId, then lowered. 81 fixtures moved. Blocker: the checker's expression typing is lossier than lowering's (typeof goes through assertion_operand_type, not speculative lowering), and whichever walk defines a tag/alias first wins the memo. c99-condexpr-1: typedef __typeof(0 ? v_ip : (void*)0) got the checker's wrong type and lowering then rejected with -Wincompatible-pointer-types. Letting lowering redefine in place instead collides with C23 compatible tag redefinition (same TypeId => redefinition path). So sharing needs the checker to type expressions exactly as lowering does, i.e. cc94.4's typer first. Other needs found: derive Clone on ResolveError (names/Layout too) for a failure memo; define_alias must return its TypeId since lowering annotates the alias; checker resolver warnings come only from define_tag (check_attributes), so they survive sharing without duplication; assertion_scope is a dead field.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move conversion/compatibility checks into the typing pass; lowering returns no Rejected
description: ctype/convert.rs callers in lowering move into the pass that fills the NodeId table, which records implicit conversions and constant values; lowering consumes them. Acceptance: no ResolveError::Rejected constructed under lowering; re-check cxg.15, cxg.31, cxg.42, v74.1.18 samples.

title: One expression typer records QualType and value category per NodeId; typeof/auto_type/classify/unevaluated read it
description: A table filled by lowering cannot serve typeof/sizeof operands, which are never lowered. Instead: one type-only expression pass (subsuming assertion_operand_type) records QualType + value category per expression NodeId; lowering and the five speculative callers (typeof, __auto_type, __builtin_classify_type, classified-operand builtins, unevaluated sizeof/_Generic) read it. Delete speculative_type, Entities::discard_after rollback, the next_id-moved VLA sizeof test, and the place-then-expr Err fallback.
notes: Order flipped 2026-09-28 (see cc94.6 notes): the typer does not need a shared arena. Lowering runs it on its own TypeResolver (compare against lowered operand types there, Internal on disagreement), and the checker runs the same typer on its own resolver for static asserts. Once both walks type identically, cc94.6 can share one resolver.
close_reason: All children done: typer answers every unevaluated operand and the speculative fallback is deleted

title: Replace Option<&Parser> context in const_expr/declarator/attributes with a non-optional context carrying the Dialect

None means standalone mode: const_expr::Parser::new falls back to StandardFeatures::default (the last flavor-blind default after iwsx), and gnu_registered/declspec_registered/c23_registered accept every name. title: Sema writes one NodeId side table (bindings, types, value category, conversions, constants) that lowering reads
description:
Sema produces no shared output. At least four passes resolve names and types from the raw AST independently:
- validate.rs analyze: a HashSet<String> of top-level typedef/tag names plus its own TypeContext.
- assertion.rs: its own TypeResolver with no references map. Likely cause of evdx (typeof(&f) in a static assertion after f's definition).
- module.rs resolve_module: names::resolve_items + TypeResolver + Lowerer.
- types.rs resolve_type_module: its own TypeResolver.

Expression types come from lowering. Five callers need an operand's type without emitting code: typeof, __auto_type, __builtin_classify_type, the classified-operand builtins, and unevaluated (sizeof/_Generic). They go through speculative_type/unevaluated, which lower the operand and then roll back next_id, globals, functions and entities. sizeof on a VLA decides whether the operand is evaluated by lowering it and checking whether next_id moved (expression.rs ~1950). Lvalue-ness is tested with match self.place(e) { Ok, Err(_) => self.expr(e) }, which discards the real error from place().

Because conversion and compatibility checks run during lowering, "IR lowering rejects what clang/gcc accept" is a recurring bug class: cxg.15, cxg.31, cxg.42, v74.1.18, plus constant-evaluation divergence (cxg.44, dyd.62, dyd.69) and ordering bugs (dyd.71).

Goal: sema walks the AST once and records, per NodeId: the binding for each reference, each expression's QualType and value category, its implicit conversions, and its constant value. validate, assertion and lowering read that table. Lowering can then fail only with Unimplemented or Internal, never because the C was ill-formed.
design:
Incremental, each step green on the standard gate:
1. Build one Sema { names, types } once and hand it to validate, assertion and lowering (one name model; drop validate's typedef/tag HashSets). Should fix evdx.
2. Record expression type and value category into a NodeId-keyed table from the current Lowerer; switch the five speculative_type/unevaluated callers to read it, then delete speculative_type, unevaluated's rollback and the place-then-expr fallback.
3. Move conversion/compatibility checks (ctype/convert.rs callers in lowering) into the pass that fills the table; lowering consumes recorded conversions.

Depends on the Dialect epic (single config) and the ResolveError split (to detect regressions by variant). Update wiki/concepts/entity-model.md and c-type-layer.md as the model changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- No speculative_type, discard_after rollback, or place-then-expr Err fallback remains.
- validate, assertion and lowering share one name resolution and one type table.
- Lowering returns no Rejected errors.
- cargo nextest run --release --no-fail-fast passes; re-check evdx, cxg.31, cxg.15 samples.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split ResolveError Unsupported/Invalid into Rejected, Unimplemented and Internal
description:
sema::numeric::ResolveError::Unsupported (239 sites) and Invalid (160 sites) are &'static str buckets that mix three different kinds of failure:

- The C is ill-formed (user error): "excess elements in initializer", "atomic builtin argument count", "unknown typedef", "non-arithmetic operand".
- slate-parser has not implemented the feature yet.
- Internal invariant broken (a slate bug): "missing asm label binding", "missing initializer field type".

As a result, sweep triage (dyd, cxg, v74) requires reading each message to know whether a failure is a feature gap, a fidelity bug, or a crash-class bug, and there's no single place for per-flavor severity or -fpermissive (cxg.10).

Goal: replace Unsupported/Invalid with three variants:
- Rejected(diagnostic): ill-formed C. Carries the per-flavor severity (wiki/concepts/diagnostic-severity.md), which is where -fpermissive plugs in.
- Unimplemented(&'static str): a gap in slate-parser.
- Internal(&'static str): an invariant violation; always a bug.
design:
- Classify all ~400 existing sites; when unsure, verify with clang and gcc whether the construct is rejected.
- Rejected can still be reported from lowering for now; sema-side-table epic moves those checks out of lowering.
- tools/corpus_sweep.py buckets results by variant: Unimplemented -> feature bead, Rejected where the oracle accepts -> fidelity bug, Internal -> bug.
- Remove the old variants once empty; don't keep compatibility aliases.
acceptance_criteria:
- ResolveError has no Unsupported or Invalid variant.
- Every Internal site is an invariant that valid or invalid input alone should not trigger.
- cargo nextest run --release --no-fail-fast passes; error-fixture expectations are regenerated with tools/update_filecheck.py where the wording changes.
close_reason: ResolveError has Rejected/Unimplemented/Internal; no Unsupported/Invalid; sweep buckets by kind

title: One immutable Dialect built at invocation and passed to lexer, pp, parser and sema
description:
Target, flavor, standard and compiler options are fixed at invocation, but each stage rebuilds what it needs from loose pieces, and the rebuilt copies disagree:

- StandardFeatures is constructed in 7 places. parser/mod.rs:375 (with_standard) and sema/names.rs:91 use the flavor-blind StandardFeatures::new; the rest use for_compiler. The parser reads implicit_int, identifier_list_definitions and auto_type_inference — exactly what cxg.14 (gcc implicit int in gnu17) and cxg.16 (gcc K&R in C23) need to vary by flavor, so a fix in for_compiler would never reach the parser.
- options.effective_target(target) is applied at 6 call sites; sema/validate.rs uses the raw self.target.
- default_contraction(flavor, standard) is computed in sema/mod.rs and sema/module.rs separately.
- TranslationUnit carries standard, flavor, target and options as four separate fields.

Goal: the driver builds one immutable Dialect { flavor, standard, features, target: EffectiveTarget, options } after argument parsing. Lexer, Preprocessor, Parser and sema take it in their constructors and read it through self. Not a real global (static/OnceLock): tests run many flavor/triple configurations in one process, and one run per target is the design.
design:
- EffectiveTarget has a private constructor (only Dialect builds it) so a raw TargetInfo cannot reach pp, parser or sema.
- StandardFeatures::for_compiler is called exactly once; StandardFeatures::new becomes private to standard_features.rs.
- Inline semantics and default FP contraction become Dialect fields computed once.
- TranslationUnit holds the Dialect in place of standard/flavor/target/options.
- Do this before cxg.14 and cxg.16.
acceptance_criteria:
- grep finds no StandardFeatures::new, effective_target or default_contraction call outside Dialect construction.
- Lexer/Preprocessor/Parser/TypeResolver/Lowerer have no separate flavor/standard/target fields; they read the Dialect.
- cargo nextest run --release --no-fail-fast passes with no FileCheck changes.
notes:
2026-09-28 step 1 done: src/dialect.rs; Preprocessor::new(search,&Dialect) seeds itself; Parser::new(search, Dialect) replaces with_* builders. Remaining: TranslationUnit holds Dialect; sema (validate.rs, types.rs with_tags, module.rs, sema/mod.rs, names.rs, assertion.rs) reads it instead of rebuilding features/effective_target/default_contraction; then make StandardFeatures::new private.
2026-09-28 step 2 done: TranslationUnit.dialect; sema reads it (Context::for_dialect, TypeResolver::with_tags(unit)); StandardFeatures::new private. Remaining: TypeResolver::constant_value partial Context (types.rs ~400); StandardFeatures::default fallbacks in Lexer/const_expr/Context::new/TypeResolver::new; CompilerArgs could produce the Dialect directly.
2026-09-28 step 3: TypeResolver holds Dialect, constant_value uses Context::for_dialect; Lexer takes features in new; Context::new folded into for_dialect; #if true fixed (7ed218c1). Remaining: slate-parser-iwsx.1 (Option<&Parser> context), CompilerArgs producing the Dialect directly.
close_reason: Dialect built once in dialect.rs (for_compiler + effective_target only there, private fields); pp/parser/lexer/sema/TranslationUnit read it; no StandardFeatures default remains

title: gcc flavor: __seg_fs/__seg_gs named address space keywords on x86
description: TEST SUITE IS RED until this lands: gcc/gcc-dg/bitint-86.c fails with 'expected Comma between parameters'. Since 78x3.2 the gcc flavor uses gcc's predefines. In clang __seg_fs/__seg_gs are predefined macros expanding to __attribute__((address_space(257/256))); gcc instead makes them keywords (x86 named address spaces) and only defines __SEG_FS/__SEG_GS. Lex __seg_fs/__seg_gs as keywords under the gcc flavor on x86/x86_64 and parse them in type-qualifier position with the same meaning as clang's address_space attribute (sema currently ignores address_space: Use::Ignored in src/sema/attributes.rs). Update ast-spec/ast-grammar if Qualifiers changes. Verify with gcc -fsyntax-only; regenerate bitint-86.
close_reason: Closed

title: _FloatN / _FloatNx / __float80 type names unavailable in C11 and older modes under gcc flavor
description:
GCC recognizes _Float16/_Float32/_Float64/_Float128/_Float32x/_Float64x as keywords in all modes (pedwarn before C23), and __float80/__float128 on x86. slate reports `unknown type name`. Also `_Fract` should be an ordinary identifier where fixed-point is unsupported (fixed-point/keywords-ignored-c99.c).

Found by the 2026-09-27 gcc.dg sweep (tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py): 21 gcc.dg files (optimizer-only dirs excluded) where `gcc -fsyntax-only` accepts and `slate-parser parse --flavor=gcc --dump-ir` fails.

## Error breakdown

- 14 × unknown type name `_FloatN`
- 4 × unknown type name `_FloatNx`
- 2 × unknown type name `__floatN`
- 1 × expected declarator

## Migrate on fix

Copy each into tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-dg/<dir>__<name>.c (path separators become `__`), append `// SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc`, `// SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES DEFAULT <defines>`, `// SLATE-FILECHECK-STD DEFAULT <std>`, then `python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>`.

- c11-floatn-1.c → c11-floatn-1.c (-std=c11)
- fixed-point/keywords-ignored-c99.c → fixed-point__keywords-ignored-c99.c (-std=c99)
- c11-floatn-2.c → c11-floatn-2.c (-std=c11)
- c11-floatn-4.c → c11-floatn-4.c (-std=c11)
- c11-floatn-5.c → c11-floatn-5.c (-std=c11)
- c11-floatn-6.c → c11-floatn-6.c (-std=c11)
- c11-floatn-8.c → c11-floatn-8.c (-std=c11)
- c23-floatn-1.c → c23-floatn-1.c (-std=c23)
- c23-floatn-2.c → c23-floatn-2.c (-std=c23)
- c23-floatn-4.c → c23-floatn-4.c (-std=c23)
- c23-floatn-5.c → c23-floatn-5.c (-std=c23)
- c23-floatn-6.c → c23-floatn-6.c (-std=c23)

## Other reproducing files (9)

c23-floatn-8.c const-float80-ped.c const-float80.c pr104511.c pr105211.c pr107967-1.c pr107967-2.c pr107967-3.c torture/pr118184.c

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Raised to P0 (2026-09-27): 78x3.2 switched --flavor=gcc on linux targets to gcc's own predefines (__GNUC__=16, no __clang__). glibc then stops typedef'ing _FloatN (floatn.h: only for !__GNUC_PREREQ(7,0)) and expects compiler-provided _Float32/_Float64/_Float128/_Float32x/_Float64x/_Float128x in ALL modes, and gcc defines __FLT128_*/__FLT32X_* etc. TEST SUITE IS RED until this lands: gcc/gcc-dg/bitint-28.c, -29, -30, -31 (unknown type name _Float128). Also #include <math.h>/<stdlib.h> with -D_GNU_SOURCE --flavor=gcc fails (gcc accepts). Fix: lex _FloatN/_FloatNx as keywords under the gcc flavor (src/lexer.rs currently returns None for them); on x86_64 _Float128 is the same type as __float128 (f128), _Float64x is long double (f80), _Float32/_Float64/_Float32x are distinct types with float/double formats. Regenerate the four bitint fixtures after.

title: Track outermost system header in span provenance
description: Rename Provenance.header to system_header and record the first system header entered from non-system code, so libc declarations retain their public system-header origin through user wrapper headers and nested implementation headers.
design: Maintain an active outermost_system_header during preprocessing. Set it only when entering a system include with no active system header, preserve it through nested includes, and restore it on return.
acceptance_criteria: A FileCheck fixture proves that a declaration reached through a user wrapper reports stdio.h as system_header, nested system declarations inherit that header, user code has no system_header, all fixtures regenerate, and Rust quality gates pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified outermost system-header provenance through user wrapper headers.

title: Make grammar AST nodes intrinsically spanned
description: Move Provenance onto Span and represent source-grammar nodes as AstName = Span<AstNameKind>, preventing construction of unspanned AST nodes. Supersede the per-struct provenance approach from ixa.13 and regenerate FileCheck fixtures.
design: Use explicit mechanical rewrites plus compiler-guided fixes. Keep value-only helper types unspanned. Preserve macro_origin separately from source provenance.
acceptance_criteria: Span carries provenance; grammar AST public node names denote spanned nodes; parser and consumers compile without per-node provenance fields; add.c demonstrates the intended dump shape; all fixtures are regenerated and cargo nextest passes.
close_reason: Implemented intrinsic span provenance and spanned grammar-node aliases; regenerated fixtures and passed quality gates.

title: Implicit int and implicit function declarations by standard mode
description: 'static x;' and 'f() { return 1; }' are rejected with 'unknown type name x'. Clang accepts implicit int in c89/gnu89 and, depending on version and mode, warns or errors in later modes. Calls to undeclared functions already parse, but sema will need the same mode to decide between implicit 'int f()' and an error. Gate both on the language standard from slate-parser-ixa.6, match clang's per-mode behavior, and express implicit int in the AST without inventing tokens. Behavioral metadata stays in slate-parser-lh7.1.10.
acceptance_criteria: c89 fixtures accept implicit int declarations and definitions; c23 fixtures report clang-matching diagnostics.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  static x;
  f() { return 1; }
Observed: 'semantic analysis failed: unknown type name `x`'.
Expected (c89): implicit int declarations accepted. Expected (c23): clang-matching diagnostic.
Fixtures: tests/fixtures/implicit_int_c89.c, plus a SLATE-FILECHECK-ERROR fixture for c23.
close_reason: Implemented C89/GNU89-only implicit int declarations and Clang-aligned later-mode diagnostics with FileCheck coverage.

title: Replace parser panics with diagnostics
description: About 79 panic!/assert!/unwrap/expect sites in the parser and front end (const_expr.rs 36, parser/declarator.rs 19, parser/attributes.rs 9, parser/mod.rs 6, parser/stmt.rs 4, pp/mod.rs 2, parser/asm.rs 2, parser/decl.rs 1). Examples: declarator.rs:857 and :871 panic on malformed array bounds, :746 on field designators, and :620 on _BitInt. Sema cannot produce a verified AST with diagnostics if the parser aborts. Related to span work in slate-parser-1uq.
acceptance_criteria: No panic/assert/unwrap is reachable from source input in the parser or preprocessor; malformed inputs for each former site produce spanned ParseErrors.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro1.c:  int a[1+];
Observed: panicked at src/parser/declarator.rs:871:49: invalid array bound: unexpected token `Plus`
repro2.c:  _BitInt 3 x;
Observed: panicked at src/parser/declarator.rs:620:9: expected `(` after _BitInt
Expected: spanned ParseError, no panic.
Fixtures: one SLATE-FILECHECK-ERROR fixture per former panic site (tests/fixtures/error_*.c).
close_reason: Replaced parser/preprocessor assertion failures with Result-based diagnostics and added malformed-input FileCheck coverage.

title: Name-based pruning drops semantically live declarations
description: filter_translation_unit (src/reachability.rs:4) runs in the parser, before name resolution, and keeps only declarations reachable by name from the main file. A header containing 'void target(void); void via_alias(void) __attribute__((alias("target")));', a 'static inline void release(int*)' used only via __attribute__((cleanup(release))), and '__attribute__((constructor)) static void init_hdr(void){}' loses target, release and init_hdr; the constructor runs at startup, so behavior changes. Move pruning after resolution, as in the ast-spec Migration row, or at minimum root attribute references (alias, weakref, ifunc, cleanup) and constructor/destructor/used/retain.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture with alias, cleanup, constructor, destructor and used declarations in a header keeps every one of them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Model calling conventions in the AST
description: Calling conventions decide the Rust extern ABI but are not modeled. GNU attributes ms_abi, sysv_abi, regparm(N), fastcall, vectorcall, cdecl, thiscall and pcs land in Attribute::Unknown; only Stdcall is typed. MSVC keyword forms fail to parse: 'void __cdecl f(void);' errors with 'expected ;' (also __stdcall, __fastcall, __vectorcall). __declspec(dllimport) and __declspec(align(N)) also fail to parse with --flavor=msvc. Add a typed calling-convention node (attribute and keyword forms, in function and function-pointer declarators) and __declspec parsing.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures for each GNU attribute and MSVC keyword show a typed calling convention on the function or pointer declarator; __declspec forms parse under msvc flavor.
close_reason: Implemented typed GNU/MSVC calling conventions, nested function-pointer support, and __declspec parsing. Generated FileCheck coverage; clippy, fmt, and cargo nextest run passed.

title: Typed AST nodes for pragmas that change semantics
description: '#pragma pack(push, 1)' and '_Pragma("pack(1)")' are dropped today, so struct layout in the IR would be wrong. The same goes for '#pragma weak', '#pragma GCC visibility push/pop', '#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS / FP_CONTRACT / CX_LIMITED_RANGE', '#pragma float_control' and '#pragma ms_struct'. slate-parser-ojp.6 preserves pragmas opaquely; this bead parses the ones that change meaning into typed nodes at their source position. It includes push/pop stacks, so sema can tell which records, declarations and operations each one covers. FP pragmas feed the per-op semantics in slate-parser-ixa.15.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures show pack push/pop/show (both #pragma and _Pragma), weak, GCC visibility and the STDC FP pragmas as typed nodes that sema can scope to records, declarations and functions.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  #pragma pack(push, 1)
  struct p { char c; int i; };
  #pragma pack(pop)
  struct q { char c; int i; };
Observed: exit 0; no trace of the pragma anywhere; p and q are identical tags.
Also dropped: _Pragma("pack(1)"), #pragma weak foo, #pragma GCC visibility push(hidden), #pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON / FP_CONTRACT OFF.
Expected: typed pragma nodes at their positions.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/semantic_pragmas.c
close_reason: Implemented despite stale open dependency ojp.6: semantic pragmas are preserved and typed in the AST with full fixture coverage

title: (T)*x parsed as a cast when a local shadows typedef T
description: typedef int T; int f(int *x){ int T = 1; return (T)*x; } parses as Cast { ty: Named("T"), value: Deref(x) }. T is an ordinary identifier in that scope, so it must be Binary Mul of Paren(T) and x. Plain 'T * x' is already handled correctly; the cast/type-name path (and likely sizeof(T), compound literals, _Generic) does not consult the scoped typedef-name set.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures with a shadowed typedef name in cast, sizeof, compound-literal and _Generic positions parse as expressions; unshadowed cases stay type names.
close_reason: Implemented scoped typedef shadowing in expression disambiguation and added FileCheck coverage

title: LangOptions: compiler flags that change semantics, enshrined by IR lowering
description:
Only -D/-std/-isystem/--flavor are accepted today (anything else is a hard error) and -std is parsed but unused. Add a LangOptions struct on TranslationUnit next to flavor/target, filled by CompilerArgParser, with each flag also setting its predefines.

Rule: flags that only weaken guarantees (-ffast-math, -fno-math-errno, -ffinite-math-only, -fassociative-math, -ffp-contract=fast) need no semantic handling, since strict IEEE output is still correct. They must still set their macros (__FAST_MATH__ etc.). Flags that strengthen guarantees or change meaning must be carried through:
- operation semantics: -fwrapv, -ftrapv, -fno-strict-overflow, -fno-delete-null-pointer-checks, -frounding-math. Sema resolves them per operation and the IR records them on the op (e.g. add<i32, wrap> vs add<i32, nsw>), because #pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT, #pragma float_control and __attribute__((optimize(...))) override them locally.
- type meaning/layout (TargetInfo): -funsigned-char, -fshort-enums, -fshort-wchar, -fpack-struct, -mlong-double-*.
- language: -std (slate-parser-ixa.6), -fms-extensions, -fdollars-in-identifiers, -fgnu89-inline.
- linkage: -fcommon/-fno-common, -fvisibility.
- codegen-only (-O, -g, -fstack-protector): macros only (__OPTIMIZE__, __NO_INLINE__).
The IR module header lists the options that produced it. The Rust lowering reads only operation kinds, never flags. Update wiki/concepts/ir-shape.md and ir-spec.md.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed flag is accepted, sets clang-matching predefines, and has a fixture showing its effect (macro, type/layout, or per-op IR semantics); pragma/attribute overrides show per-op differences.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  int v = __FAST_MATH__;
Command: cargo r -- parse repro.c -ffast-math   (also -fwrapv, -funsigned-char, -fshort-enums)
Observed: 'unsupported argument: -ffast-math' (same for the others).
Expected: flags accepted; __FAST_MATH__ = 1; -funsigned-char flips char signedness; -fwrapv visible on IR ops once lowering exists.
Fixtures: one per flag category (needs a SLATE-FILECHECK directive for arbitrary flags).
close_reason: Closed

title: Box<Stmt> bodies so braces are preserved
description: if/loop bodies are Vec<Stmt>; a braced body is flattened the same as a brace-less statement, breaking the ast-spec invariant that 'if (x) y;' and 'if (x) { y; }' are distinguishable (Migration row). A null statement ';' as Block([]) is acceptable as long as it does not affect the final Rust.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture distinguishes braced and brace-less bodies for if/else/while/do/for/switch.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  void f(int x){ if (x) x++; if (x) { x--; } }
Observed: both Ifs render then_branch: [Expr(...)] identically.
Expected: the second body is a Block.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/braced_vs_unbraced_bodies.c (if/else/while/do/for/switch)
close_reason: Closed as unnecessary: outer control-body brace presence has no semantic effect for valid C and Rust lowering always emits a braced body; nested compound scopes remain explicit Block nodes.

title: Provenance on every declarator and Stmt::Decl
description: InitDeclarator and FieldDeclarator carry no provenance and Stmt::Decl has none (ast-spec Migration row).
acceptance_criteria: Every declarator and block declaration carries Provenance, shown in the AST dump by a fixture covering global, block, for-init and field declarators.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  int g; void f(void){ int a, b; }
Observed: the top-level Declaration carries provenance; the InitDeclarators and the block Stmt::Decl carry none.
Expected: provenance on every declarator and block declaration.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/declarator_provenance.c (the dump can show it once the fields exist).
close_reason: Closed

title: Keep enum fixed underlying type
description: 'enum small : unsigned char { A = 1, B };' parses, but TagDefinition drops the ': unsigned char'. Add fixed_type to the enum tag body (ast-spec Migration row).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture shows fixed_type on the enum definition.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  enum small : unsigned char { A = 1, B };
Observed: TagDefinition has name/body only; ': unsigned char' is gone.
Expected: fixed_type: unsigned char on the enum body.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/enum_fixed_underlying_type.c
close_reason: TagBody::Enum { fixed_type, enumerators }; accepted in all standards like clang/gcc; fixture enum_fixed_underlying_type.c

title: Single qualifier encoding
description: Qualifiers live in both DeclarationSpecifiers.qualifiers and CType::Qualified (plus FunctionDecl.qualifiers). Pick one place so sema never has to merge them. Coordinate with the TypeSpecifier split in slate-parser-lh7.3.5.
acceptance_criteria: Qualifiers appear in exactly one AST location per written position; ast-spec updated.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  void f(const int a);
  const int b;
Observed: parameter a -> ty: Qualified { is_const, Integer } (CType::Qualified); b -> specifiers.qualifiers { is_const } with plain Integer ty. The same written const lands in two different places.
Expected: one encoding.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/qualifier_single_encoding.c (params, globals, locals, typedef'd T, casts, fields)
close_reason: qualifiers only in DeclarationSpecifiers and Pointer declarators; fixture qualifier_single_encoding.c

title: Add a NodeId to Span
description: The IR spec keys metadata by NodeId, but AST nodes have no identity; Span locations are ambiguous (all nodes from one SQUARE(x) expansion share an expansion Loc). Add a unique id to Span<T>, allocated by the parser, so sema can attach metadata by id.
acceptance_criteria: Every spanned AST node has a unique NodeId within the TranslationUnit; a renderer/FileCheck mode prints ids, and a macro-expansion fixture shows distinct ids for nodes sharing an expansion Loc.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  #define SQUARE(x) ((x)*(x))
  int f(int x){ return SQUARE(x); }
Observed: no node identity; the Paren/Binary/Identifier nodes from SQUARE(x) share one expansion Loc, so Loc can't key metadata.
Expected: a unique NodeId on every Span.
Test needs a renderer mode that prints ids (e.g. --show-ids); the fixture checks the ids are distinct.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/node_ids_macro_expansion.c
close_reason: Added Span<T>.id: NodeId, a globally unique id allocated by an atomic counter in Span::new/Span::cover (with_value/map keep the original id since they relabel the same node). slate-parser parse --show-ids prints it on every Span in the debug dump (thread-local toggle read by Span's Debug impl); tools/update_filecheck.py and tests/filecheck.rs gained a // SLATE-FILECHECK-SHOW-IDS <prefix> directive to enable it per fixture config. New fixture tests/fixtures/node_ids_macro_expansion.c (the SQUARE(x) repro from the bead notes) shows the two macro-expanded Identifier("x") nodes getting distinct ids despite sharing one expansion Loc. Updated wiki/concepts/ast-spec.md. cargo clippy/fmt/nextest all green. See wiki/log/2026-09-14-13-27.md.

title: _Alignof expr fails with an out-of-bounds error span
description: 'int g(int x){ return _Alignof x; }' fails with 'expected (, found x' (const_expr.rs:1263 requires a parenthesized type name), and the diagnostic label is out of bounds: '[Failed to read contents for label <none> (offset: 0, length: 39): OutOfBounds]'. Add AlignOfExpr (GNU _Alignof/__alignof__ on expressions) and fix the error span.
acceptance_criteria: _Alignof x and __alignof__(x) parse to AlignOfExpr; a malformed _Alignof produces an in-bounds span.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  int g(int x){ return _Alignof x; }
Observed: 'expected `(`, found `x`' and '[Failed to read contents for label <none> (offset: 0, length: 39): OutOfBounds]'.
Expected: AlignOfExpr(x); malformed forms produce in-bounds spans.
Fixtures: tests/fixtures/alignof_expr.c, plus a SLATE-FILECHECK-ERROR fixture for a malformed _Alignof.
close_reason: Fixed: added ExprKind::AlignOfExpr, _Alignof/__alignof__ now accept an expression operand (mirrors sizeof's two-path structure) instead of erroring or misparsing an identifier as a bogus type name. Root-caused and fixed the OutOfBounds diagnostic span by clamping offset/length centrally in ParseError::new. Added tests/fixtures/alignof_expr.c and tests/fixtures/error/alignof-malformed.c; moved all SLATE-FILECHECK-ERROR fixtures into a new tests/fixtures/error/ directory.

title: Span member names, designator fields, labels and goto targets
description: ExprKind::Member.field, Designator::Field, Stmt::Labeled.label, Stmt::Goto, LabelAddress and LocalLabelDecl hold bare Strings with no location. Make them Span<String> so diagnostics and Rust name mapping can point at them.
acceptance_criteria: Every identifier-bearing AST field is spanned; a renderer/FileCheck mode prints those spans, and a fixture exercises member, designator, label, goto and label-address spans.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  struct p { int x; }; void f(struct p *q){ q->x = 1; l: goto l; }
Observed: Member.field "x", Labeled.label "l", Goto("l") are bare Strings; the dump has no way to show spans.
Expected: Span<String> for each.
Test needs a renderer/FileCheck mode that prints spans (e.g. --show-spans + a SLATE-FILECHECK directive).
Fixture: tests/fixtures/identifier_spans.c
2026-09-14: Structural fix landed (this session). Member.field, Designator::Field,
Stmt::Labeled.label, Stmt::Goto, ExprKind::LabelAddress, and Stmt::LocalLabelDecl
now hold Span<String> instead of String, capturing the span at every parse site
(const_expr.rs expect_field_name/designator/LabelAddress, parser/stmt.rs
Labeled/LocalLabelDecl/Goto, parser/declarator.rs designator loop). See
wiki/log/2026-09-14-13-06.md.

Remaining from acceptance criteria, explicitly deferred per user instruction
("For showing the span, we shouldn't need a test"): the --show-spans /
SLATE-FILECHECK renderer mode and tests/fixtures/identifier_spans.c fixture
were NOT added. Leaving this open until that's confirmed done or dropped.
close_reason:
Structural fix (Span<String> for Member.field, Designator::Field,
Stmt::Labeled.label, Stmt::Goto, ExprKind::LabelAddress, Stmt::LocalLabelDecl)
landed 2026-09-14, see wiki/log/2026-09-14-13-06.md. The --show-spans /
SLATE-FILECHECK renderer mode and identifier_spans.c fixture from the original
acceptance criteria are unnecessary and intentionally not added (per explicit
user decision) — the spans now exist on the AST nodes, which was the actual goal.

title: Gate C23 auto inference and nullptr/true/false on c23 mode
description: C23 'auto x = 1.0;' is parsed as TargetBuiltin("__auto_type") plus storage Auto, conflating storage class with inference. In c23 mode 'auto' without a type specifier is type inference; before c23 it is only a storage class. nullptr, true and false are plain Identifiers; in c23 they are keywords/literals. __auto_type stays a GNU extension in all modes.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures under c17 and c23 show auto as storage class vs inferred type, and nullptr/true/false as identifiers vs literals.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  void f(void){ auto z = 1.0; int *p = nullptr; _Bool t = true; }
Observed: z -> ty TargetBuiltin("__auto_type") + storage Auto; nullptr and true -> Identifier.
Expected (c23): inferred type, nullptr/true literals. Expected (c17): auto is storage only (z is an error/implicit int per clang), nullptr/true identifiers.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/c23_auto_nullptr_bool.c run under c17 and c23.
close_reason: auto x=...; now infers only under c23 (storage cleared, TargetBuiltin __auto_type), stays storage-only pre-c23; nullptr/true/false lex to new ExprKind::NullPtrLiteral/BoolLiteral under c23, plain identifiers otherwise. Fixture: c23_auto_nullptr_bool.c (C17/C23). 41 pre-existing fixtures regenerated (nullptr/true/false were misrendered as identifiers everywhere).

title: Language standard mode (c89/c99/c11/c17/c23), default c23
description: There is no -std mode. Thread a LanguageStandard through CompilerArgs (-std=c89/gnu89/.../c23/gnu23), the preprocessor predefines (__STDC_VERSION__), lexer keyword sets and parser, alongside CompilerFlavor. Default to c23.
acceptance_criteria: -std= is accepted; __STDC_VERSION__ matches the mode; a fixture shows a keyword difference between c17 and c23.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c -std=<mode>). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change; it can't land earlier without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  #ifdef __STDC_VERSION__
  int v = __STDC_VERSION__;
  #else
  int no_stdc_version;
  #endif
Observed: -std=c89 and -std=c23 both give v = 202311; -std is parsed but unused.
Expected (matching clang): c89/gnu89 -> no_stdc_version; c99 -> 199901; c11 -> 201112; c17 -> 201710; c23 -> 202311. Keyword sets differ by mode.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/std_mode_stdc_version.c (needs a SLATE-FILECHECK directive that passes -std per check prefix).
close_reason: Threaded LanguageStandard through CompilerArgs -> Parser -> Preprocessor -> Lexer; __STDC_VERSION__ now matches -std (undefined pre-C99), and bare bool/thread_local/static_assert keyword aliases are gated to c23+. Fixtures: std_mode_stdc_version.c, std_mode_bool_keyword.c.

title: Represent _Alignas separately from the aligned attribute
description: attributes.rs:102-110 parses _Alignas/alignas into Attribute::Aligned, same as __attribute__((aligned)). They have different rules (e.g. _Alignas cannot reduce alignment, is not allowed on typedefs/bit-fields), and the IR should be able to apply different Rust rules to each. Add a distinct node (e.g. AlignAs with expr or type-name operand).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture shows _Alignas(16), _Alignas(type) and aligned(16) as distinct AST nodes.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change; it can't land earlier without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  struct s { _Alignas(double) int a; _Alignas(16) int b; int c __attribute__((aligned(16))); };
Observed: 'semantic analysis failed: layout attribute requires an integer constant expression' at _Alignas(double), so the valid C11 type-name form is rejected. Without field a, _Alignas(16) and aligned(16) both render as Attribute::Aligned(16).
Expected: AlignAs(Type double), AlignAs(Expr 16) and Aligned(16) as distinct nodes; no error.
Fixture: tests/fixtures/alignas_vs_aligned.c
close_reason: Fixed: added AlignAsOperand{Type|Expr} and Attribute::AlignAs, distinct from Attribute::Aligned (the GNU __attribute__((aligned)) form). _Alignas(type-name) now tries a full type-name parse (const_expr::Parser::try_parse_full_type_name, gated on starts_type_name) before falling back to the constant-expression parser, fixing the false 'layout attribute requires an integer constant expression' on _Alignas(double). Regenerated 6 fixtures with the old Aligned(...) shape baked in; added tests/fixtures/alignas_vs_aligned.c matching the bug repro exactly.

title: Parse __real__/__imag__ as unary operators
description: const_expr.rs:1278-1291 turns __real__ c / __imag__ c (and __real/__imag) into Call { callee: Identifier("__real__") }, which name resolution would treat as an unknown function. Add UnaryOp::Real and UnaryOp::Imag.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture shows Unary { op: Real/Imag } for all four spellings.
notes:
Repro (2026-09-14, run: cargo r -- parse repro.c). Test: add it as a FileCheck fixture in the fixing change (python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>); it can't land before the fix without breaking cargo nextest.
repro.c:
  double f(_Complex double c){ return __real__ c; }
Observed: Return(Call { callee: Identifier("__real__"), arguments: [c] }).
Expected: Unary { op: Real, operand: c }; likewise __imag__, __real, __imag.

The rewrite must use promoted parameter types (with the declared type recoverable for the local), and implicit-int parameters stay int. title: (BUG) pp-number paste: name##2_cb pastes to idle2 + _cb because the lexer splits 2_cb
description:
C11 6.4.8: 2_cb is one pp-number, so name##2_cb with name=idle must paste to the single identifier idle2_cb (clang, gcc). slate's lexer splits 2_cb into IntLit 2 and Ident _cb, so ## joins only idle+2 and _cb stays a separate token; the parser then sees idle2 _cb.

Repro (libuv test/test-queue-foreach-delete.c:73): #define D(name) static void name##2_cb(void) {} / D(idle) -> clang: static void idle2_cb(void) {}.

Found by tools/pp_diff.py after slate-parser-ryfo.3; it was hidden behind the signal.h failure before. Fix in the lexer's number scan when lexing replacement lists (pp-numbers absorb [A-Za-z0-9_.] and e+/p+), or re-lex the operand spelling in paste. Acceptance: libuv test-queue-foreach-delete.c same under pp_diff.
close_reason: Lexer numeric_end includes _ so pp-numbers like 2_cb are one token (C11 6.4.8); name##2_cb pastes to idle2_cb as in clang, gcc and cl.exe. Corpus pp_diff now has zero diffs; fixture pp-number-paste.c

title: GNU comma elision: `, ##__VA_ARGS__` keeps the comma when the variadic argument is omitted
description:
Repro (clang and gcc: `f("a"); f("b",); f("c", 1);` / `g(a); g(b,);`; slate: `f("a",); ... g(a,);`):

```c
#define F(msg, ...) f(#msg, ##__VA_ARGS__)
F(a); F(b,); F(c, 1);
#define G(fmt, ...) g(fmt, ##__VA_ARGS__)
G(a); G(b,);
```

When the invocation supplies no variadic argument at all (`F(a)`, as opposed to `F(a,)`), GNU `, ## __VA_ARGS__` deletes the comma. Given an empty variadic argument, gcc and clang both keep the comma. Slate keeps it in both cases, so every logging macro of the form `LOG(fmt, ...)` called with just a format produces a trailing `,)` and fails to parse.

Real-world impact: redis tests/modules/basics.c (`FAIL("Wrong or no reply for foo")`), found by tools/pp_diff.py. The idiom is everywhere in C logging code, so expect more.

Code: substitute_function_macro's `##` branch in src/pp/expand.rs (around line 574), where paste() with empty right_tokens returns `vec![left]`. It needs to know whether the variadic argument was absent or merely empty, which the argument collector has to record. Check the msvc behavior too: cl.exe elides the comma before an empty __VA_ARGS__ even without `##` (tools/cl.exe). C23 __VA_OPT__ is separate. Does not depend on the ryfo.3 rewrite.
close_reason: comma_elision: gnu/clang drop ', ## __VA_ARGS__' when the variadic argument is omitted (H() only in gnu modes); msvc drops the comma before any __VA_ARGS__ empty after expansion. Checked with clang, gcc (gnu17/c17) and cl.exe; redis pp_diff clean; fixture va-args-comma-elision.c

title: Builtin macros (__COUNTER__, __LINE__, __FILE__, ...) are not `defined`, so #ifdef/defined() on them is false
description:
Pp::is_defined (src/pp/mod.rs:959) checks self.macros plus is_defined_operator. The builtins expanded in expand.rs (__LINE__, __FILE__, __FILE_NAME__, __BASE_FILE__, __INCLUDE_LEVEL__, __COUNTER__, __DATE__, __TIME__, __TIMESTAMP__) are in neither, so `#ifdef __LINE__` and `defined(__COUNTER__)` are false. Clang and gcc report all of them as defined.

Repro (clang -E -P prints `has_counter`; slate prints nothing):

```c
#if defined(__COUNTER__)
int has_counter;
#endif
```

Real-world impact: mbedtls tf-psa-crypto/core/tf_psa_crypto_common.h picks MBEDTLS_STATIC_ASSERT through `#elif defined(__COUNTER__)`. Slate falls through to the `extern int (*mbedtls_static_assert_anchor(void))[...]` fallback, and 6 TUs diverge in tools/pp_diff.py (psa_crypto_random.c, psa_crypto_slot_management.c, psa_crypto_cipher.c, psa_crypto_ecp.c, psa_crypto_ffdh.c, psa_crypto_rsa.c).

Fix: have is_defined also recognize the builtin names expand.rs handles, ideally from one shared list so the two can't drift. #undef of a builtin and the msvc behavior (check with tools/cl.exe) need a decision, and fixtures should cover both. Does not depend on the ryfo.3 rewrite.
close_reason: Builtin macros are entries in the macro table marked builtin, seeded per flavor (msvc lacks __FILE_NAME__/__BASE_FILE__/__INCLUDE_LEVEL__ and ignores #define/#undef of its builtins, checked with cl.exe); __TIMESTAMP__ added. mbedtls pp_diff clean; fixtures builtin-macros-defined.c for clang, gcc, msvc

title: Default -std per flavor: clang 22 defaults to gnu17, slate defaults every flavor to gnu23
description:
LanguageStandard's #[default] is Gnu23 (src/compiler_args.rs:48), set on 2026-09-17 (wiki/log/2026-09-17-22-17.md) because gcc 15+ defaults to gnu23 and strict c23 broke the libc shims. But clang 22.1.8 defaults to gnu17 (`clang -E -P` of `__STDC_VERSION__` gives 201710L, slate gives 202311L).

Impact: every corpus TU without -std (sqlite, lua, most of curl/redis) is compiled by slate as C23 while clang checks it as gnu17. glibc then picks different declarations: `typedef typeof(nullptr) nullptr_t` in stddef.h, `__isoc23_fscanf` instead of `__isoc99_fscanf`, and different stdlib.h feature sets (l64a vs strtol at the same point). tools/pp_diff.py found 81+12+1 sqlite TUs diverging this way before it pinned -std=gnu17 on both sides. The README trophy counts were measured at slate gnu23 vs clang gnu17.

Fix: make the default depend on the flavor (clang: gnu17; gcc: gnu23 for gcc 15+; msvc: whatever cl.exe's default maps to), probably through Dialect, since CompilerArgParser builds the standard before the flavor is known. Fixtures without -std rely on gnu23, so expect FileCheck churn. Either add -std=gnu23 to those fixtures or regenerate them; decide per directory and justify it in the log. Afterwards remove CLANG_DEFAULT_STANDARD from tools/pp_diff.py and rerun the trophy sweep.

title: Initializer plan: checker's current-object walk emits a flat plan that lowering's Builder executes
description:
Step 4 of slate-parser-ygrj. See the epic's Target design, point 3. It can run in parallel with step 3.

- check_initializer/check_braced (walk_fill, walk_place, walk_item) produce an InitializerPlan per initializer: an ordered list of { subobject path (field/index chain with union member choice), element expression NodeId or zero-fill, recorded conversion }. GNU [a ... b] ranges replay the designator path per element, and the continuation lands in the last element (see bd memory aggregate-initializer-current-object). A braced sub-initializer replaces its subobject whole.
- Lowering's Builder executes the plan. Delete braced/fill/init_into/item_entry/designate/resume on the Lowerer side and the convert_element compatibility check.
- inferred_array_length reads the plan's extent.
- Oracle: clang -emit-llvm for the designated-range fixtures (designated_range_overwrites.c and the gcc-torture initializer tests).

Acceptance: one walk (checker), the suite is green, and wiki ir/initialization.md and sema-passes.md are updated.

title: Lowering reads result types from the typer's facts; remove the typer/lowering cross-check
description:
Step 3 of slate-parser-ygrj. See the epic's Target design, points 1, 2 and 4.

- Make the facts table total over checked code. Every expression lowering visits has a memoized Typed (including unevaluated-operand paths that lowering does evaluate, such as VLA sizeof and typeof). A missing fact is Internal. Typer failures other than rejections are reported as Unimplemented by the checker. Lowering does not fall back to its own derivation.
- Variably modified types: record the shape with extent slots, and lowering binds the slots (vla<T,*> becomes vla<T,%id>) without re-deriving.
- Lower_expr and lower_place take the node's c from the facts. Delete the remaining checklist entries (members, subscripts, calls, builtins, atomics, statement expressions, _Generic).
- Builtin argument conversions: sizes, memory orders, fetch operands and the other builtin/atomic arguments that lowering still classifies with convert_expr (c-type-layer.md#conversions). The checker records them, as AtomicBuiltin::operands already does for value operands. Lowering applies the recorded steps (the ygrj.2 Step shape).
- Remove the 'expression typer disagrees with lowering' checks in Lowerer::expr and Lowerer::place.

Acceptance: grep 'typer disagrees' src/ is empty, the checklist is fully ticked, and the suite is green.
notes:
From the ygrj.1 audit: expat xmlparse.c:6302 is caused by module.rs:308. Lowering redeclares a function's entity with the definition's declarator type before the body, while the checker merged it through composite, which keeps the typedef sugar. Minimized repro in the ygrj.1 notes; add it as a clang/linux/x86_64 fixture with the fix. Also in scope here: K&R parameter conversion (module.rs:871), VLA extent conversion (module.rs:1388), union_cast_member, elementwise_conversion, swizzle/chosen_expr/generic_selected re-runs.
From ygrj.2: vararg targets in call() (enum_operand + default_promotion) were deferred here with the other convert_recorded targets. &&/|| and unary ! still apply enum_operand before condition(); decide whether a bool test is a Step. The constant folder still uses binary_operand/unary_operand/arithmetic_operands (see the ygrj.1 checklist).
Done 2026-09-30. Checklist resolution:
- Result types: expr/place read facts; cross-check removed. The typer turned out to be total over lowered expressions (FACTGAP probe), so no new rules were needed.
- Member swizzle, _Generic, choose_expr, union cast: recorded in TypeResolver::choices. convertvector's elementwise_conversion is an IR emitter over IR types, so it stays.
- Subscript/callee is_vector/pointee dispatch: shape reads on fact types, kept.
- Place __real/__imag, literals, string/char types, statement expressions, types_compatible: result from facts. Literal values and types_compatible/classify_type constants are still decoded in lowering.
- Builtin/atomic args, varargs, K&R, VLA extents: recorded steps (Slot::Argument/Parameter/Extent). Lowerer::convert is removed. EnumToInt now carries its tail.
- expat: the definition's entity is merged before the body. Fixture function_definition_typedef_type.c.
- VM: handled by the typer typing again under lowering's bound extents (operand_steps, computation, result). A separate extent-slot shape wasn't needed.
- &&/||/!: enum_operand stays with the condition emitter. A truth test is not a C conversion.
Follow-ups: ygrj.6 (lowering re-merges declaration entities), ygrj.7 (constant folder + comparison warnings).
close_reason: Lowering reads result types, choices, and all operand/argument conversions from checker facts; typer/lowering cross-check removed; expat fixed with fixture; suite green (7497).

title: Record operand conversions for binary, unary, conditional and compound-assignment expressions; lowering applies them
description:
Step 2 of slate-parser-ygrj. See the epic's Target design, points 1 and 2.

- Extend record_conversion (c-type-layer.md#conversions) from assignment, argument, return, cast and initializer to every operand the checker types: integer promotions and usual arithmetic conversions on binary and compound-assignment operands (including the computation type of compound assignment), unary promotions, ?: arms to the result type (arithmetic, pointer composite, void, null pointer constant), comparison operands, shift operands (promoted separately), and enum-to-underlying.
- Lowering applies the recorded conversion and emits the op at the recorded type. Delete the lowering-side calls for each migrated ExprKind from the step 1 checklist.
- Fixes the enum ?: case (clang: unsigned int) and the zlib, zstd and mbedtls corpus failures.

Acceptance: the step 1 fixtures pass, the checklist entries for these ExprKinds are ticked, and the suite is green. IR type changes are checked against the clang AST.
notes:
## Design: operand conversion facts (proposed 2026-09-30, from the ygrj.1 discussion)

### Why the current table can't carry this
`TypeResolver::conversions: HashMap<NodeId, Conversion>`, `Conversion { kind: CastKind, warning }`.
- No target type: `convert_recorded(e, value, to, reason)` takes `to` and `value.c` from lowering's own derivation, which is the thing being removed.
- One conversion per node: an arithmetic operand can take several steps (enum -> underlying, integer promotion, usual arithmetic conversion), and each step is its own IR `Convert` node with its own `ConversionReason`. The IR output shape must not change.
- One node in two roles: in GNU `x ?: y`, `x` is both the condition and the then-value. In `a op= b`, `a` is converted to the computation type and the result is converted back to `a`'s type. `insert` silently overwrites the first record today.

### Shape
Key operand conversions by the edge (the operator node plus the operand slot), not by the operand node. This is where clang hangs its ImplicitCastExprs, and it can't collide.

```rust
pub struct Step {
    pub kind: CastKind,          // existing enum covers EnumToInt, Arithmetic, Pointer, NullPointer, Identity...
    pub to: QualType,            // unqualified target of this step
    pub reason: ConversionReason, // Promotion | UsualArith | ... (the reason printed in the IR)
}

pub enum Slot { Left, Right, Operand, Condition, Then, Else, Result }

// on TypeResolver, beside `conversions`
operand_conversions: HashMap<(NodeId /* operator */, Slot), Vec<Step>>,
```

- An empty `Vec` means the checker decided "no conversion". A missing key is `Internal("operand conversion not recorded")`. The two must stay distinguishable.
- Warnings are emitted once at record time, as `record_conversion` does today. `Step` carries no warning.
- Lvalue-to-rvalue and array/function decay are not steps. Lowering's `read` and decay already follow from the typer's `lvalue` flag and the operand's type. Revisit in ygrj.3 if the audit shows lowering picks between them anywhere.
- The existing `conversions` map (assignment, argument, return, cast, initializer, atomic value) stays as it is in ygrj.2. Once `Step` exists, ygrj.3 decides whether to fold it into the edge map (Slot::Argument(n) etc.). That is optional; it isn't needed for correctness.

### Which slots each ExprKind fills
| ExprKind | Slots | Steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arithmetic / bitwise binary | Left, Right | [EnumToInt?] [Promotion?] [UsualArith?] |
| shifts | Left, Right | each promoted separately, no usual arithmetic conversion |
| comparisons | Left, Right | usual arithmetic conversion, or pointer composite / null pointer to the other pointer |
| `&&` / `\|\|` | none | condition handling is unchanged |
| unary `+ - ~` | Operand | [EnumToInt?] [Promotion?] |
| `?:` | Condition (if needed), Then, Else | arithmetic: to the result type. Pointer: composite or null to pointer. Void: none (lowering's `voided` stays) |
| GNU `x ?: y` | Condition and Then both on the same `x` node | the reason for keying by slot |
| compound assignment `a op= b` | Left, Right, Result | Left/Right to the computation type (clang's ComputationLHSType). Result: computation type back to `a`'s type |
| `++`/`--` | per the audit | pointer and bool cases need checking |

The operation's own type is the `to` of the last step on its operands. The C result type is `Typed.c` (read from facts in ygrj.3). `emit_binary` / `emit_unary_arith` stay as IR-level emitters over the converted values.

### Who records
The typer (`typer.rs`) records the steps where it computes the operand types today (`binary_types`, `arithmetic_type`, `promoted`, `conditional_pointers`). `typed` is memoized per node, so each edge is recorded once. Recording from unevaluated operands (`sizeof`) is harmless.

Lowering gets `apply_steps(value, &[Step]) -> Operand`, a loop over `apply_conversion` / `emit_cast` that sets `c = step.to`. `arithmetic_operands`, `promote`, `enum_operand`, `compatible_unqualified` used to choose behaviour, and `convert_expr` in `?:` and comparisons all go away from the Lowerer side.

### Open points for the audit / ygrj.3
- VM types: pointer steps whose `to` has unbound extents (`vla<T,*>`) can't be memoized as-is. Pointer `?:` / comparisons over VM pointers need the ygrj.3 extent-slot binding. Until then, lowering keeps `emit_cast`'s "drop a Pointer cast whose IR types are equal" behaviour.
- Pointer arithmetic index operands: check whether lowering converts the index today (to ptrdiff / intptr). If it does, it becomes a Right step.
- Before claiming the enum `?:` IR change matches clang, check it with `clang -Xclang -ast-dump`.
Fixtures moved here from ygrj.1 (no pending mode): the enum ?: repro, mbedtls cast-arm, zlib nested ?: with a call through a function-pointer member, and expat if minimizing shows it's an operand-conversion case. Add them in clang/linux/x86_64.
Audit additions (see ygrj.1 checklist): switch discriminant promotion (module.rs:1574) and case label conversion (module.rs:1414) are operand conversions of the same shape; do them here. binary_operand / unary_operand (operand.rs) both work out types and emit IR; split them. Expat is NOT a ygrj.2 case: it's the function-definition entity type (module.rs:308), moved to ygrj.3.
close_reason: Operand conversions for binary, unary, ?:, compound assignment, ++/--, subscripts and switch/case are recorded by the checker and applied by lowering. Enum ?: fixed (u32, matches clang). Fixture conditional_enum_arms.c. Suite green. Corpus files not re-run.

title: Audit lowering's typing-rule call sites and pin every corpus typer disagreement as a fixture
description:
Step 1 of slate-parser-ygrj.

- List every place in the Lowerer (expression.rs, module.rs, initializer.rs, atomic.rs, asm.rs, type_of.rs Lowerer halves) that computes a C type or chooses a conversion instead of reading one: arithmetic_operands, promoted, arithmetic_type, compatible_unqualified used to pick behavior, enum_operand, pointer composites, integer_constant_zero decisions and similar. Put the list in the bead notes, grouped by ExprKind, as the migration checklist for the later steps.
- Make the Internal error print both types (typer's vs lowering's) and the ExprKind, so corpus triage shows the cause without a debugger.
- Minimize the libexpat xmlparse.c:6302 case (function designator of a typedef'd function type with XMLCALL/PTRCALL, assigned to a function-pointer member).
- Add clang/linux/x86_64 fixtures for: the enum ?: repro from the epic, the mbedtls cast-arm shape, the zlib nested ?: with a call through a function-pointer member, and the expat shape. These are expected to fail until step 2. The harness has no pending mode, so these move to step 2 (see notes).

Acceptance: the checklist is in the notes, the diagnostic shows both types, and the expat shape is minimized.
notes:
## Decisions (2026-09-30)
- Fixtures move to ygrj.2. The harness has no pending mode, and SLATE-FILECHECK-IR-ERROR would lock in the Internal message as expected output. The expat fixture goes with whichever step fixes it; minimizing it decides that. It may be a function-type identity issue (typedef'd fn type with XMLCALL/PTRCALL) rather than an operand conversion, in which case it goes to ygrj.3 or its own bead.
- Builtin argument conversions (sizes, orders, fetch operands; `convert_expr` from builtin/atomic lowering) belong to ygrj.3.
- The diagnostic needs a new variant, since `Internal(&'static str)` can't carry types. Something like `ResolveError::TypeDisagreement { kind: &'static str, typer: String, lowering: String }`, rendered with `CTypes` display. Add it to the ResolveError table in sema-passes.md in the same change.
- Design for operand conversion facts: see the ygrj.2 notes (edge-keyed `(operator NodeId, Slot) -> Vec<Step { kind, to, reason }>`). The audit must tag each checklist entry with the Slot(s) it needs, and flag any operand node used in two roles.

## Audit method: LSP call hierarchy, names as the classifier
Verified 2026-09-30: rust-analyzer `outgoingCalls` on `Lowerer::lower_expr` (expression.rs:1931) returns 125 calls, each with call-site line:col. Map each call site to its ExprKind arm by line range.

1. Roots: `lower_expr`, `lower_place` (expression.rs); the Lowerer halves of `module.rs` (statement and declaration lowering that touches expressions), `initializer.rs`, `type_of.rs`, `atomic.rs`, `asm.rs`, `function.rs`.
2. BFS over `outgoingCalls`. Recurse only into Lowerer-owned helpers in those files (`binary`, `member`, `subscript`, `call`, `promote`, `convert_expr`, `condition`, `pointee`...). Stop at leaves in other modules and classify them by name. Don't read bodies unless the name is ambiguous.
3. Name buckets:
   - TYPING (checklist entry): arithmetic_operands, arithmetic_type, promote/promote_operand/integer_promotion, enum_operand, binary_types, unary_operand, conditional_pointers, compatible_unqualified / types_compatible / is_arithmetic / is_pointer when used in an `if` choosing a conversion, integer_constant_zero / is_null_pointer_constant, convert_expr / convert_classified (classifies in lowering), classify_conversion, composite, pointee used to pick behaviour.
   - FACT READ (ok): typed, convert_recorded, constant, builtin_callee, chosen_expr, generic_selected, statement_expression_parts, resolve_type_name (declared types), entities.ty.
   - EMITTER / plumbing (ok): operand, value, read, emit_*, apply_conversion, ir_type, storage, layout, access_of, fresh, annotate, std.
   - AMBIGUOUS: read the call site only (not the callee body): `condition`, `truth`, `pointee`, `voided`, `materialize`, `layout_constant`.
4. Known blind spots, to cover with one grep pass at the end: calls inside closures (rust-analyzer attributes them to the enclosing fn, which is fine), calls through `self.types.ctypes.*` predicates used as conditions (these show up as leaves, but whether they choose a conversion needs the call-site line), and macro-generated calls.

## Checklist
(to be filled by the audit, grouped by ExprKind: call site, typing call, Slot(s), which step removes it)
## Checklist (audit done 2026-09-30; line numbers as of the ygrj.1 commit)
Method: LSP `incomingCalls` on each typing-rule function, filtered to Lowerer callers, plus `outgoingCalls` on lower_expr, lower_place, binary, update, subscript, member, call, callee, condition, read, emit_cast. Paths are src/sema/.
Note: rust-analyzer goes stale after out-of-band writes (python/sed). An Edit-tool write to the file resyncs it.

### ygrj.2: operand conversions (Slot in brackets)
- Binary, arithmetic/bitwise/shift (expression.rs:2188-2190 enum_operand on both operands, then `binary` :1682 -> operand.rs:335 `binary_operand`, which does promote_operand + binary_types + arithmetic_conversion + emit). [Left, Right] Split binary_operand: the typing half moves to the typer's record, the emit half stays.
- Binary, pointer arithmetic: `binary` :1689-1700 (compatible, require_pointer_element, ptrdiff_type), `pointer_offset` :1721 -> `promote` :1731 on the index. [Right] (index promotion); the ptrdiff result type goes to ygrj.3.
- Binary ==/!= with a pointer: :2205-2223. Lowering picks the common type itself (is_c_pointer, is_nullptr, pointee) and then calls convert_expr (unrecorded classify_conversion). [Left, Right]
- Binary < <= > >= with a pointer: :2239-2256, same pattern. [Left, Right]
- Binary && ||: condition() :1027 does enum_underlying/enum_integer to bool. [Left, Right] as a condition-to-bool step, or leave it emitter-side if the design says bool tests aren't conversions.
- Unary + - ~: :2151 enum_operand; :2165 promote; :2179 operand.rs:475 `unary_operand` (promote_operand + emit). [Operand] Split unary_operand the same way.
- Unary __real/__imag on non-complex: :2122 promote. [Operand]
- Unary !: :2168 condition(). [Operand] (condition step)
- Conditional: :2347-2398. Lowering's ladder: voided / IR-type arithmetic -> arithmetic_operands / compatible_unqualified + enum_operand + arithmetic_operands / conditional_pointers + convert_expr / pointer-vs-null convert_expr; then compatible_unqualified as a sanity Internal. [Condition, Then, Else] This is the enum ?: bug site.
- Assign compound (a op= b): `update` :1752. bit-field old value promote_operand :1774; `binary` computation; classify_conversion :1779 back to the target type (unrecorded). [Left, Right, Result]
- Pre/post ++/--: go through `update` with a constant 1 rhs, same entries. [Left, Right, Result]
- Place read of a bit-field: `read` :1673 promote_operand(bits). This is the rvalue_type bit-field rule, derived again. [Operand on the read] or record it as the node's rvalue type in ygrj.3. Decide in ygrj.2.
- Statements: switch discriminant promote (module.rs:1574) [Operand on the Switch stmt]; case label convert (module.rs:1414 `case_value`, unrecorded) [Operand on the Case]. Not listed in the ygrj.2 description, but same shape; do them in ygrj.2.
- Call, variadic arguments: expression.rs:78 enum_operand + :82 default_promotion pick the target, then convert_recorded. The kind is recorded but the target is derived. Give the step list its `to`. [Argument]

### ygrj.3: result types, selections, builtin arguments, declarations
- Builtin/atomic argument conversions via unrecorded `convert` (expression.rs:673): custom_builtin :354, :371; real_floating_operand :628; real_floating_pair :645-646; atomic.rs fetch_result :702, lock_free :948 :956, fetch_computation :1065 :1066 :1099 :1104 :1142 :1145, compared_as :1281 :1282.
- Declarations: K&R parameter conversion module.rs:871 (`parameters`); VLA extent conversion module.rs:1388 (`extents`).
- Function definition entity type: module.rs:308 overwrites the entity with the definition's declarator type before the body, while the checker merges through composite (keeps typedef sugar). **This is the expat xmlparse.c:6302 cause.** Minimized:
  ```c
  typedef int F(int);
  static F f;
  F *p;
  static int f(int x) { p = f; return x; }
  ```
  Error: `internal error: expression typer disagrees with lowering on Identifier: typer 'F', lowering 'int(int)'`. clang: DeclRefExpr 'F':'int (int)'. The typer matches clang. A use after the definition agrees. Fixture goes with the ygrj.3 fix. Entity types are checker facts; lowering should read the merged type, not redeclare.
- Member: swizzle (typer.rs:212) re-run at :1399 :1419 for the vector swizzle result; is_record/is_vector dispatch.
- Subscript: is_vector dispatch :1310 :1318 (shape, reads the type; ok once c comes from facts).
- Callee: pointee/is_function dispatch :1627-1629.
- Place __real/__imag: arithmetic_component lower_place :1263; value :2133.
- Generic / __builtin_choose_expr: generic_selected :1597, chosen_expr (typer.rs:637) re-run in lower_place :1165 :1171 and lower_expr. Should read the recorded choice.
- Cast to union: union_cast_member (types.rs:954) at :2034 (picks the member in lowering).
- __builtin_convertvector: elementwise_conversion (numeric.rs:947) at :2652.
- Literals: string_type :1991, character_constant :1969, literal :2472 (shared, low risk, but still a second derivation).
- TypesCompatible: types_compatible :2546 computes the constant in lowering (fine as a fact read if the checker records the value).
- StatementExpression: statement_expression_parts (shared rule).

### ygrj.4: initializers
- initializer.rs:347 `initializes_whole` compatible_unqualified (TypeResolver side, used by both walks); convert_element's check. Covered by the plan.

### Out of epic scope, flagged
- Constant folding: types.rs `constant_value_with_context` (:487) calls promote_operand :560 :655, arithmetic_conversion :561 :686, arithmetic_operands :550, binary_operand :637. That's a third derivation of the operand rules. Once ygrj.2 records steps, the folder could read them too. Decide whether that is ygrj.5 or its own bead.
- Harmless duplicate checks in lowering (Internal, not typing): require_modifiable_lvalue at :2280 and :1761, temporary_rooted.
