title: Lowering merges declaration entity types again instead of reading the checker's merged entities
description: Found in ygrj.3. The checker's declare_object and lowering's declaration paths (module.rs declare_function, the function-definition path, object declarations) both call entities.declare + merge_redeclaration, and lowering also emits the ConflictingTypes warning. Since ygrj.3, expressions no longer read entity types in lowering (Identifier places take the typer's fact), so lowering's merge only feeds declaration IR emission. The two merges run in different orders: lowering used to merge a function definition only after its body (the expat xmlparse.c:6302 bug, fixed in ygrj.3 by merging before the body). Make the checker's merged entity the fact: lowering reads the final type per BindingId and stops calling merge_redeclaration. Watch the point-in-time cases (int a[]; ... int a[10];) where a declaration's IR type is the type at that point.
close_reason: Checker records merged declaration types (declared_types) and warns conflicting-types; lowering reads them and no longer merges; checker declares definition parameters before the function type; suite green (7497).

title: msvc: a user '#define __has_builtin(x) 0' shim is ignored; #if still evaluates slate's own __has_builtin
description: Under --flavor=msvc, #ifndef __has_builtin / #define __has_builtin(x) 0 / #if __has_builtin(__builtin_expect) takes the true branch; cl takes the false one. expand_has_checks evaluates __has_attribute/__has_builtin/__has_feature/__has_extension for every flavor, and expand_condition protects any __has_* name from expansion, so a user macro of that name never expands. Should apply only where the compiler owns the name (is_defined_operator), and a defined user macro should win otherwise.

title: __LINE__ in a function-like macro body: clang uses the line of the closing paren, gcc and slate use the macro name's line
description:
Repro (clang -E -P gives 5, gcc and slate give 3):

```c
#define F(a, b) a b __LINE__
int v[] = { F(1,
  2
  ), };
```

__LINE__ inside an argument uses the argument token's own line in all three compilers, and slate agrees there. Clang sets the expansion location of a function-like replacement to span name..rparen and reports the end, so its __LINE__ is the `)` line. Found by tools/pp_diff.py in cJSON tests/compare_tests.c (unity's TEST_ASSERT_* with multi-line arguments: 168 vs 165).

Fix in the ryfo.3 expander: when the flavor is clang, record the invocation's closing-paren location for builtin-macro evaluation. Keep gcc's behavior for the gcc flavor. The msvc behavior still needs checking with tools/cl.exe.
notes: After ryfo.3 this is the largest remaining pp_diff cluster: about 180 of 188 diff TUs (assert/__LINE__ in multi-line invocations: redis, mbedtls, libuv, zstd, libyaml...). Now unblocked.
close_reason: Per-flavor __LINE__: clang uses the outermost invocation's rparen, gcc the name, msvc the source read position (checked with cl.exe /EP, also /Zc:preprocessor). pp_diff __LINE__ cluster gone; fixtures multiline-invocation-line.c for clang, gcc, msvc

title: Grow ~/c-corpus: add projects chosen to stress distinct C features
description:
Add each project with a compile_commands.json (cmake -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON, or bear -- make), then run tools/c_corpus_sweep.py and file each new failure cluster as a P1 bug under slate-parser-6x05. The stress each project brings is in parentheses.

Tier 1 (small to medium, easy builds, distinct stress):
- xxHash (SSE2/AVX2/NEON intrinsics, heavy macros)
- libdeflate (target attributes, per-function ISA intrinsics)
- mimalloc (C11 atomics, TLS, attributes, builtins)
- lmdb (small, classic systems C)
- jq plus oniguruma (bison output, big switch)
- bzip2 and xz/liblzma (old-style C, liblzma SIMD CRC)
- brotli (large tables, bit tricks)
- libsodium (intrinsics, inline asm, many target attributes)
- stb (stb_image, stb_truetype, stb_sprintf: single-header, macro-heavy)
- miniz
- cglm (_Generic, SIMD, inline headers)
- jansson
- libevent
- c-ares
- nghttp2

Tier 2 (large, real applications):
- git (GNU extensions, huge codebase)
- CPython (computed goto, big macro layers)
- tmux (with libevent)
- BusyBox (GNU extensions everywhere, K&R leftovers)
- GNU make
- dash
- vim or neovim
- libgit2
- libarchive
- libjpeg-turbo (C parts)
- libwebp (SIMD dispatch)
- FreeType
- pixman (SIMD)
- SDL3 (platform macro maze)
- raylib
- micropython

Tier 3 (stretch):
- PostgreSQL (huge, varied)
- OpenSSL (perlasm-generated C, huge macro layers)
- Perl (macro hell)
- Ruby MRI
- PHP
- FFmpeg (inline asm, massive)
- GNU coreutils via gnulib

Acceptance: at least tier 1 is cloned into ~/c-corpus with compile_commands, swept, and its failures filed.

title: Subscripting an array-of-pointers parameter to an incomplete struct fails 'incomplete field type'

Found in gcc.dg/Wmismatched-dealloc.c:137 after cxg.51 fixed its malloc(fclose) attributes; migrate that file (-std=gnu23) into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/ on fix.

title: malloc(deallocator[, index]): resolve the deallocator and keep it as an IR function attribute
description:
Only bare malloc parses; malloc(myfree), malloc(fclose), malloc(__builtin_free), __malloc__(reallocarray) are Invalid. Parse the deallocator as an Expr (like cleanup), name-resolve it to a function BindingId, keep the optional pointer-argument index. Emit it on the IR function as an attribute Slate can use (ownership / Drop). Reachability must keep the deallocator (fclose from stdio.h). Check oracle rules for non-function / bad index. Document the name-argument rule in attributes.md: arguments are resolved references when possible (cleanup, malloc deallocator), strings only when they name assembler symbols (alias, weakref, ifunc).

Files: Walloc-size-4.c, Wcalloc-transposed-args-1.c, Wmismatched-dealloc.c, Wmismatched-dealloc-2.c, Wmismatched-dealloc-3.c, pr118024.c (-std=gnu23 unless the file says otherwise).

weakref applies to functions and variables. Only weakref("t") is parsed; bare weakref is Invalid. Support weakref combined with alias("t") (weakref target = alias target, not an alias definition), including split across redeclarations (attr-weakref-1.c:121-122: static weakref; extern alias("wf1")). _Alignas(E) with enum e { E = _Alignof(max_align_t) } fails 'layout attribute requires an integer constant expression'. title: cleanup attribute: argument is an unresolved, unvalidated name string
description:
Not dropped: sema/module.rs copies the name into Variable.cleanup, printed as [cleanup=f]. But the argument never goes through name resolution or the checker:
- cleanup(nope) with no declaration: accepted (clang: undeclared identifier; gcc: not a function).
- cleanup(f) where 'int f;': accepted (clang/gcc: not a function).
- cleanup(f) where f takes long* for an int local: accepted (clang error: incompatible parameter type; gcc: incompatible pointer type).
- The IR holds a String, not a binding id, so Slate must redo name lookup, and a shadowing local with the same name is ambiguous.
Fix: resolve the argument in names.rs to a BindingId, check in the checker that it is a function taking a pointer compatible with &var (clang rule), and store the binding/function id in Variable.cleanup. Probes: c2/c3/c4 cases above.
close_reason: Closed

title: Plain parse accepts int-conversion assignments that lowering rejects (i = p, i += p)
description: classify_conversion returns an int-conversion warning for pointer->integer Assign; lowering's convert escalates it to an error ('incompatible pointer to integer conversion') while the checker records the conversion without reporting. clang and gcc both error by default. The checker should report the escalated warning so plain parse and lowering agree; covers 'int x = "abc"' too.

title: Too-strict operand rules now diagnosed by the checker: clang pointer-mismatch conditionals, pointer/integer ordered comparison, bit cast to array, atomic pointer offsets
description: Pre-existing rejections that cc94.5.5 moved from lowering into the typer (same strictness, now reported by plain parse). Oracle-verified: (1) clang accepts 'c ? (int*)p : (float*)q' with -Wpointer-type-mismatch and yields void*; slate rejects 'conditional operands are pointers to incompatible types' (gcc errors, so clang flavor only). (2) clang and gcc accept 'p < 1' (warning only); slate rejects 'non-arithmetic operand' in binary_type. (3) clang accepts __builtin_bit_cast to an array type; slate rejects 'bit cast to an array type'. (4) clang accepts __atomic_fetch_add on T** with a floating offset; gcc accepts __atomic_fetch_and on pointers; slate's fetch_rule rejects both. Fix in typer.rs/numeric.rs/atomic.rs rules plus the matching lowering.

Conflicting always_inline/noinline across declarations: gcc warns 'ignoring attribute noinline because it conflicts with always_inline' and keeps the first, clang accepts silently; slate rejects (function.rs record_function, checker function_rules). Found during cc94.5.3.

title: Block-scope typedef redefinition to the same type is rejected as a duplicate name
description: void f(void){ typedef int T; typedef int T; } is accepted by clang and gcc (-std=c11; C11 6.7p3 allows redefining a typedef to the same non-VM type in any scope) but names.rs::bind_ordinary only reuses an existing entry at file scope or for linked names, so it reports 'duplicate ordinary name T'. Too strict.

title: Shrink AbiPass to native_c except where rustc diverges from the C compiler
description:
AbiPass is a label for Slate, not a lowering: rustc's extern "C"/"stdcall"/... computes coerce/sret/byval from the Rust type's layout and field kinds the same way clang does. Precise shapes are only needed where the obvious Rust type would make rustc pass a value differently from the C compiler (per flavor).

1. List the divergent cases. Candidates: _Atomic records (gcc keeps ordinary/HFA passing, clang/msvc do not), long double / __float128 / _Float16 (no stable Rust type with the right class), _Complex on i686 (EAX:EDX vs sret for a two-float struct), unions of floats if emitted as byte arrays, _BitInt, __int128 on i686, vectors without the target feature, i686 char/packed records (slate-parser-hy3i). Verify each with rustc --emit=llvm-ir against clang -emit-llvm and gcc for every supported target.
2. Turn every other record case back to native_c (fewer coerce/byval/sret classifications, e.g. the sysv64/x86 cdecl/aapcs field walks for ordinary records), keeping explicit shapes only for the divergent list, and mark those so Slate knows a boundary conversion is needed.
3. Update ir-spec.md (native_c = trust rustc; explicit shape = rustc diverges) and regenerate fixtures.
close_reason: Records/complex are native_c unless rustc diverges; divergence list verified with rustc --emit=llvm-ir vs clang/gcc per target, table in ir-spec.md; abi_rust_divergence.c fixtures

title: x86 Win32/cdecl returns an empty record in a register or via sret instead of ignoring it
description: clang's X86_32ABIInfo::classifyReturnType ignores a record with no fields (isEmptyRecord) before its small-struct-in-register rule, so typedef struct {} ZeroSized; ZeroSized returnZero(ZeroSized x) returns void under clang --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc -emit-llvm. slate's X86Win32 return path (abi.rs abi_pass -> win32_returns_in_register) has no empty-record case: with MS layout (sizeof 4) it gives coerce<i32>; before 7y5 (sizeof 0) it gave sret<align=1>. Fixture: suites/clang-test/clang/windows/i686/CodeGen__X86__x86_32-fpcc-struct-return.c records the current wrong answer. Check the Linux i686 cdecl return path for the same gap.
close_reason: clang-flavor x86_win32 empty record results are void; cl and rustc return them in registers

title: msvc flavor: implicit function declarations must be accepted (cl.exe warns C4013)
description:
void f(void){ g(4); }

cl.exe /TC /std:c17 accepts with warning C4013 ('g' undefined; assuming extern returning int). clang (and slate --flavor=clang) reject this in C99+, which is correct for the clang flavor. slate --flavor=msvc rejects: "unresolved ordinary name `g`".

The gcc-flavor equivalent is slate-parser-cxg.14; the msvc flavor should reuse that mechanism (implicit `int g()` declaration at file scope) and warn.

description: __declspec(deprecated("a" "b")) and __attribute__((deprecated("c" "d"))) fail with 'invalid arguments for attribute deprecated'; clang accepts. single_string in src/parser/attributes.rs matches exactly one Token::StringLit, used by section/visibility/alias/target/annotate/tls_model/code_seg/ifunc/weakref too. title: Preprocessor is ~28x slower than clang -E on windows.h
description: windows_h_msvc.c: slate preprocess phase 3.1s (154k PP nodes, 274k tokens) vs clang -E 0.11s. Profile after the checkpoint fix lands (parse currently dominates) - build with RUSTFLAGS='-C force-frame-pointers=yes' CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only, perf record -g; without frame pointers libc memcpy/free samples don't unwind. Hot path is under Preprocessor::resolve_and_parse_include/walk_group.
close_reason: Include-cycle macro-state snapshots replaced by clang/gcc's 200-deep include limit; windows.h 3.3s -> 0.8s

title: Report up to 20 sema errors per run instead of stopping at the first
description:
Decided 2026-09-27: sema keeps going after an error to report more of them, but any error still means no IR is emitted. Stop after 20 errors, matching clang's default -ferror-limit ('too many errors emitted, stopping now'); gcc's -fmax-errors defaults to unlimited. This is not recovery: nothing downstream sees a partial module.

Where it aborts today:
- src/sema/validate.rs TranslationUnit::analyze already collects Vec<SemaError> into SemaErrors, so it is not the problem.
- src/sema/names.rs resolve() propagates the first ResolveError with ? out of the visitor (e.g. 'unresolved ordinary name').
- src/sema/module.rs resolve_module() lowers unit.decls with ? on every item, so the first bad declaration ends the run.

Shape: collect errors per top-level item in both passes, continue with the next item, and return them all together (reuse SemaErrors/#[related]). Then stop cascades: a name whose declaration failed should be entered in scope as poisoned, so later uses don't each raise their own error (clang marks such decls invalid). Keep the limit counter in one place and add a final 'too many errors' diagnostic.

Acceptance: a fixture with several independent errors (e.g. two functions referencing different undeclared names) reports all of them and prints no IR; a fixture with more than 20 errors stops at 20 with the limit notice; a use of a failed declaration adds no second error.
close_reason: Sema reports up to 20 located errors with poisoning; no IR on error. Fixtures and wiki updated.

title: GNU asm operands do not keep header names reachable
description: Header globals, typedefs and enumerators used only in a GNU asm statement's output/input operands were pruned before sema ('unresolved ordinary name' / 'unresolved typedef name'); clang accepts. Reachability::mark_stmt treated StmtKind::Asm as a leaf.
close_reason: Fixed: reachability marks GNU asm output and input operand expressions

title: File-scope _Static_assert does not keep header typedefs it uses reachable
description: A typedef declared in an included header and used only in a main-file _Static_assert is pruned before sema, so the IR pipeline fails with 'static assertion requires an integer constant expression: unknown typedef'. Repro: h.h has 'typedef void *HANDLE;'; main has '#include "h.h"' then '_Static_assert(sizeof(HANDLE) == 8, "x");' and slate-parser ir fails; the same typedef in the main file works. Cause: Reachability::mark (src/reachability.rs, DeclKind::StaticAssert arm) marks the decl reachable but not the names in its condition. Found while writing slate-parser-g097 (sizeof(HANDLE) from windows.h); clang and cl.exe accept.
close_reason: Fixed: static assert conditions are now marked in reachability (file and block scope)

title: File-scope _Static_assert rejects a header typedef that nothing else references (unknown typedef)
description: Repro (any target, e.g. default x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu): '#include <stddef.h>' then '_Static_assert(sizeof(size_t) == 8, "x");' fails with 'static assertion requires an integer constant expression: unknown typedef'. Adding 'size_t n;' before the assertion makes it pass, and a typedef declared in the main file works, so header typedefs appear to be materialized only when an ordinary declaration uses them. clang/gcc accept. Found while writing i686-pc-windows-msvc fixtures (slate-parser-9k8k).
close_reason: Duplicate of slate-parser-4opf; fixed by the same reachability change

title: x86 cdecl expands records with sub-32-bit or packed fields instead of passing them byval
description: clang's X86_32ABIInfo::canExpandIndirectArgument only expands a record argument when every field is a 32/64-bit basic type (or pointer/complex of one) and the fields fill the record without padding; otherwise it passes byval align 4. slate's X86Cdecl (and X86Win32, which shares the argument path) expands from record_field_chunks, so e.g. struct { char a; } gives coerce<i8> (clang: byval align 4), struct { char a,b,c; } gives coerce<i8,i8,i8>, a packed struct { char c; int i; } gives coerce<i8,i32>, and an _Alignas(16) int record passed variadically gives coerce<i32>. Verified with clang --target=i686-unknown-linux-gnu and i686-pc-windows-msvc -emit-llvm (same answers on both). Fix in sema/abi.rs record_abi / record_field_chunks.
notes: Another instance: typedef struct {} ZeroSized passed as an argument on i686-pc-windows-msvc. It is sizeof 4 with no fields under MS layout (slate-parser-7y5); clang passes it byval align 4, slate gives x86_win32(coerce<>). See suites/clang-test/clang/windows/i686/CodeGen__X86__x86_32-fpcc-struct-return.c.
close_reason: Superseded by slate-parser-xjv8: x86 cdecl/win32 record arguments are native_c now; rustc's byval matches clang's expand/byval stack layout

title: _Static_assert message rejects adjacent string literals
description: _Static_assert(1, "a" "b"); fails with 'expected static assertion message' (clang and gcc accept; also hits macros like #x " y"). The message parser must accept a concatenated string-literal sequence. Found while writing probes for cxg.9.
close_reason: parse_static_assert now accepts a sequence of adjacent string literals of any encoding

title: Build the target registry and route target consumers through it
description:
First step of the target-registry epic. Introduce one table of supported triples (in or next to src/target_info.rs), each entry holding: the TargetInfo layout, the predefines file for each supported flavor (from the matches in src/pp/mod.rs seed_builtin_macros), sysroot layout (Windows CRT/SDK vs GNU multiarch vs Darwin, from src/sysroot.rs), compiler-header set (src/compiler_headers.rs), AbiConvention (src/sema/abi.rs abi_convention) and VaListKind (target_info.rs va_list_kind).

Route for_triple, seed_builtin_macros, include_paths_at, compiler_headers, abi_convention and va_list_kind through it and delete their private matches and triple-suffix checks. Behaviour must not change: the full filecheck suite must pass unchanged (no regenerated expectations).

Also: an unsupported triple x flavor combination is rejected when arguments are parsed, not mid-preprocessing; add a fixture that runs every registered triple under every flavor it claims (a trivial TU with the predefines/sizeof probes) so an incomplete entry fails the suite. tools/corpus_sweep.py should take its sysroot candidates from slate (or be documented as a mirror). Update wiki/concepts/compiler-arg-rules.md and add a short wiki page on adding a triple.
close_reason: Closed

title: One target registry: every supported triple defined in one place
description:
Supporting a triple today means editing places that key on the target independently, with nothing checking that they agree:

- src/target_info.rs for_triple: string match to a hand-written constructor per triple (layout, long double, wchar, stack alignment).
- src/pp/mod.rs seed_builtin_macros: match on (os, environment, family, flavor) picking a predefines file; an unmatched combination fails at runtime ('no predefines for ...').
- src/sysroot.rs include_paths_at: string suffix checks (-windows-msvc, -unknown-linux-gnu).
- src/compiler_headers.rs: suffix check (-apple-darwin).
- src/sema/abi.rs abi_convention: match on (family, environment); every X86 gets X86Cdecl, so a new i686 Windows triple would silently get the Linux convention.
- src/target_info.rs va_list_kind: match on (family, os).
- tools/corpus_sweep.py: its own copy of the sysroot suffix logic.
- tests/fixtures/<flavor>/<os>/<arch | triple>/: one fixture directory per flavor and triple, resolved through CANONICAL_TRIPLES and OS_DIRECTORIES, which are duplicated in tests/filecheck.rs and tools/update_filecheck.py (wiki/concepts/fixture-layout.md).

A half-wired triple parses and silently uses the wrong predefines, sysroot or ABI (clang on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc had the Linux sysroot layout until v74.1.4).

Goal: one registry entry per supported triple carrying its layout, a predefines file per supported flavor, sysroot layout, compiler-header set, ABI convention and va_list kind. The consumers above read from it instead of matching on their own. A missing flavor/predefines combination is a startup error, and a test runs every triple x flavor through a fixture so a new triple cannot be half-wired. New triples (starting with i686-pc-windows-msvc, slate-parser-9k8k) are then a registry entry plus whatever genuinely new semantics they need.

title: Model x86-32 calling conventions (__stdcall/__fastcall/__vectorcall) in function types and ABI
description:
x86 calling-convention attributes (__stdcall, __fastcall, __vectorcall, __cdecl, __thiscall and __attribute__((stdcall)) etc.) are accepted but dropped. On 32-bit x86 clang makes them part of the function type and ABI; slate does neither. This matters on i686-unknown-linux-gnu today and on i686-pc-windows-msvc once it exists (WINAPI = __stdcall throughout windows.h).

Verified with clang (i686-pc-windows-msvc and i686-unknown-linux-gnu):
- Type identity: 'int __stdcall sc(int)'; _Generic(&sc, int (*)(int): 1, default: 2) == 2. Slate gives 1.
- ABI: 'define x86_stdcallcc i32 @sc(i32)', 'x86_fastcallcc i32 @fc(i32 inreg, i32 inreg)', 'x86_vectorcallcc i32 @vc(i32 inreg)'. On windows the symbols are decorated (_sc@4, @fc@8, vc@@4).
- On x86_64 and aarch64 clang ignores them (warning), so the model applies only when the target is 32-bit x86.

Work: a calling convention on the Function CType (part of compatibility) and on the IR function/signature, printed; ABI: callee-cleanup for stdcall, inreg register assignment for fastcall/vectorcall; symbol decoration on windows as metadata. Oracle: clang -S -emit-llvm; clang tests CodeGen/stdcall-fastcall.c, Sema/stdcall-fastcall.c.
close_reason: Calling conventions are part of the C and IR function type on 32-bit x86 and carried on AbiSignature.calling; inreg/decoration left to the Rust side by decision

title: Support the i686-pc-windows-msvc target (layout, predefines, Win32 struct ABI)
description:
Support the i686-pc-windows-msvc target in both flavors (--flavor=clang like clang-cl, --flavor=msvc like 32-bit cl.exe). Today TargetInfo::for_triple rejects it ('unsupported target triple'); only x86_64/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc exist. The 32-bit MS pointer model (v74.1.6) is only reachable via --flavor=msvc -target=i686-unknown-linux-gnu, which has Linux layout.

Verified with clang --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc vs i686-unknown-linux-gnu:
- Layout: _Alignof(long long) == _Alignof(double) == 8 (linux: 4); struct { char; long long; double; } is 24 (linux: 20). long double is f64, size 8 (linux: x87, 12). long 32-bit, wchar_t 16-bit unsigned, pointer 4/4.
- ABI: small structs are returned in registers: struct {int,int} ret8() lowers to 'i64 @ret8()' (linux: sret). This is clang's X86_32ABIInfo with IsWin32StructABI; slate's AbiConvention::X86Cdecl is the linux form.
- va_list is char* (already true for all X86 in va_list_kind).

Work:
- TargetInfo::windows_msvc for TargetFamily::X86 (pointer 4/4, the scalar alignments above, stack alignment 4 per clang's i686 windows datalayout; verify).
- Predefines: generate src/predefines/clang-22.1.8_i686_windows_msvc.h from 'clang --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc -dM -E -x c /dev/null' (391 lines); wire it and the existing msvc_19.51.36256_x86_windows.h into seed_builtin_macros.
- Sysroot: the Windows include layout is arch-independent; check include_paths_at and slate-sysroots.
- ABI: a Win32 cdecl convention (struct return in EAX:EDX up to 8 bytes, per clang).
- Fixtures under tests/fixtures/sema/i686-pc-windows-msvc/ (layout, predefines, CRT headers, windows.h in both flavors; move ms_mixed_pointers_32_bit.c there).

Out of scope: __stdcall/__fastcall/__vectorcall (see the calling-convention bead), which windows.h uses everywhere (WINAPI) but which only change IR, not parsing.
close_reason: i686-pc-windows-msvc wired in both flavors: layout, predefines, x86_win32 ABI, fixtures. windows.h split to slate-parser-g097 (blocked on MSVC __asm blocks, 25m.6).

title: MS mixed-size pointers: __ptr32/__sptr/__uptr, and __ptr64 on 32-bit targets (parse + type + IR)
description:
MS mixed-size pointers: __ptr32 with __sptr/__uptr on 64-bit targets, and __ptr64 on 32-bit targets. In basetsd.h, POINTER_32 = __ptr32 on _WIN64, along with SPOINTER_32/UPOINTER_32, and inline helpers really use them (Handle32ToHandle, PtrToPtr32; basetsd.h:315-336, 407). Do it as one change: parsing, C type and IR.

Semantics (clang, verified):
- 64-bit target (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): 'int * __ptr32 p' is a distinct pointer type. sizeof == 4, _Alignof == 4, and _Generic(p, int *: 1) is not selected. It converts implicitly both ways with plain pointers without diagnostics; cl.exe warns C4244 'possible loss of data' going 64->32.
- __sptr (the default) sign-extends when widened to a 64-bit pointer, __uptr zero-extends. clang models these as address spaces 270 (ptr32_sptr) and 271 (ptr32_uptr): 'f(int * __ptr32 __sptr s, int * __ptr32 __uptr u)' lowers to 'ptr addrspace(270)' / 'ptr addrspace(271)', with an addrspacecast on conversion.
- 32-bit target (clang i686-pc-windows-msvc, or i686-linux -fms-extensions): 'int * __ptr64' is a distinct 8-byte pointer (address space 272). sizeof == 8, _Alignof == 8, and _Generic((int * __ptr64)0, int *: 1) is not selected. In slate this is reachable with --flavor=msvc -target=i686-unknown-linux-gnu or armv7. The parser currently rejects it there ('__ptr64 on a 32-bit target is not supported'; fixture tests/fixtures/error/ms-ptr64-32-bit-target.c). Replace that error with the real model.
- __ptr64 on 64-bit targets is the plain pointer (done in v74.1.3, dropped in parse_pointer_qualifiers). __ptr32 on 32-bit targets is presumably the plain pointer too; verify with clang.

Work:
- Parse after '*' (in any order with const/volatile/restrict/__unaligned) under MS extensions.
- A CType pointer variant or attribute carrying the width and extension.
- An ir::Type pointer width with storage 4/4 or 8/8.
- ABI (passed as an integer of that width).
- Casts: widening sext/zext, narrowing truncate.
- Printing, plus ir-spec/ir-grammar/type-family-touchpoints.
See wiki/concepts/type-family-touchpoints.md for the match sites.

Oracles: clang --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc -S -emit-llvm, cl.exe /Zs. Clang tests: Sema/MicrosoftExtensions.c, CodeGen/ms-mixed-ptr-sizes.c.
close_reason: MS mixed-size pointers modeled per clang (PointerSpace, address_space_cast); msvc treats sptr/uptr as non-identity like cl

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: After v74.1.3, this is the only blocker for <windows.h>/<winsock2.h> in both flavors: they parse with -D__ptr32= -D__sptr= -D__uptr=. First hit: basetsd.h:315 'const void * POINTER_32 p'.

title: __unaligned type qualifier
description:
MS __unaligned (winnt.h:519 'typedef WCHAR UNALIGNED *LPUWSTR', UNALIGNED = __unaligned on x64) is not recognised.

Semantics (clang-cl, verified on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc):
- A real type qualifier like const/volatile, allowed before or after the type and after '*'. _Generic(up, int *: 1) is NOT selected for '__unaligned int *up'; '__unaligned int *' is.
- Dropping it warns like dropping const: 'plain = up' gives -Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers (cl: C4090). 'up = plain' is fine.
- Alignment: _Alignof(__unaligned int) == 1, an '__unaligned int ua' global is align 1, _Alignof(__unaligned struct s) == 1, and 'int *__unaligned pu' is align 1. sizeof is unchanged.
- Record layout is NOT affected: struct { char c; __unaligned int x; } is still size 8, align 4.
Needs: an AST Qualifiers flag, the sema qualifier set (compatibility, discard diagnostics), object/_Alignof alignment, printers and grammar docs. Gate: MS extensions.

Oracles: clang-cl -S -emit-llvm, cl.exe /Zs /W4. Clang tests: Sema/address-unaligned.c, Sema/unaligned-qualifier.c.
close_reason: Done in the winnt keywords change; fixtures ms-winnt-keywords-*.c

title: __ptr64 pointer qualifier (no-op on 64-bit targets)
description:
MS __ptr64 after '*' (winnt.h:155 'typedef void* POINTER_64 HANDLE64', POINTER_64 = __ptr64) is not recognised.

Semantics (clang-cl, verified on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc): on a 64-bit target it changes nothing. sizeof(int * __ptr64) == 8 and _Generic(p64, int *: 1) selects int *, so it is the same type as a plain pointer. It combines with other pointer qualifiers ('int * __ptr64 const p'). All of slate's Windows targets are 64-bit, so the parser can accept and drop it. If a 32-bit Windows target is ever added it becomes a 64-bit address space (see the __ptr32 bead). Gate: MS extensions, as for __int64/__pragma.

Oracles: clang-cl, cl.exe /Zs. Clang test: Sema/MicrosoftExtensions.c.
close_reason: Done in the winnt keywords change; fixtures ms-winnt-keywords-*.c

title: __forceinline function specifier
description:
MS __forceinline (winnt.h FORCEINLINE, used by hundreds of inline helpers) is not recognised: '__forceinline int f(void){return 0;}' fails with 'expected declarator'.

Semantics (clang-cl, verified): a keyword under MS extensions (msvc flavor, or clang on *-windows-msvc) meaning __inline plus __attribute__((always_inline)). A plain '__forceinline int f(void){...}' is C99 inline: no external definition is emitted (clang -emit-llvm defines nothing for it), and 'static __forceinline' is internal. In slate's IR that is [inline=always] with the same definition= rules as inline. cl.exe accepts the same forms. Outside MS mode it stays an identifier.

Oracles: clang --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -S -emit-llvm, tools/cl.exe /Zs. Clang tests: CodeGen/ms-declspecs.c.
close_reason: Done in the winnt keywords change; fixtures ms-winnt-keywords-*.c

title: Declaration specifiers only parse in fixed orders (int long, char signed, long const long rejected)
close_reason: Specifiers are collected into a clang-DeclSpec-style set and validated as they are added; every order clang/gcc/clang-cl accepts now parses, incompatible combinations are rejected at the offending keyword

title: Build tools/llvm_lit_sweep.py, run three-way sweep, file clusters, migrate passing tests
description:
Build tools/llvm_lit_sweep.py (a sibling of tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py) and run the three-way sweep described on the epic:
- Split each ~/llvm-project/clang/test *.c file into one configuration per RUN line, and keep the Windows-triple and %clang_cl ones.
- Map the options:
  - -triple i686/x86_64/aarch64 → slate -target and MSVC_ARCH x86/x64/arm64
  - -std → /std:c11|c17|clatest
  - -D/-U carried over
  - -fms-compatibility-version → note it only
- Run slate --flavor=clang and --flavor=msvc, clang-cl and cl.exe; skip .cpp files.
- Status per configuration: all-accept, clangcl-only-gap, msvc-only-gap, shared-gap, clang-only-accepts, all-reject, slate-only-accepts, timeout.
- File one bead per root cause under .1 or .2 with "Migrate on fix" lists, as in cxg.
- Migrate the passing files to tests/fixtures/msvc/clang-test/ with RUN:/CHECK*: stripped; FLAVOR msvc or clang, plus -target.
- About 65 -verify files have expected-error lines and will fail on every compiler; leave them out of the first pass.

The header beads in this epic only affect the 46 files that #include system headers. The sweep can run before they are fixed; report those files separately.
close_reason: Sweep tool built and run: 161 configs, 13 cluster beads filed under v74.1/v74.2, 200 fixtures migrated to tests/fixtures/msvc/clang-test

title: slate-sysroots: unpinned xwin gives mismatched CRT 14.44 + old UCRT, skewed from cl.exe oracle
description:
Fix in ../slate-sysroots (src/windows_msvc.rs). `xwin splat` runs unpinned (no --crt-version / --sdk-version), and the installed x86_64 sysroot has a mismatched CRT/UCRT pair that differs from the cl.exe oracle:
- The sysroot has MSVC CRT 14.44.35220 (crt/include) with an older UCRT (sdk/include/ucrt: monolithic math.h, no corecrt_math.h, corecrt_math_defines.h, tgmath.h, stdalign.h or stdnoreturn.h).
- The oracle is msvc-wine: MSVC 14.51.36231 + Windows Kits 10.0.26100.0 UCRT.

Consequences:
- crt/include/threads.h:13 uses _UCRT_DISABLE_CLANG_WARNINGS, which only newer UCRT corecrt.h defines. threads.h is therefore broken on this sysroot for everyone: real clang --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc rejects it too.
- <tgmath.h> is missing under --flavor=msvc, while cl.exe finds it.
- Sweep results that include headers would compare slate on one CRT against cl.exe on another.

Fix:
- Pass --crt-version and --sdk-version (xwin 0.10 supports both) so the CRT and UCRT match each other and the oracle.
- Record the chosen versions in SYSROOT-MANIFEST.txt.
- Have `doctor` check that the CRT and UCRT are compatible, e.g. by probing that _UCRT_DISABLE_CLANG_WARNINGS is defined whenever crt/include uses it.

Afterwards re-run the header probe (#include each of the 33 headers, comparing slate --flavor=clang/msvc with clang-cl and cl.exe).
close_reason: slate-sysroots now uses xwin as a library: VS 2026 manifest, CRT 14.51 + SDK 10.0.26100 with the SDK's own UCRT (byte-identical to the msvc-wine oracle's). Doctor checks CRT/UCRT compatibility; SYSROOT-MANIFEST.txt records versions. All MSVC sysroots reinstalled; 4369 slate-parser tests pass.

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Toolchain skew also shows in predefines: the pinned snapshot src/predefines/msvc_19.51.36256_x86_windows.h has _MSC_FULL_VER 195136256, but the local tools/cl.exe is 19.51.36257 (195136257). All other i686 predefines probed (_MSC_VER, _WIN32, _M_IX86, _INTEGRAL_MAX_BITS, _MSC_EXTENSIONS, no __STDC__/_WIN64 under /std:c11) match.

title: winnt.h keywords: __forceinline, __ptr64, __unaligned
description:
Windows SDK declaration keywords that slate does not recognise, reached from winnt.h via <windows.h> once __int64 and __pragma work:
- __ptr32 / __ptr64 pointer qualifiers (plus __sptr / __uptr). winnt.h:155 `typedef void* POINTER_64 HANDLE64;`
- the __unaligned qualifier. winnt.h:519 `typedef WCHAR UNALIGNED *LPUWSTR`
- the __forceinline function specifier. winnt.h:3226 FORCEINLINE; `__forceinline int f(void){return 0;}` fails with "expected declarator"

With these defined away by -D (plus the __int* and __pragma workarounds), windows.h and winsock2.h parse in both flavors. Oracles: clang-cl and cl.exe accept all of them. __ptr32 changes the pointer size (32-bit on x64), so the fix should model it rather than drop it. Clang test coverage: Sema/MicrosoftExtensions.c, Sema/address-unaligned.c, Sema/unaligned-qualifier.c, Sema/attr-ms-forceinline.c.
close_reason: Done in the winnt keywords change; fixtures ms-winnt-keywords-*.c

title: MSVC-only gaps: cl.exe accepts, slate --flavor=msvc rejects
description: Gaps where only cl.exe (tools/cl.exe, msvc-wine) accepts, clang-cl rejects or differs, and slate-parser --flavor=msvc rejects. These are MSVC-specific behaviour that clang does not emulate. The priority is below the clang-cl sub-epic.
close_reason: all children closed

title: gcc flavor: sema rejects conversions GCC accepts (pointer/integer, transparent unions, conditional operands, _Atomic)
description:
Cases GCC accepts without -fpermissive. Includes: transparent_union argument conversion (transparent-union-*.c), gnu89 array init from compound literal/string (gnu89-init-*.c, init-string-1.c), conditional operands with incompatible pointer/types in gnu mode, passing to unprototyped functions whose block-scope prototype went out of scope (Warray-parameter-10.c: `void gia(int[2])` declared at block scope must not stick to the file-scope `void gia();`), `_Atomic` qualifier drop with memcmp/void*, strftime with user-declared struct tm (format/*).

Found by the 2026-09-27 gcc.dg sweep (tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py): 48 gcc.dg files (optimizer-only dirs excluded) where `gcc -fsyntax-only` accepts and `slate-parser parse --flavor=gcc --dump-ir` fails.

## Error breakdown

- 23 × incompatible pointer types
- 9 × invalid in this context: conditional operands have incompatible types
- 4 × invalid in this context: conversion to a function or array
- 4 × invalid in this context: conversion between a struct or union and an
- 3 × incompatible integer to pointer conversion
- 2 × invalid in this context: conditional operands are pointers to incompatible
- 2 × pointer conversion drops _Atomic from the pointee
- 1 × invalid in this context: conversion from void

## Migrate on fix

Copy each into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/<dir>__<name>.c (path separators become `__`), append `// SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc`, `// SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES DEFAULT <defines>`, `// SLATE-FILECHECK-STD DEFAULT <std>`, then `python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>`.

- redecl-6.c → redecl-6.c (-std=gnu23)
- delay-slot-1.c → delay-slot-1.c (-std=gnu23)
- gnu89-init-1.c → gnu89-init-1.c (-std=gnu89)
- transparent-union-4.c → transparent-union-4.c (-std=gnu23)
- c11-null-pointer-constant-1.c → c11-null-pointer-constant-1.c (-std=c11 -Wno-pointer-compare)
- gnu23-tag-composite-6.c → gnu23-tag-composite-6.c (-std=gnu23)
- c11-atomic-1.c → c11-atomic-1.c (-std=c11)
- c99-const-expr-2.c → c99-const-expr-2.c (-std=iso9899:1999)
- setjmp-2.c → setjmp-2.c (-std=gnu23)
- setjmp-3.c → setjmp-3.c (-std=gnu23)
- setjmp-4.c → setjmp-4.c (-std=gnu23)

title: Gate __declspec attributes per flavor and target in attribute_support
description: attribute_support.rs gates __attribute__ and [[scope::name]] spellings but not __declspec. Measured 2026-09-26: clang (windows-msvc, or -fdeclspec) registers only align, allocate, thread, noalias, restrict, selectany, noinline, noreturn, nothrow, naked, code_seg, deprecated, cpu_dispatch, cpu_specific, plus dllimport/dllexport on Windows; anything else is '__declspec attribute X is not supported [-Wignored-attributes]' (not -Wunknown-attributes). Without -fdeclspec on non-Windows clang rejects __declspec outright. cl rejects unknown ones with C2485, and knows naked only on x86 and nothrow only in C++. Today the parser accepts every modeled name under __declspec, so __declspec(dllimport) on an ELF target still sets dll_storage. Needs a declspec column in attribute_support.rs and an ignored-attributes (not unknown-attributes) identity.

title: Avoid repeated token scans when covering spans
description: Nested expression nodes use Span::cover over growing token ranges. Span::cover scans every token to decide whether all macro origins agree, making otherwise linear parsing quadratic on uniformly originated or origin-free input. Introduce reusable range summaries and route parser range coverage through them so each range query is constant time while preserving location, provenance, and macro-origin semantics.
design: Precompute adjacent macro-origin changes per token stream and answer range uniformity in constant time. Keep generic Span::cover semantics for non-indexed one-off uses, and add an indexed range helper for parser inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Large literal-only and macro-heavy expression benchmarks scale approximately linearly; all Span::cover call sites over token ranges use a reusable summary or combine immediate child summaries; AST macro-origin propagation and diagnostics remain unchanged; cargo nextest release passes.
notes: Added SpanRangeIndex, which precomputes adjacent macro-origin changes once for the main ParserInput token stream and each standalone const-expression token stream. Span range queries now derive uniform origin from endpoint run ids and preserve first/last source locations, instead of rescanning all descendants. Routed const-expression nodes and parser range spans through the reusable index. Added literal-only mode to tools/bench_macro_expansion.py. The 50,000-term literal-only #if improved from 4.546s (prior measurement) to 0.198s (~23x); the 50,000-use macro benchmark remains ~1.19s, confirming the scan was quadratic mainly for uniform-origin ranges. cargo clippy/fmt/nextest passed.
close_reason: Introduced reusable token-range origin summaries and routed parser span construction through them. The 50,000-term literal-only #if improved from 4.546s to 0.198s; release nextest passed.

title: Symbol and layout attributes on a parameter are refused where clang accepts them
description:
sema::attributes maps a Symbol or Layout attribute on Subject::Parameter to Unsupported('symbol/layout attribute on a parameter'), so the whole translation unit fails to lower. Measured with clang 22.1.8 on x86_64-linux: __attribute__((weak)) int p, __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) int p and __attribute__((common)) int p on a parameter are all accepted silently, with no diagnostic at all. A parameter has no linkage or storage, so there is nothing to apply and nothing to observe -- but refusing the declaration is category (3), too strict for every compiler, and stops real headers ingesting.

That refusal was a deliberate choice in slate-parser-8lv/the -Wparameter-alignment work ('Use::Ignored passes, everything else is refused rather than dropped'), taken before applicability was modelled. Now that Use::Inapplicable exists, the right answer is to drop these the same way and say so, rather than to error.

Note section("s") on a parameter IS a clang error, so not every case collapses to accept; keep the ones clang rejects rejected. Fixture to update: sema/ir_parameter_attribute_diagnostics.c (ERR_SYMBOL, ERR_LAYOUT).
close_reason: Clang-rejected parameter attributes are Invalid, the rest warn and drop, vector attributes pass

title: Report -Wunknown-attributes for spellings clang does not register
description:
clang reports an attribute it has no handler for -- and one gated behind a target or flavor it is not building for -- under -Wunknown-attributes, not -Wignored-attributes. Measured on x86_64-linux with clang 22.1.8: scalar_storage_order, dllimport, dllexport and any unrecognized __attribute__ or [[vendor::name]] spelling all report 'unknown attribute X ignored [-Wunknown-attributes]'.

slate-parser-dyd.15 gave those the ignored-attributes identity instead, which is the wrong warning name and, for dllimport/dllexport, still applies the attribute into SymbolAttributes on a target where clang drops it. That is wrong IR (a dll_storage marker on an ELF target), not just a warning gap.

Needs: a Warning::UnknownAttributes identity, a registration predicate keyed on target and flavor rather than on the subject, and Attribute::Unknown routed through it.
close_reason: attribute_support.rs gates __attribute__ and [[scope::]] spellings per flavor/target; unregistered spellings become Attribute::Unknown and report -Wunknown-attributes

title: Do not parse asm instruction bodies on the GCC path
description:
Decision: reject the instruction-IR proposal in todo/ir-asm-design.md for GNU extended asm.

Rust asm! is itself a template-with-placeholders format, so translating "movl 8(%[base],%[index],4), %[out]" to "movl 8({base},{index},4), {out:e}" is a substitution at the operand-reference sites. Lowering to mov.i32 mem{base,index,scale,disp} and re-rendering AT&T text returns the same string while acquiring a per-target assembler as a maintenance liability, plus a large Opaque escape hatch that directives, .byte, prefixes, SIMD and every non-x86 target fall into. AsmPiece::{Text, Operand} is already the right body shape; what is missing is the operand model around it (slate-parser-25m.11 through .17).

Instruction reading stays scoped to the MSVC __asm frontend (slate-parser-25m.6), where there are no constraints and effects must be inferred. The shared IR between the two frontends is the operand model, not an instruction IR.

Also out of scope: the MASM / ml64 PROC + directive + unwind layer from todo/msvc-asm-design.md. That is a standalone assembler file format, not C, and has no path into this pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded; todo/ir-asm-design.md reflects it.
close_reason: Decision already recorded in 015014e5: todo/ir-asm-design.md keeps the body as AsmPiece text and structures only operands; logged in wiki/log/2026-09-21-14-35.md

title: Resolve asm constraint letters to register classes
description: AsmConstraintLocation::Letters(String) passes raw GCC constraint letters through to the backend, which would then need per-target GCC constraint knowledge. Resolve during lowering to a class enum: Reg, RegAbcd, RegByte, XmmReg, YmmReg, ... plus Memory, Imm, and Explicit(AsmRegister). x86: r->reg, q->reg_abcd, x->xmm_reg, a->Explicit(rax), i->Imm, m->Memory. Keep the original letters alongside for diagnostics and as an unsupported-constraint fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Constraint letters lower to a resolved register class with the raw letters preserved; unresolved letters fall back explicitly rather than silently; fixture covers r, q, x, a, i, m.
close_reason: Letters lower to AsmOperandClass (reg classes, explicit reg, mem, imm, Unresolved) per target; raw letters kept; fixtures sema/**/ir_asm_classes.c

title: Unify asm operands into one GCC-numbered list with normalized direction
description:
outputs/inputs are separate vectors but AsmPiece::Operand{index} uses GCC unified numbering (outputs then inputs), so every consumer redoes the split arithmetic. Replace with operands: Vec<AsmOperand> in GCC order so the piece index is a direct subscript.

Also normalize direction into a single enum instead of a modifier bag, mapping GCC to Rust:
  "=r"  -> LateOut    (no early clobber: allocator may reuse an input reg)
  "=&r" -> Out
  "+r"  -> InLateOut
  "+&r" -> InOut
Note this is inverted from the naive reading; computing it once here keeps the inversion out of the backend.

Collapse tied operands: AsmConstraintLocation::Matching(n) plus its separate input entry is one Rust inout operand. Resolve the tie during lowering. Keep Commutative and Pic as separate flags, they are not direction.
acceptance_criteria: ir::InlineAsm exposes a single GCC-numbered operand list with a Direction enum; Matching(n) ties are collapsed into one inout operand; fixtures cover "=r", "=&r", "+r" and a "0" tie.
close_reason: ir::InlineAsm::operands is one GCC-ordered list of AsmOperand { kind: In | Out | InOut }, with direction() giving in/out/lateout/inout/inlateout. Full ties ("0", "0,0", "[out]") fold into the output as InOut { input: Some } and pieces renumber; partial ties stay for .15. Parser now rejects the invalid constraint shapes the fold depends on (clang wording, flavor-aware double-tie rule).

title: Record target arch and asm dialect on ir::InlineAsm
description: ir::InlineAsm carries no target or dialect. The Rust backend cannot decide options(att_syntax) vs Intel, cannot map GCC constraint letters to Rust register classes (they are per-target), and cannot apply per-target implicit-clobber rules. Add the target arch and the source dialect (AT&T / Intel, and which side of a %{...|...%} dialect alternation was selected) to the asm node during lowering.
acceptance_criteria: ir::InlineAsm records target arch and dialect; the IR printer emits them; sema/ir_asm.c fixture covers an x86 AT&T asm and the printed header shows both.
close_reason: ir::InlineAsm records dialect (Att on x86, None elsewhere), printed as [dialect=att]. Arch deliberately not copied per node: Module::target.family already holds it. Also fixed %{ %| %} being misread as dialect markers; bare {a|b} on x86 is now the alternation, resolved to the selected side during lowering.

title: Matching library redeclarations must keep builtin status
description: Builtin status is decided by signature alone, as in clang (provenance plays no part; see the libc-identity bead for that). Today any declaration of a builtin name in scope turns its calls into plain calls to the declared function, so '#include <string.h>' + strlen("abc") lowers as call @strlen, while clang keeps the builtin (folds to 3 at -O1). Incompatible redeclarations (int malloc(int)) already lower as plain calls, which matches clang's IR; the -Wincompatible-library-redeclaration text is diagnostic-only and out of scope per the dyd.17 policy. Conflicting __builtin_* redeclarations are a clang error; we accept them as plain calls (permissive, accepted).
acceptance_criteria: A call to a name whose in-scope declaration has the builtin's type lowers exactly as the undeclared builtin would (Callee::Builtin + c_builtin); a declaration with a different type lowers as a plain call to that function. Covered by a fixture with both cases.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unprototyped function declarations: acceptance and argument passing
description:
Split from the function-warning bead (dyd.17), keeping only the part that is not cosmetic. A declaration with an empty parameter list, int f(), and a K&R definition are not lint: C23 removed them, so acceptance depends on the standard, and how arguments are passed to an unprototyped call is an ABI question that the IR has to get right (default argument promotions, no parameter type checking).

clang reports these under -Wdeprecated-non-prototype; that name is the observable, the rule is acceptance plus lowering.

Out of scope: -Wmissing-declarations, -Wsizeof-array-argument, -Wvarargs, -Wreturn-type (already modeled as ir::Fallthrough), and the whole -Wformat family - see dyd.17.
acceptance_criteria: Unprototyped declarations and K&R definitions are accepted or rejected per standard as clang does; calls through them apply the default argument promotions and lower with the right ABI; the named diagnostic fires where clang's does.
close_reason: Closed

title: sizeof of a dereferenced VLA-typed expression drops the extent capture
description:
sizeof(*(int (*)[n])p) lowers to 'mul<u64>(read<u64>(%12), const<u64>(4))' where %12 is never bound -- the IR references a dangling BindingId. Same for the compound-literal spelling sizeof(*(int (*)[n]){(int (*)[n])p}).

sizeof does not evaluate its operand, so the ValueKind::Capture wrapper produced by type_name_extents/with_extents (sema/expression.rs) is discarded along with the operand value, but the resulting Type::VariableArray still names the captured binding, and runtime_size emits a Read of it.

Pre-existing since lh7.2.24; found while implementing lh7.2.35, which is unaffected (it is the value-producing path). Note the two functions in the repro printed the SAME id %12, so the binding is likely allocated once inside a sub-lowering that is then rolled back.

Repro:
  int hcast(int n, int *p) { return sizeof(*(int (*)[n])p); }

C requires the bound to be evaluated here (C11 6.5.3.4p2: if the type is variably modified, the operand IS evaluated), so the fix is to keep the capture rather than drop it.
close_reason:
unevaluated_type (sema/expression.rs) lowered the operand purely to read its type and then rolled back next_id/entities/globals, so the extent captures the operand created were discarded while the resulting Type::VariableArray still named their BindingId -- runtime_size then emitted a read of an unbound id. The recycled next_id is why every affected function printed the same %N.

Fix: unevaluated_type now returns (QualType, Option<Value>). It skips the rollback exactly when the operand allocated new bindings AND its type is a top-level VariableArray, returning the lowered operand (AddressOf for the place case) so its Capture chain survives; SizeOfExpr sequences that value before runtime_size, and effects.rs turns each Capture into a hoisted Temporary. Everything else rolls back as before, including the error path.

Both gate conditions matter. Without the next_id check, sizeof(*q) on an already-captured VLA parameter would emit a noise statement (a pure operand is not suppressed by discard()). Without the VariableArray check, sizeof((int (*)[next()])p) would evaluate next(); clang returns a flat 8 there, verified against clang 22.1.8 -emit-llvm, while it does call next() for sizeof(*(int (*)[next()])p).

Fixture tests/fixtures/sema/variable_length_array_sizeof_expressions.c covers the cast and compound-literal spellings, a side-effecting bound evaluated once, an already-declared VLA pointer (unchanged output), the non-evaluated pointer-typed sizeof, and _Alignof.

title: Mark arbitrary evaluation order for unsequenced expressions in IR
description:
Split out of slate-parser-dyd.14, which was closed because its warning families are all well-defined C. This one is not: an unsequenced modification is UB (C11 6.5p2), so there is no correct order to translate and lowering silently picks one.

Measured on all three oracles, same source, i starts at 1:

  int f(int a, int b) { return a * 10 + b; }
  f(i++, i++)

  clang 22  -O0/-O2   12   = f(1, 2)   final i = 3
  gcc   16  -O0/-O2   21   = f(2, 1)   final i = 3
  MSVC 19.51 /Od,/O2  11   = f(1, 1)   final i = 3
  slate               12   = f(1, 2)

Three distinct strategies, all applying both increments: clang interleaves read/write per argument left to right, gcc does the same right to left, MSVC snapshots both reads before either write. MSVC is silent at /W4. Slate hoists left to right and so matches clang.

Two other unsequenced shapes were probed and all three compilers agree on both, so the divergence is narrow: 'j = (j, --j)' gives 4 everywhere and 'k += (1 + v[k++]) * 2' gives 12 everywhere.

Recommendation: keep one order rather than emulate per flavor.
- Per-flavor emulation would pin three compiler versions' codegen accidents, not documented semantics. gcc's order is a calling-convention artifact and is not guaranteed between releases, so the emulation could silently go stale.
- The flavor mechanism exists for cases where the compilers give the same C different DEFINED meanings (__PRETTY_FUNCTION__ spelling, MSVC accepting what clang rejects). Unsequenced order is the absence of a meaning.
- Rust evaluates arguments left to right, so clang's order is also the one that translates to natural Rust. Reproducing gcc's would mean emitting contorted hoists to force right-to-left.
- Two corpus sites, both in code that is already broken.

What is missing is not the choice but the record of it. Every other UB the IR carries as an attribute the backend consumes: overflow=ub, amount_out_of_range=ub, negative_left=ub, by_zero=ub, min_by_neg_one=ub, fallthrough=ub_if_used. Evaluation order is the gap: the printed IR for the unsequenced f(i++, i++) is indistinguishable from the sequenced, well-defined f(i++).

wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md's 'Hard cases hoisting must respect (evaluation order and sequencing)' list covers f(i++) and never states what happens when the source is unsequenced.

Scope: mark the operation in the spirit of overflow=ub, state the left-to-right policy in ir-spec.md, and pin it with a fixture. A -Wunsequenced diagnostic is also justified here on the project's own criterion, since this is the one family in dyd.14 where the translated Rust can differ from the C-compiled binary.

Corpus sites (2): tests/fixtures/expressions.c (DEFAULT), tests/fixtures/sema/ir_indirect_calls.c (IR); both currently agree across all three compilers.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lex C23 alignof as the _Alignof keyword
description:
Unmasked by slate-parser-dyd.13: the corpus sweep grouped tests/fixtures/c23_language.c (DEFAULT) under its leading #warning, hiding the real failure 'unresolved ordinary name `alignof`'.

C23 6.4.1 makes 'alignof' a keyword spelling of '_Alignof'. src/lexer.rs:705 maps only '_Alignof', '__alignof' and '__alignof__', so 'alignof(int)' lexes as an identifier and reaches name resolution unbound. 'alignas' is already accepted (parser/attributes.rs:120, parser/stmt.rs:233) and '_Alignof' works, so alignof is the only gap.

Fix shape matches the existing 'bool' gate: add a StandardFeatures availability flag and lex 'alignof' as Token::Alignof when accepted, leaving pre-C23 spellings to <stdalign.h>.

Note tests/fixtures/c23_language.c:2576 currently pins the identifier parse, so its AST expectations must be regenerated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower __auto_type and C23 auto type inference
description: TypeSpecifier::TargetBuiltin("__auto_type") reaches sema/types.rs base() and fails as 'target builtin type'. Deduce the declared type from the initializer (lvalue conversion, array/function decay, qualifier stripping) as clang does. Repros: tests/fixtures/gnu_auto_type.c, tests/fixtures/statement_expr_auto_type.c, tests/fixtures/c23_auto_nullptr_bool.c (C23). Split out of slate-parser-dyd.10.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ignore invalid attribute arguments instead of failing lowering
description: parser_grammar_transactions.c fails with 'invalid attribute' on __attribute__((alloc_size(sizeof(enum { T = 2 }), +))). The parser preserves the malformed argument list as Attribute::Invalid and sema/attributes.rs:46 rejects it. Clang warns and ignores the attribute; lowering should do the same so a bad attribute does not sink the translation unit.
acceptance_criteria: parser_grammar_transactions.c produces IR; Attribute::Invalid is ignored rather than an Unsupported error.
close_reason: Premise wrong: clang and gcc both hard-error on the malformed alloc_size argument list (expected expression), and the enum inside it makes the following line an expression, so the function cannot produce IR under any compiler. The IR error is correct; the fixture's value is the parser transaction recovery. Surveyed other Attribute::Invalid cases: all match clang (error) except visibility("bogus"), where clang warns but gcc errors, which is not a too-strict case.

title: Lower GNU variable-size struct members
description: gcc-torture/20010605-1.c fails with 'nonconstant or unknown identifier': a local struct with a member array sized by a runtime variable (typedef struct { char val[size]; } block; where size is an int object). Clang accepts this GNU extension. Array-member extents need the variable-length path that local VLAs already use.
acceptance_criteria: 20010605-1.c lowers to IR with the member array modeled as a variable-length extent.
close_reason: Premise wrong: clang rejects VLA struct members; gcc-only. Kept as an error and folded into dyd.56 (the repro also needs a nested function).

title: [BUG] Apply the mode attribute to resolved types
description: `__attribute__((mode(QI|HI|SI|DI|TI|word|byte|pointer|SF|DF|XF|TF)))` is parsed but never applied, so it is refused with `machine mode attribute`. It replaces the declared type with the machine type of that mode while keeping signedness, and combines with vector_size. Repros: gcc-torture/20020108-1.c, cbrt.c, pr23135.c, simd-1.c, zerolen-2.c.
acceptance_criteria: Integer and floating machine modes select the target type of the named mode, signedness is preserved, mode combined with vector_size resolves, and the five listed fixtures lower with sizes matching clang.
close_reason: Closed

title: [BUG] Carry typedef alignment through the IR type model
description: `typedef int A __attribute__((aligned(16)));` is refused with `typedef alignment attribute`. The alignment belongs to the aliased type: clang applies it to every object of type A, to records containing an A field, and to `_Alignof(A)`, and unlike a declaration-site `aligned`, a typedef `aligned(1)` *lowers* alignment below natural for both clang and gcc. `ir::Type` is structural and desugars typedefs, and ObjectRequest alignment runs through `effective_alignment`, which cannot express the lowering rule, so there is nowhere to put it today. Repros: gcc-torture/align-1.c, gcc-dg/torture__pr52419.c, gcc-dg/torture__pr57748-1..4.c, gcc-torture/20050215-1.c, attribute-expressions.c, layout-attributes.c (9 configurations).
acceptance_criteria: A typedef alignment applies to objects, record fields, and _Alignof of the alias, including alignment below natural; the nine listed configurations lower and match clang -fdump-record-layouts and clang -S -emit-llvm.
close_reason: Typedef alignment carried on CTypeKind::Typedef and applied to fields, objects, and _Alignof; 8 of 9 repros lower and match clang; layout-attributes.c now blocked on mode (dyd.31)

title: Implement MS bit-field record layout for ms_struct
description:
__attribute__((ms_struct)) is parsed and then ignored: layout_record always uses the Itanium algorithm, so bf-ms-attrib.c, bf-ms-layout-3.c and bf-ms-layout-5.c pass the sweep with wrong bit-field offsets. target-type-attributes.c fails earlier on 'declaration attribute'.

slate-parser-dyd.27 added the #pragma ms_struct state and made a record laid out under it an explicit Unsupported('ms_struct record layout') error rather than a silent Itanium layout. The attribute form still silently mislays out, because changing it to an error would regress three fixtures that currently lower.

Work: implement the MS algorithm (each bit-field allocated in a unit of its declared type, a new unit started when the current one cannot hold it, no cross-unit straddling, unit alignment contributing to the record) and drive it from both Attribute::MsStruct and Pragmas::is_ms_struct, replacing the error.

Oracle: clang -Xclang -fdump-record-layouts with -mms-bitfields.
acceptance_criteria: Records marked ms_struct by attribute or pragma lay out with MS bit-field rules and match clang -fdump-record-layouts; the ms_struct Unsupported error is gone; bf-ms-* fixtures check the offsets.
close_reason: Closed

title: Apply region-scoped FP pragmas: STDC FENV_ACCESS/FP_CONTRACT/CX_LIMITED_RANGE and float_control
description:
Split out of slate-parser-dyd.27, which applied the declaration-scoped pragmas (pack, ms_struct, weak, visibility, redefine_extname) and left these.

These differ in kind: they are region-scoped, taking effect for the statements they enclose rather than for the declarations that follow, and the IR has nowhere to put two of them. FloatingSemantics carries only rounding and exceptions, both a single global in numeric::Context; FP_CONTRACT (fused multiply-add) and CX_LIMITED_RANGE (complex mul/div algorithm) have no representation at all.

Work: give FloatingSemantics contraction and complex-range fields, thread the state per region through Lowerer instead of reading it once from CompilerOptions, and have sema::pragmas produce region state rather than a declaration lookup. FENV_ACCESS ON should give exceptions=Observable and dynamic rounding.

Fixtures: stdlib_fp_contract.c, stdlib_fenv_access.c, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range.c, semantic_pragmas.c, pp-pragma-operator.c.
acceptance_criteria:
FP_CONTRACT, FENV_ACCESS, CX_LIMITED_RANGE and float_control change the lowered floating semantics of the statements they enclose, scoped to the enclosing block; the listed fixtures' IR reflects the pragma rather than only the command-line default.

Per compiler flavor (verified clang 22.1.8, gcc 16.2.1):
- Clang flavor: each pragma is an error unless at file scope or at the start of a compound statement ('#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS' can only appear at file scope or at the start of a compound statement); state reverts at the end of the enclosing block.
- GCC flavor: all four pragmas are ignored (-Wunknown-pragmas: ignoring '#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS', etc.); no placement error, and regions keep the command-line semantics (-frounding-math/-ftrapping-math/-ffp-contract/-fcx-limited-range).
close_reason: Region-scoped FP pragmas applied per compound statement; contract=/range= on float arithmetic; clang placement/interlock errors; gcc flavor ignores them. Follow-ups dyd.57-.59.

title: Lower remaining unsupported statements: nested functions, attributed statements, local labels
description: With asm lowered (slate-parser-dyd.2), the corpus sweep still reports 22 configurations failing with "unsupported in numeric IR lowering: module statement". The remaining StmtKind variants that fall through to the catch-all in Lowerer::statements (src/sema/module.rs) are NestedFunction, Attributed (with attributes other than fallthrough), LocalLabelDecl in positions that matter, and Pragma. Representative fixtures: nested-function-definition.c, parser_attributed_statements.c, sema/names_control_labels.c, stdlib_fenv_access.c, gcc/gcc-torture/20010226-1.c. Statement pragmas overlap with slate-parser-dyd.3.
acceptance_criteria: No corpus configuration fails with "module statement"; each remaining StmtKind has an explicit lowering or an explicit, narrower error.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower vector element subscript and vector lvalues
description: `v[i]` on a GNU/ext vector fails IR lowering with 'expected pointer': subscript lowering only handles pointers and arrays, and there is no PlaceKind for a vector lane. 16 corpus configurations fail on this root cause, including tests/fixtures/vector_extension_ops.c, saturating_arith.c, target_stack_builtin_ops.c, gcc/gcc-torture/pr105613.c, pr94412.c, pr94524-1.c, pr94524-2.c, pr126405.c, pr126405-2.c, pr123625-2.c, pr70903.c, pr71626-1.c, pr85169.c, ieee__fp-cmp-cond-1.c, ieee__pr72824-2.c, gcc-dg/torture__pr52402.c. Needs an IR place (or read/insert value pair) for a lane, plus printer, grammar and ir-spec updates.
notes:
Done (2363 -> 2378 accepted, +15, 0 regressions).

PlaceKind::Lane { base: Place, index: Value } prints as lane(place, value): a vector lvalue subscript projects into the place, so v[i] = x stays a write and v[i] += x stays an update over a stabilised base (effects::stable_place hoists both the base and the index). Like a bit-field, a lane is readable and writable but not addressable, so &v[i] is rejected.

ValueKind::Lane { vector, index } prints as lane<T>(value, value) and covers a subscript whose base has no storage — f()[0], (a + b)[i], ((V8)(V64){..})[1] — which three gcc-torture fixtures need. Expression::subscript now lowers the base once and returns either a place or a value; place() rejects the value form and expr() passes it through, which also removed the old double-lowering of the base.

ir-spec.md and ir-grammar.md updated in the same change; tests/fixtures/sema/ir_vector.c gained read_lane/write_lane/value_lane/extended_lane, regenerated with tools/update_filecheck.py.

Overlaps slate-parser-lh7.2.17.7, which also covers ext_vector swizzles (v.x, v.xy, v.lo/.hi); those are still unlowered and no corpus fixture needs them, so that bead stays open for the swizzle half.

Remaining in vector_extension_ops.c: __builtin_shufflevector, filed as dyd.25.
close_reason: Closed

title: Predeclared __func__, __FUNCTION__ and __PRETTY_FUNCTION__
description: C99 __func__ is a function-local predeclared static const char[] holding the enclosing function's name; __FUNCTION__ and __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ are the GNU aliases. Sema reports them as unresolved ordinary names in 6 corpus configurations: assert_compile_time_true.c, assert_runtime_false.c, assert_runtime_true.c, c99.c, gcc-torture/pr58831.c (__func__), gcc-torture/20001011-1.c (__FUNCTION__), gnu_misc_extension_survey.c (__PRETTY_FUNCTION__). Needs the enclosing function's name available during lowering, which sema does not track today (Lowerer has in_function: bool only), plus an internal-linkage string global per use site. Shares that plumbing with slate-parser-dyd.22.
close_reason: __func__, __FUNCTION__ and __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ lower to an internal string global as a char[N] lvalue, so sizeof/indexing/decay all work. __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ splits on CompilerFlavor: bare name under Gcc, full declaration under Clang via the new CTypes::declaration_spelling. Verified byte-for-byte against clang and gcc.

title: Lower CustomTypeChecking Clang builtins
description: Builtins marked CustomTypeChecking get no derived signature from the typed prototype model, because their argument types are computed by Sema rather than declared. The corpus IR sweep still reports ~25 configurations failing on them: __builtin_complex, __builtin_isnan/isinf/isfinite/isunordered/isinf_sign, __builtin_signbit, __builtin_classify_type, __builtin_addressof, __builtin_assume_aligned, __builtin_elementwise_sqrt, __builtin_nondeterministic_value, __builtin_choose_expr. Each needs a handwritten semantic handler.
notes:
Closed out: every CustomTypeChecking builtin the sweep reported is handled.

This pass (2354 -> 2363 accepted, +9, 0 regressions):
- builtins::derived_signature maps a tblgen record to a signature computed from the actual argument types, and the result is routed through the ordinary Callee::Builtin call path. Covers the whole __builtin_elementwise_* family (uniform T(T..) with an integer/floating/arithmetic operand class, Ldexp's T(T,int), Ctlz/Cttz), __builtin_clzg/__builtin_ctzg as int(T[,int]), __builtin_nondeterministic_value as T(T), and __builtin_assume_aligned, whose declared prototype was already accurate (TypeResolver::declared_signature).
- New CustomBuiltin arms: AddressOf (place -> AddressOf, no lvalue conversion), ClassifyType (unevaluated; folds to the GCC type-class code, verified against clang for void/int/char/bool/enum/pointer/real/complex/function/struct/union/array/bitint/vector/string/bit-field) and FloatClassify (__builtin_fpclassify as a nested conditional over FloatClass tests), which blocked gnu_builtins_numeric once clzg was fixed.
- typeof_operand split: speculative_type returns (type, is_bit_field) so classify_type and the derived signatures can see through a bit-field while typeof still rejects it.
- Drive-by: vector copy-initialization (v4si a = b) was rejected as 'aggregate initialized without braces'; Shape::Array now accepts a whole-vector initializer of the same type.

Remaining, filed as dyd.24: vector element subscript (v[i]) still fails with 'expected pointer', which is what keeps saturating_arith.c and target_stack_builtin_ops.c red. Still separate: __builtin_exit/__builtin_FUNCTION are absent from the generated table.
close_reason: Closed

title: Constant-expression arithmetic validation: shift, division, overflow
description:
Split from the original conversion+constant-arithmetic warning bead. This half keeps only what decides acceptance: shift count out of range or negative, division by zero, and signed overflow *in constant-expression contexts* - array bounds, enum values, bit-field widths, static initializers, and #if. In those positions clang rejects the translation unit, so this is constant-evaluation correctness, not a warning.

Explicitly out of scope (dropped, not deferred): -Wabsolute-value, -Wstring-plus-int, -Wconstant-conversion on non-constant truncations, and bit-field conversion. Those produce text and nothing else.

The default-error conversions (-Wint-conversion, -Wincompatible-pointer-types) split out to their own bead.
acceptance_criteria: Constant expressions with an out-of-range/negative shift count, division by zero, or overflow are rejected where clang rejects them, matching clang on the corpus configurations both tools accept. Non-constant contexts are unaffected.
notes: Direct oracle runs: Clang accepts overflow and invalid shifts by default, with oversized 1<<32 folded to INT_MIN. GCC 16.2.1 accepts overflow and oversized left shift but folds 1<<32 to zero; it rejects nonzero left operands with negative shift counts in enum/static initializers, accepts 0<<-1, and sign-fills invalid right shifts. MSVC cl.exe accepts typed 1/0 in enum/static assertions/static initializers and folds it to zero (verified /Zs and /c); invalid typed shifts fold to zero except signed right shift sign-fill. All three reject #if division by zero. Clang/GCC invalid #if shifts fold to zero; MSVC masks shift counts to 6 bits. Implemented flavor-aware typed ICE and PP evaluation, compiler-specific static-initializer validation, and MSVC static-initializer division folding. Generated FileCheck fixtures for GCC/MSVC; direct compiler checks and cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, cargo nextest run --release (1/1) passed. Warning promotion under -pedantic-errors/-Werror remains in dyd.55.
close_reason: Verified Clang, GCC, and MSVC acceptance and values; added flavor-aware constant evaluation and generated fixtures, with release tests passing.

title: Complete function declaration and call warning validation
description: The warning sweep reports missing return-type, deprecated-non-prototype, varargs, format, format-extra-args, incompatible-library-redeclaration, missing-declarations, and sizeof-array-argument diagnostics. Group these around function type, declaration, and call validation.
acceptance_criteria: Function declarations and calls emit the matching named warnings on accepted corpus configurations, with standard and compiler flavor respected.
close_reason:
Won't do as scoped. Policy: implement a rule when it decides acceptance or changes what we lower; do not implement a rule whose only output is diagnostic text.

Per family:
- return-type: the semantics are already modeled. Every function carries ir::Fallthrough (sema/module.rs:132, printed as fallthrough=ub_if_used). Only the text is missing.
- format / format-extra-args: a format-string parser with archetypes and va-arg checking. The largest cost in the bead and zero effect on the IR.
- missing-declarations, sizeof-array-argument, varargs: lint.

The two parts that are not cosmetic were split out: dyd.44 (unprototyped declarations - C23 acceptance plus argument-passing ABI) and dyd.45 (incompatible library redeclaration dropping builtin status, which feeds dyd.20/dyd.23).

title: Match clang attribute applicability: applied vs ignored
description:
The corpus sweep surfaced this as a warning gap (unknown-attributes, ignored-attributes, gcc-compat, visibility, alloc-size, underlying-cv-qualifier-ignored), but the underlying question is not diagnostic text: it is whether an attribute is *applied* or *dropped*. Attribute parsing currently preserves many attributes without deciding applicability per compiler flavor and standard, so attributes that clang ignores can reach lowering and attributes clang applies can be silently dropped.

Getting this wrong produces wrong IR (wrong alignment, visibility, section, allocation size), not just a missing warning. The named diagnostic is the cheap observable of a rule we need regardless; it is a byproduct, not the goal.

Overlaps dyd.37 (invalid attribute arguments failing lowering), dyd.31 (mode), dyd.35 (scalar_storage_order/address_space) - the same applicability surface. Follow the consensus/measurement method in wiki/log/2026-09-21-08-57.md (-Wparameter-alignment).
acceptance_criteria: Each attribute family is applied or ignored as clang does for the fixture's flavor and standard, observable in the IR (alignment, visibility, linkage, size). The corresponding named diagnostic is emitted where clang emits one, with flavor and standard sensitivity.
close_reason: Closed

title: Diagnose discarded values and suspicious control expressions
description: The Clang warning diff reports 42 missing unused-value diagnostics plus unused-comparison, constant-logical-operand, empty-body, parentheses, switch, switch-bool, unsequenced, and tautological comparison families. These require expression-effect and control-flow aware validation rather than IR lowering failures.
acceptance_criteria: For the corpus cases accepted by both compilers, Slate matches Clang's enabled-by-default discarded-value and suspicious-control warning families without warning on value-producing expressions used meaningfully.
close_reason: Closed by design, not implemented. The named families (unused-value, unused-comparison, constant-logical-operand, empty-body, parentheses, switch, switch-bool, tautological-compare) are all well-defined C whose behavior slate already lowers correctly; verified by inspecting the IR for one case of each. The project's rule is that behavior-relevant facts are IR attributes the Rust backend consumes (overflow=ub, by_zero=ub, amount_out_of_range=ub, fallthrough=ub_if_used), not diagnostics, so reproducing clang's style warnings would add nothing the backend can act on. The one family that is genuine UB, unsequenced, is split out as slate-parser-dyd.42.

title: Keep accepted warning directives non-fatal during IR generation
description: At least one Clang-accepted corpus configuration containing #warning reaches the IR sweep as a failure even though preprocessing records it as a warning. Preserve warning severity through the parse/analyze/IR command path.
acceptance_criteria: A source containing #warning emits a warning, exits successfully, and can produce IR unless another error is present.
close_reason: Closed

title: Merge compatible ordinary redeclarations during name resolution
description: Clang accepts corpus cases that currently fail as duplicate ordinary name __finite or T, including gcc-torture/20031112-1.c and parser_declaration_lifetimes.c. Name resolution rejects before C type compatibility and scope/redeclaration rules can merge the declarations.
acceptance_criteria: Compatible redeclarations share one binding/entity, incompatible same-scope declarations retain a diagnostic, and both representative fixtures produce IR.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bind predefined function-name identifiers in function scope
description: Clang-accepted IR configurations fail name resolution for __func__, __FUNCTION__, __PRETTY_FUNCTION__, and __builtin_FUNCTION. These are compiler-provided function-scope string objects or builtins and must be synthesized with the correct spelling, type, and lifetime before expression lowering.
acceptance_criteria: The corpus cases using all four spellings resolve and lower to string-valued IR without source declarations.
close_reason: Closed

title: Complete GNU and complex numeric expression lowering
description: The sweep finds Clang-accepted failures for GNU omitted conditional operands, complex bitwise complement, bit-precise integer literals, floating/type specifier gaps, and nonliteral numeric expressions. Split these into implemented semantic paths while retaining precise diagnostics for genuinely unsupported target-dependent cases.
acceptance_criteria: Representative accepted fixtures for omitted conditionals, complex complement, BitInt literals, and reported numeric forms produce typed IR.
close_reason: Closed

title: Complete aggregate initializer lowering for brace elision and designated ranges
description: The sweep confirms Clang-accepted failures for aggregate initialized without braces and overlapping designated range, including gcc-torture/20060420-1.c and the designated-range corpus case. Model brace elision against C aggregate type structure and preserve GNU range overwrite semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Representative brace-elided and GNU designated-range initializers lower to the correct aggregate IR without blanket rejection.
close_reason: Closed
