title: Complete Slate attribute coverage
description: Track the remaining GNU, Clang, and platform attributes observed in the Slate parent project after the initial typed/C23 attribute slices. Each child must preserve unsupported forms losslessly, add typed variants where semantics are stable, validate malformed or invalid arguments in sema, and use generated FileCheck fixtures rather than hand-written checks.
close_reason: Completed the remaining Slate attribute families across aliases, allocation/result, optimization/control-flow, target/platform, and type/ABI/formatting coverage.

title: Support attribute aliases and expression payloads
description: Normalize GNU double-underscore aliases such as __aligned__, __vector_size__, __nonnull__, __noinline__, __noreturn__, __pure__, __const__, __packed__, and __may_alias__. Preserve or parse expression-valued aligned and vector_size arguments such as sizeof(int) * 4 and 8 + 8, with invalid forms reported by sema.
close_reason: Layout attributes now use Expr payloads, sizeof is lexed and represented in constant expressions, GNU aliases normalize to typed attributes, and generated FileCheck coverage passes.

title: Make frontend errors directly reportable
description: Make FrontendError a miette diagnostic enum and aggregate source-aware SemaError values so callers can use ? without manually formatting or printing diagnostics. Preserve all semantic errors in one report.
acceptance_criteria: FrontendError has PPError, ParseError, and SemaErrors variants implementing miette Diagnostic; TranslationUnit semantic validation returns an aggregate SemaErrors report with source excerpts for every error; main uses ? without manual diagnostic printing; generated FileCheck coverage remains green.
close_reason: FrontendError now transparently reports PPError, ParseError, and aggregate SemaErrors through miette; main uses ? directly and generated FileCheck covers related semantic diagnostics.

title: Unify frontend error reporting
description: Introduce a top-level frontend error boundary with distinct preprocessor, parsing, and semantic error variants. Preserve source excerpts and labels for all three classes and have main render them consistently with phase-specific context.
acceptance_criteria: Preprocessor, parser, and semantic failures have distinct top-level variants; each diagnostic includes source name, source excerpt, and labeled span; main reports phase-specific errors without a second generic failure report; generated FileCheck fixtures cover representative PP, parse, and semantic failures.
close_reason: Added FrontendError::{PP, Parse, Sema} and source-aware miette rendering for preprocessor, parser, and semantic diagnostics.

title: Validate attribute semantics
description: Move semantic validation of structurally valid attributes into the configuration-aware semantic pass. The parser should preserve valid attribute syntax and Sema should diagnose invalid argument types, counts, placements, and conflicts.
acceptance_criteria: Parser accepts structurally valid attribute argument syntax; Sema reports invalid attribute arguments and placements with generated FileCheck diagnostics; malformed attribute delimiters remain parser errors.
close_reason: Structurally valid attribute syntax is preserved through parsing and invalid known-attribute arguments are diagnosed by TranslationUnit::analyze with generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Structural Clang AST oracle after the parser refactor
description: Reactivated by the 2026-09-15 structural-refactor plan. Replace the existing one-way declaration-summary containment check with an explicitly supported common structural projection of Slate AST and pinned Clang AST JSON. Compare declarations/order/counts, expression operators and nesting, type-vs-expression choices, explicit casts, sizeof operands, initializer designators, literals and statement structure. Normalize implicit Clang semantic wrappers without erasing written syntax. Report unsupported constructs explicitly instead of silently skipping them. Pin standard, target, compiler version, defines and include paths for this AST track independently of executable IR-oracle setup. Add reproducible scope/declarator generation and whitespace/comment/macro-equivalence transformations; compare provenance separately. Minimize mismatches into FileCheck integration fixtures. No unit tests; generate CHECK expectations with tools/update_filecheck.py and inspect them.
acceptance_criteria: Missing or extra declarations and wrong sizeof/cast/string nodes fail symmetric comparisons. ixa.27-.31 repros are covered. The AST track runs without IR/sema/interpreter completion. Clang-generated expectations are reproducible with recorded version/configuration; normal nextest can check committed expectations without Clang. No silent unsupported-node filtering.
notes: Previous closure superseded AST projection work when 2lv was scoped exclusively to IR execution. Reopened explicitly for the new AST validation track; original IR work remains intact.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build generated corpus and minimization workflows
description: Generate freestanding, UB-free programs with Csmith and/or YARPGen, seeded reproducibly. Replace the generator runtime headers (e.g. Csmith's checksum/platform hooks) with the harness observe-hook header so no libc is needed on the interpreter side. Minimize failing inputs with cvise/creduce using an interestingness test that keeps clang -O0/-O2 agreement while preserving the interpreter mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: The harness produces reproducible seeds and minimized failures that can be promoted to checked-in regression fixtures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Run differential IR-interpreter vs clang comparison
description: Runner that, per input and concrete configuration (target, -fwrapv/-ftrapv, long double format, etc.), lowers to IR, interprets it, and compares output and exit code with the oracle. Classify outcomes: match, output mismatch, interpreter UB trap, unsupported IR construct (tracked, not a failure), front-end error. Promote minimized reproducers to fixtures run by cargo nextest.
acceptance_criteria: Mismatches identify source, configuration, expected oracle result, actual interpreter result, and a minimized reproducer; unsupported constructs are reported separately from real divergences.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin and invoke the clang oracle reproducibly
description: Define the pinned clang version, target triple, and compile flags used to build oracle binaries, plus capture of stdout (the observe hook) and exit code. Build each input at -O0 and -O2; if they disagree the input has UB or unspecified behavior and is discarded rather than reported. Record tool version and flags alongside generated expectations.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout can regenerate oracle expectations deterministically, reports the clang version/flags used, and diagnoses missing or mismatched clang setups.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implement C type checking and implicit conversions
description: Add recursive type compatibility checks, lvalue rules, pointer conversions, integer promotions, usual arithmetic conversions, function calls, assignments, and return statements.
acceptance_criteria: Supported type errors and conversions produce ordered diagnostics with source provenance and are covered by generated FileCheck fixtures.
notes: Closed 2026-09-19 by epic slate-parser-9ve. Both recorded gaps are fixed: int<->pointer assignment now warns int-conversion (accepted, per MSVC C4047 — clang/gcc reject but MSVC does not, so the three-compiler consensus rule makes it a warning), and assignment, compound assignment and ++/-- to a const-qualified lvalue, an array, or a struct with a recursively const member are ResolveError::Invalid. The wider description (recursive compatibility, lvalue rules, pointer conversions, promotions, usual arithmetic conversions, calls, assignments, returns) is delivered by src/sema/ctype/{compat,convert,arith}.rs with classify_conversion as the single legality decision point. Acceptance met: diagnostics are ordered and source-located, covered by generated fixtures ir_conversion_rules.c, ir_modifiable_lvalue.c, ir_pointer_comparison.c, ir_conditional_composite.c, ir_atomic_pointee.c, ir_c_type_operands.c.
close_reason: Closed

title: Complete constant-expression semantic validation
description: Validate integer constant expressions in contexts requiring them, including enumerators, array bounds, case labels, initializers, and static assertions, after configuration evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid constant expressions produce semantic diagnostics matching clang for supported constructs; valid expressions are accepted.
notes: Verified 2026-09-18 vs clang 22 (-std=c17): these are accepted by slate-parser but clang errors. (1) duplicate case value: 'switch(x){ case 1: case 1: break; }' (2) division by zero in constant expression: 'int x = 1/0;' (3) non-constant global initializer: 'int n; int m = n;'. Already covered: non-constant enumerator, negative array size, non-constant case, negative bitfield width, static_assert failure/non-constant.
close_reason: Remaining clang-only rejections (duplicate case, non-constant static initializer) are rejected by all three compilers, so accepting them is permissive; 1/0 was already handled. Survey fixed the too-strict cases found: pointer->_Bool (dyd.68) and floating arithmetic in integer constant contexts; gcc const-object folding filed separately.

title: Resolve scopes, tags, and declarations

acceptance_criteria: Semantic diagnostics agree with clang for supported scope and declaration cases under each supplied -D configuration.
notes: Verified 2026-09-18 vs clang 22 (-std=c17): these are accepted by slate-parser but clang errors. (1) conflicting function redeclaration: 'int f(int); double f(int);' (2) tag redefinition: 'struct S{int a;}; struct S{int b;};'. Already covered: variable redeclaration, undeclared names/labels, duplicate labels, incomplete types.
close_reason: Conflicting function redeclarations and tag redefinitions now follow clang/gcc/MSVC consensus: reject where all reject, -Wconflicting-types where MSVC only warns; C23 identical tag redefinitions accepted. Follow-ups: slate-parser-9wx, slate-parser-y47, slate-parser-rsm.

title: Parse builtins, vectors, inline assembly, and remaining C23 syntax

close_reason: Parse-only builtin calls, vector types, structured GNU inline asm, and remaining C23 syntax are represented and covered by generated fixtures; deeper builtin semantics remain in dedicated epics

acceptance_criteria: Generic selections and statement expressions round-trip through generated FileCheck fixtures without requiring semantic resolution.
close_reason: Implemented parse-only _Generic and GNU statement-expression AST support with generated FileCheck coverage.

close_reason: Macro expansion now emits branch-aware conditional AST nodes for divergent macro uses in declarations, types, and statements, with generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Represent conditional macro definitions and redefinitions
description: Replace the current simple macro state with conditional macro definitions keyed by branch conditions, retaining relevant provenance and source order across redefinitions and includes.
acceptance_criteria: Object-like and function-like macro definitions diverging across branches expand as conditional token streams and have generated FileCheck coverage.
close_reason: Added conditional macro definition representation and FileCheck coverage.

title: Implement object-like macro expansion
description: Expand object-like macros recursively with replacement-list rules, disabled-macro recursion protection, and configuration-independent preservation of divergent expansions.
acceptance_criteria: Preprocessor output and parsed AST match clang for concrete configurations; polyvariant expansion is checked separately with generated FileCheck.
close_reason: Implemented recursive object-like macro expansion and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Implement function-like macro operators
description: Add function-like macro argument substitution, variadics and __VA_ARGS__, token stringification (#), token pasting (##), and rescanning rules.
acceptance_criteria: Macro operator fixtures are generated through the FileCheck updater and evaluated output matches clang for supported cases.
close_reason: Implemented function-like macro operators and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Complete nested conditional directive handling
description: Finish nested #if/#ifdef/#ifndef/#elif/#else/#endif handling, including condition evaluation and omission of inactive no-else branches, while preserving source-order branch structure.
acceptance_criteria: Nested directives produce correct Conditional nodes and malformed directive structure yields parser diagnostics in generated FileCheck fixtures.

title: Make typedef-name tracking branch-aware

acceptance_criteria: Cast-versus-call and declaration-versus-expression ambiguities resolve correctly under every selected branch and are covered by FileCheck.
close_reason: Added branch-local typedef environments with common-name merging and FileCheck coverage for typedef-driven cast versus call parsing.

title: Phase 4: GNU, Clang, and C23 extensions
description: Implement the parse-only extensions listed in README Phase 4. Preserve extension syntax in the polyvariant AST, use typed enums where the syntax has stable semantics, and retain unknown or unsupported attributes losslessly.
acceptance_criteria: Each supported extension has generated FileCheck coverage; parse-only behavior does not require complete semantic validation until Phase 6.
close_reason: Closed

title: Clang oracles for AST structure and IR semantics
description: Two validation tracks in this existing standalone epic. First, after the ixa structural parser refactor, compare syntactic AST structure against a pinned Clang projection (2lv.4). This track needs no IR interpreter or semantic lowering. Second, preserve the existing differential IR-interpreter workflow: freestanding C -> parse/sema/IR -> interpreted behavior versus Clang-compiled output. Existing IR tasks, observation-hook design, and generated corpus work remain in scope. The epic stays outside ixa; only its AST track follows ixa.35.
design: Interpreter reads only required IR semantics (concrete types, overflow/rounding policy, places, resolved control-flow destinations) and never metadata; a program that only runs correctly with metadata means required semantics were misplaced. UB-labelled operations trap. Inputs are freestanding: the only observation channel is a harness header declaring an output hook (e.g. __slate_observe_u64) implemented natively by the interpreter and with printf on the clang side. Generated programs must be free of UB and unspecified behavior (Csmith/YARPGen), since IR hoisting fixes one evaluation order clang need not match. Expected outputs are generated with clang and checked in, so cargo nextest never needs clang. See wiki/concepts/ir-spec.md.
acceptance_criteria: AST track: symmetric structural comparisons detect missing/extra nodes and wrong grammar choices for supported constructs, with reproducible minimized regression inputs. IR track: generated programs interpreted from IR match Clang observable behavior; mismatches and UB traps are minimized into checked-in fixtures. Normal cargo nextest runs without a Clang installation; pinned Clang is used to regenerate/check oracle expectations.

title: Phase 5: concrete AST evaluation
description: Track README Phase 5 evaluation of the polyvariant AST against concrete macro and target environments. Evaluation must produce a conditional-free concrete AST and diagnose invalid multi-selected branches.
acceptance_criteria: The evaluated AST is conditional-free, configuration-dependent, and covered by FileCheck fixtures and the evaluated clang oracle where the modeled AST supports comparison. This phase is already implemented and is retained as a completed milestone.
close_reason: Phase 5 concrete AST evaluation is already implemented and covered by FileCheck and evaluated oracle fixtures.

title: Phase 2: conditional object and function-like macros
description: Implement README Phase 2 macro expansion while preserving divergent macro definitions as conditional data. The macro table must support object-like and function-like macros, and expansion must expose conditional token streams to the branch-aware parser.
acceptance_criteria: Macro definitions and expansions preserve branch conditions, support the listed C macro operators, and are validated through generated FileCheck fixtures plus preprocessor comparison against clang.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 0: flat lexer and parser
description: Track the foundational non-conditional lexer and parser described in README Phase 0: tokens, the initial translation-unit AST, function definitions, compound statements, return statements, and integer constant expressions. This work is already implemented and is retained as a completed milestone for project history.
acceptance_criteria: The flat lexer and parser behavior is covered by the existing FileCheck fixtures; no conditional preprocessing or sema is required for this phase.
close_reason: Phase 0 flat lexer and parser is already implemented and covered by existing FileCheck fixtures.

title: Phase 1: conditional preprocessing and branch-aware parsing
description: Track README Phase 1: conditional directives, condition-stack representation, Conditional AST nodes, interleaved branch points in declaration and statement lists, and branch-aware typedef-name tracking for grammar disambiguation. The currently implemented subset is retained as the baseline for completing this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Conditional branches and typedef-sensitive parsing are represented in the polyvariant AST and covered by FileCheck fixtures; remaining phase gaps are explicit child tickets.
close_reason: Closed

title: Expose semantic analysis as a TranslationUnit method
description: Refactor the semantic pass public API from a free function to TranslationUnit::analyze, keeping implementation helpers private and updating CLI call sites.
acceptance_criteria: TranslationUnit::analyze accepts -D defines and returns semantic errors; no public free-function entry point remains; CLI behavior and FileCheck coverage are unchanged; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
close_reason: Semantic analysis is exposed as TranslationUnit::analyze and the CLI uses it.

title: Implement configuration-aware semantic pass and CLI diagnostics
description: Create the first semantic-analysis pass over the evaluated concrete AST, accepting -D defines and returning multiple structured diagnostics. Hook it into the parse command so semantic errors render through the existing miette diagnostic path after parsing succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: A public semantic API accepts TranslationUnit and -D defines and returns a list of errors; conditionals are evaluated for supplied defines; independent semantic errors aggregate; parse CLI prints semantic diagnostics similarly to parser diagnostics and exits nonzero; valid fixtures remain unchanged and invalid semantic fixtures are covered by generated FileCheck.
close_reason: Implemented configuration-aware semantic validation and CLI diagnostics with aggregated errors and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Phase 6: configuration-aware semantic validation pass
description: Add a semantic validation phase after preprocessing and AST evaluation. The pass accepts the polyvariant TranslationUnit plus a list of -D defines, evaluates the AST for that configuration, validates that the resulting concrete program is well formed, and returns a list of diagnostics instead of panicking or stopping at the first error. The phase should grow from declaration/type/name validation into broader C semantic checks while remaining separate from parsing and code generation.
design: Run eval once per requested macro configuration, then validate the monomorphic ConcreteTranslationUnit. Keep the polyvariant AST free of semantic conclusions. Represent diagnostics as structured errors with stable messages and provenance, and reserve target/type-system details for child tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A public semantic pass API accepts a TranslationUnit and -D define list and returns an ordered list of semantic errors; conditional branches are evaluated using the supplied defines before validation; multiple independent errors are reported in one run; diagnostics identify the relevant declaration or source provenance; parser behavior remains separate; generated FileCheck or equivalent integration coverage exercises valid and invalid configurations.
close_reason: All children done. The pass exists as sema over a single-configuration TU; the polyvariant/-D-list design in the description was superseded by the 2026-09-12 single-configuration architecture. New semantic gaps are filed under the active epics.

title: Parse record and type layout attributes
description: Extend typed attribute parsing for record and type layout attributes based on clang-ir fixtures, including aligned(integer), packed trailing placement, vector_size(integer), mode(name), and field-level packed/aligned forms where the grammar supports them.
acceptance_criteria: Known record/type layout attributes have typed enum variants and preserve source order/payloads on records, typedefs, and fields; generated FileCheck coverage uses clang-ir aligned, packed_aligned, vector, and mode examples; malformed payloads produce diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented typed record/type layout attributes with generated FileCheck coverage, including aligned, vector_size, mode, field attachment, and trailing packed placement.

title: Parse function and declaration attributes
description: Extend typed attribute parsing for GNU declaration attributes used by clang-ir, including visibility(string), section(string), weak, used, retain, noinline, always_inline, noreturn, constructor, destructor, nonnull(indices), annotate(string), target(string), alias(string), weakref(string), malloc, pure, and related declaration/function forms.
acceptance_criteria: Known function/declaration attributes have typed enum variants and attach to functions, declarations, typedefs, parameters, and fields where permitted; before/after placement and ordered lists are preserved; generated FileCheck coverage validates representative clang-ir fixtures and malformed syntax diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented typed function and declaration attributes, parameter attachment, placement handling, and generated FileCheck diagnostics.

title: Parse C23 and unknown attributes losslessly
description: Add C23 [[attribute]] spelling and an opaque/raw typed attribute fallback so unsupported attributes are retained rather than discarded. Cover deprecated(message), noreturn, nodiscard, maybe_unused, fallthrough, and namespace-qualified forms where practical.
acceptance_criteria: C23 attributes parse into typed variants when known and an opaque variant when unknown; placement and arguments are preserved; generated FileCheck coverage includes C23 fixtures and unknown attributes; malformed attribute syntax produces diagnostics.
close_reason: Implemented C23 [[...]] and namespace-qualified attribute parsing, typed standard forms, unknown lossless attributes, parser diagnostics, and generated FileCheck coverage.

title: Parse packed attributes on records
description: Implement and test GNU __attribute__((packed)) on struct and union declarations, preserving it as a typed Attribute enum in the polyvariant AST.
acceptance_criteria: Attribute::Packed is present on struct and union records; generated FileCheck coverage validates the parsed polyvariant form; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
close_reason: Packed attribute parsing and generated FileCheck coverage were implemented before the attribute work was split into subtickets.

title: Parse GNU and C23 attributes into typed AST enums
description: Add source-level attribute parsing based on the attribute forms exercised by ~/Projects/clang-ir. Represent attributes as a dedicated enum with typed payloads rather than raw strings, and attach ordered attribute lists to structs, unions, enums, functions, declarations, typedefs, and fields/parameters where C permits them. Preserve unknown attributes through an explicit opaque/raw variant so parsing does not discard source information. Initial coverage should include packed, aligned(integer), visibility(string), section(string), weak, used, retain, noinline, always_inline, noreturn, constructor, destructor, nonnull(parameter indices), annotate(string), target(string), and deprecated(message). Support GNU __attribute__((...)) placement before/after declarations and C23 [[...]] spelling where practical. Use clang-ir fixtures such as packed_aligned_struct.c, aligned_struct.c, visibility/main.c, used_retain/main.c, noreturn_prototype.c, nonnull_prototype.c, allocation_attribute_metadata.c, and c23_language.c as parser references.
design: Use a Vec<Attribute> on each declaration-like AST node rather than booleans scattered across node types. Keep semantic interpretation out of parsing. Model attributes with typed enum variants for known forms and preserve unsupported forms in Raw/Opaque(String) so extensions remain lossless.
acceptance_criteria: Attributes are represented by a public typed enum with explicit payloads and an opaque fallback; representative attributes parse on structs/unions/enums, functions, declarations, typedefs, fields, and parameters; source order and placement are preserved in the AST; generated FileCheck fixtures cover GNU and C23 forms and unknown attributes; malformed attribute syntax produces diagnostics; cargo fmt, cargo test, and cargo clippy pass.
notes:
Packed slice implemented: Attribute::Packed is parsed on struct/union prefixes and preserved in polyvariant rendering, with generated FileCheck coverage in tests/fixtures/packed.c. Remaining work includes trailing placement and other attribute variants.
Work split into child tickets 1tx.1 through 1tx.4. Child 1tx.1 (packed records) is complete; remaining attribute families are tracked separately.
close_reason: Typed GNU/C23 attributes, opaque/invalid preservation, placement handling, and generated attribute fixtures are implemented; release FileCheck passes.

title: Separate polyvariant filechecks from Clang AST oracle
description: Update filechecking so the polyvariant AST is validated only against preprocessing-aware FileCheck expectations, while the evaluated AST is the sole comparison against Clang post-sema output. Ensure the oracle comparison reflects only declarations visited by the evaluated AST and add regression coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Polyvariant output is not compared to clang; evaluated output is compared to clang under each define configuration; unvisited conditional declarations do not cause mismatches; tests pass.
close_reason: Separated evaluated AST oracle naming and documented the preprocessing/evaluation comparison boundary; verified reachability behavior.

title: Set miette parser diagnostics to C syntax highlighting
close_reason: Configured miette parser sources with C syntax highlighting.

title: Add parser diagnostics with thiserror and miette
close_reason: Added typed miette parser diagnostics, Result propagation through main, and an autogenerated failing-parser fixture checked through stderr FileCheck.

title: Extract compiler argument parsing into CompilerArgParser
close_reason: Added compiler_args module with CompilerArgParser for -D and -std options; main no longer parses compiler arguments inline.

title: Refactor renderer to write AST output
close_reason: Renderer now owns a generic Write target and renders AST plus evaluated AST directly; all checks pass.

title: Refactor top-level parsing into a parser struct
close_reason: Introduced Parser as the top-level parsing facade with source, file, declaration, and internal parsing methods; all checks pass.

title: Remove redundant translation-unit evaluation wrapper
close_reason: Removed the redundant eval_translation_unit wrapper; callers now invoke TranslationUnit::eval directly.

title: Move declaration and declarator helpers onto AST impls
close_reason: Moved declaration, declarator, condition, conditional, translation-unit, declaration, and statement evaluation helpers onto their owning types; all checks pass.

title: Filter AST to reachable declarations
description: Included headers currently inject every typedef/declaration into the rendered translation unit. Add a reachability pass so the public polyvariant/concrete AST contains primary-source roots plus transitive declarations needed by referenced names, types, tags, calls, and conditional branches. Preserve the full include environment internally for lookup, but omit unused header declarations such as ULONG_MAX_TYPE and MyConfigType from includes.c.
design: Use provenance to distinguish primary-file roots from included declarations. Index declarations by symbol/tag. Traverse identifiers and type references from roots, recursively marking dependencies. Treat conditional branches as a union for polyvariant reachability; concrete evaluation may then remove inactive branches. Keep macro definitions/preprocessor state separate from declaration reachability.
acceptance_criteria: Unused declarations from included headers are absent from FileCheck output; a source declaration that references a header typedef/tag/prototype retains that dependency; reachability is computed over all possible conditional branches before concrete evaluation and rechecked after branch selection.
notes: Added src/reachability.rs and applied it during parsing. Primary-file declarations are roots; included declarations are indexed by symbol and retained only when referenced through named/ tagged types, pointers, arrays, function return types, or parameters. Conditional branches are filtered after reachability is computed, so possible branch dependencies remain polyvariant and inactive concrete branches disappear. Updated includes.c to prove unused header typedefs are omitted and added includes_reachable.c to prove a referenced header typedef is retained. Clang comparison now requires every exposed summary to exist in clang while intentionally ignoring clang-only unused header declarations. Validation: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, generator freshness, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Reachability filtering implemented and fixture coverage proves unused includes are omitted while referenced typedef dependencies remain.

title: Expand clang oracle coverage for Phase 3 AST shapes
description: Extend the clang comparison tests beyond summarized returns/typedefs to compare normalized declarations, types, declarators, records, arrays, function pointers, and initializers. Pin normalization to the clang version documented by the project.
acceptance_criteria: Each implemented Phase 3 slice has a clang-backed regression test and normalization clearly documents intentionally ignored clang-only details.
notes: The oracle comparison intentionally does not require our AST to mirror clang. It normalizes both sides to semantic facts: declaration identity, base type, array extents, function-vs-function-pointer category, return-pointer status, parameter types, variadicness, typedef types, and evaluated returns. Clang qualType spelling is only an input to this normalization; our FileCheck output remains our own AST shape. This lets clang expose missing behavior without making its AST schema our design.
close_reason: Clang oracle normalizes and compares Phase 3 declarations, types, declarators, records, arrays, function signatures/pointers, initializers, and evaluated returns

title: Parse qualifiers and storage classes
description: Support const, volatile, restrict, _Atomic where applicable, typedef, extern, static, auto, register, and inline in the parse-only AST, including their valid declaration-specifier combinations.
acceptance_criteria: Qualifier/storage-class combinations are retained in AST tests and invalid combinations fail with useful parser diagnostics.
close_reason: Added qualifier and storage-class parsing, pointer/function qualifier retention, enum conversion helpers, rendered AST coverage, and invalid storage-class diagnostics.

title: Parse initializers and designated initializers
description: Add scalar, aggregate, string, compound, nested, and designated initializers, including array-index and struct-field designators. Keep initializer expressions polyvariant where conditionals occur.
acceptance_criteria: Representative initializer forms parse and preserve source order/designators; clang-backed tests cover nested aggregates and designated fields.
close_reason: Implemented initializer AST/parser/rendering/evaluation, conditional initializer support, generated fixture coverage, and documented FileCheck regeneration workflow.

title: Implement integer constant expressions for grammar decisions
description: Add integer constant folding sufficient for #if, array bounds, enumerator values, case labels, and static assertions as required by Phase 3 parsing. Keep this separate from full semantic analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Supported constant expressions fold consistently with clang for grammar-dependent cases, and unsupported expressions produce explicit diagnostics rather than silent values.
notes: Audit confirms case labels are implemented; old parser blocker is stale. Static assertion validation tracked in slate-parser-33i (in progress). Remaining acceptance gaps reported by read-only audit: preprocessor operator precedence and unsigned comparisons silently misfold, enum casts silently discard narrowing; cross-enum identifiers and enum array bounds explicitly unsupported. Keep this issue open pending independent reproduction and fixes.
close_reason: Fixed the silent constant-folding defects found by audit: C operator precedence in const_expr::Parser (shifts/relational/equality/bitwise/logical were collapsed), unsigned semantics for #if comparisons (WideInt is now suffix/width aware and pp conditions use it), and enum initializer/array-bound casts (typed constant_integer evaluation instead of the untyped evaluator, plus conditional/comma support). Verbatim AST preservation is unaffected; five stale parser fixtures regenerated through tools/update_filecheck.py. Probes match clang: #if 1|2^3, #if -1<1U, enum (unsigned char)257 -> 1. Static assertion validation (slate-parser-33i) remains open and now has correct folding primitives to build on.

title: Parse struct union and enum declarations
description: Add parse-only support for struct/union/enum definitions, forward declarations, fields, enumerators, anonymous records, and references. Track tags and typedef names sufficiently for grammar disambiguation.
acceptance_criteria: Representative record/union/enum declarations parse and match the corresponding clang AST structure; conditional declarations remain represented polyvariantly.
close_reason: Added parse-only struct, union, enum definitions, fields, forward declarations, anonymous records, tag references, typedef-tag aliases, rendering, reachability, and fixture/oracle coverage.

title: Parse arrays and function pointer declarators
description: Add postfix array declarators, multidimensional arrays, parameter lists, function declarators, pointer-to-function and function-returning-pointer composition, including parameter declarations.
acceptance_criteria: Nested array and function-pointer declarations parse with unambiguous AST structure and clang-oracle tests cover declaration permutations.
notes: Implemented declarator parsing in src/parser.rs and lexer support for char/void, pointers, brackets, commas, and ellipses. Added Declaration/ConcreteDecl integration, arrays, multidimensional arrays, function parameter lists, variadics, pointer-to-function, and function-returning-pointer coverage. Added clang type-spelling oracle tests. Validation: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass.
close_reason: Array and function-pointer declarators implemented with parser unit tests and clang oracle coverage; tests and clippy pass.

title: Phase 3: full C declarator/type grammar
description: Expand the parser from the Phase 2 conditional/macro surface to the Phase 3 parse-only C grammar described in README.md. Keep the AST polyvariant and defer ordinary type checking to Phase 6. Validate each slice against clang AST output.
design: Implement grammar in dependency order: shared type/declarator representation, records/enums, arrays/function pointers, qualifiers/storage, initializers/designators, then constant-expression folding. Use comment-embedded FileCheck AST expectations for readable fixture tests.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 3 grammar work is decomposed into independently testable parser slices; all slices preserve conditional AST branches and have clang-backed coverage.
close_reason: Closed

title: AST foundation: C types and declarators
description: Define the polyvariant AST representation for named/tagged types, pointers, arrays, function types, qualifiers, storage classes, and declarator composition. Preserve source/provenance and conditional branches without adding sema.
acceptance_criteria: The AST can represent every Phase 3 declarator/type shape needed by downstream parser slices, with structural unit tests.
notes: Added the Phase 3 AST foundation in src/ast.rs: richer CType variants for primitive/named/tagged/qualified/pointer/array/function types, declarator composition, parameters, qualifiers, storage classes, declaration specifiers, and deferred array-size expressions. Added structural unit tests. Updated the existing clang oracle normalization to remain exhaustive while dedicated Phase 3 oracle work is pending. Validation: cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings pass.
close_reason: AST type/declarator foundation and structural tests implemented; cargo test and clippy pass.

title: Drop lowering's always_inline/noinline conflict check
description: function.rs record_function rejects conflicting always_inline/noinline, duplicating Checker::inlining (listed as a known duplicate in sema-passes.md). Make lowering's copy Internal or read the checker's result, and remove the wiki note. Acceptance: one rejection site; suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lowering reads recorded declarator types for non-VM declarations
description: module.rs re-resolves every local declarator with resolve_declarator_type (plus inherit_convention) although the checker already resolved it. Only variably modified declarators need a re-resolution with bound extents. Record the checker's resolved type per declarator node and have lowering read it, re-resolving only when has_unbound_extent. Acceptance: resolve_declarator_type is called by lowering only for VM types; suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: __has_c_attribute argument macro expansion and __has_feature/__has_extension names
description:
`#define foo deprecated` + `__has_c_attribute (foo)` must give 202311L: the argument is macro-expanded. has-feature.c: __has_feature/__has_extension must know gcc's list (e.g. cxx_binary_literals as an extension in C) — take the table from gcc/c-family/c-common.cc has_feature_table.

Files: c23-has-c-attribute-2.c, has-feature.c (migrate: has-feature.c, -std=gnu23). Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: #elifdef / #elifndef are not directives before C23 in a skipped group
description:
Under -std=c11, `#if 0` / `#elifdef A` / `#error` / `#endif`: gcc treats #elifdef as an unknown directive inside the skipped group, so the #error is skipped. slate applies #elifdef in C11. Gate on the standard (gcc and clang both accept it as an extension only in C23/gnu modes; check clang).

Files: cpp/c11-elifdef-1.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: #line with an out-of-range line number
description:
`#line 18446744073709551616` fails with 'invalid #line directive, expected a digit sequence' (the digit sequence overflows). gcc warns 'line number out of range' and continues.

Files: cpp/line6.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: Stray backslash as a preprocessing token in macro arguments / stringification
description:
`#define str(x) #x` then `str (\);` fails (expected `;`): a lone \ is a valid "other" preprocessing token that can be passed and stringified (gcc only warns that `str(\)` and `str(\\\)` are invalid string literals).

Files: cpp/strify2.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: UTF-8 byte order mark at start of a source file
description:
A leading EF BB BF must be skipped. slate lexes it into the first declaration ('cannot combine `int` with previous declaration specifiers').

Files: cpp/pr33415.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: Digraph %: as the directive introducer
description:
`%:define glue` is not recognized as a directive, so `#ifndef glue` fires. %: and %:%: are the digraphs for # and ## everywhere, including starting a directive and as stringify/paste operators in macro bodies. Digraphs are on from C94 (iso9899:199409) and in all gnu modes.

Files: cpp/digraph1.c (migrate: cpp__digraph1.c, -std=iso9899:199409), cpp/digraphs.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.
notes: 2026-09-29: the lexer has no <: :> <% %> digraphs at all (`int a <: 1 :>;` fails under -std=c99), not just %: as a directive introducer. cpp/paste2.c (migrate: cpp__paste2.c, -std=c99) now fails only at `glue (<, :)` and belongs here.

title: Trigraphs in ISO modes (-std=c89/c99/c11/c17)
description:
`x ??'= 3;` fails (expected declarator): gcc replaces trigraphs in strict ISO modes before C23 and ignores them (-Wtrigraphs) in gnu modes and C23. ??/ followed by newline is a line splice, including at the end of a // comment. Gate on Dialect/standard.

Files: cpp/trigraphs.c (migrate: cpp__trigraphs.c, -std=c89), cpp/c11-trigraphs-1.c, cpp/Wtrigraphs-2.c (also needs the backslash-whitespace-newline splice bead). Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: Line splice with whitespace between backslash and newline
description:
gcc (and clang) treat a \ followed by spaces/tabs and then a newline as a line splice (warning "backslash and newline separated by space"). slate treats the backslash as a stray token (expected `;`).

Files: cpp/backslash.c, cpp/Wtrigraphs-2.c (also needs trigraphs, slate-parser-cxg.7.13). Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: __has_embed embed parameters (limit(...), prefix, suffix, if_empty, gnu::)
description:
`__has_embed (__FILE__ limit (1))` fails with 'expected `)`, found `limit`': __has_embed accepts the same embed-parameter-sequence as #embed.

Files: cpp/embed-2.c (migrate: cpp__embed-2.c, -std=c17; note embed + __FILE__ output-stability rule in migration_blocker), cpp/embed-3.c, cpp/embed-17.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: #include: macro-expanded header names and trailing tokens that expand to nothing
description:
`#define h h>` + `#include <stddef.h` and `#define foo stddef.h>` + `#include <foo` must be formed from macro-expanded tokens; `#include <stddef.h> EMPTY_OBJ` / `EMPTY_FUNC()` (both expanding to nothing) fail with 'expected "FILENAME" or <FILENAME>'.

Files: cpp/include4.c (migrate: cpp__include4.c, -std=c89), cpp/include5.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.
close_reason: Fixed by ryfo.4: header names form from expanded tokens when not spelled before expansion; trailing tokens ignored; migrated cpp/include4.c and include5.c

title: #import directive (include once)
description:
`#import "file.h"` is 'unsupported preprocessor directive'. gcc: like #include but the file is included at most once, including when it was already #included; deprecated warning. The tests need their companion headers, so they are not migratable as-is.

Files: cpp/import1.c, cpp/import2.c.

title: #assert / #unassert and #if #pred(answer), with GCC's predefined assertions
description:
The directives fail with "unsupported preprocessor directive"; `#if #foo(bar)` fails with "unexpected token Hash". GCC predefines assertions on x86_64-linux such as #system(linux) #system(unix) #system(posix) #cpu(x86_64) #machine(x86_64); they are not visible in gcc -dM -E, so take the list cpp/assert4.c tests plus gcc/config sources. Deprecated GCC extension: warn, do not reject.

Files: cpp/assert1.c (migrate: cpp__assert1.c, -std=gnu23 -Wno-deprecated), cpp/assert4.c (migrate: cpp__assert4.c, -std=c89 -Wno-deprecated), cpp/trad/assert1.c, cpp/pr22168.c, cpp/pr22168-2.c, cpp/extratokens.c, cpp/tr-warn1.c, cpp/tr-warn3.c, cpp/warn-deprecated.c, cpp/warn-deprecated-2.c, cpp/warn-traditional.c, cpp/warn-traditional-2.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: Dynamic builtin macros: defined(__TIME__), __TIMESTAMP__, redefining and -D/-U of __DATE__/__TIME__
description:
__DATE__/__TIME__ expand (src/pp/expand.rs) but `#ifndef __TIME__` / `defined(__TIME__)` is false; __TIMESTAMP__ is missing (unresolved ordinary name); -U__DATE__ -D__TIME__=X and #define __TIME__ "X" do not replace the builtin (gcc: -Wbuiltin-macro-redefined warning). Output with these macros is unstable, so the files are not migratable; verify by hand.

Files: cpp/trad/builtins.c, cpp/warn-redefined.c, cpp/warn-redefined-2.c, builtin-redefine.c, pr61861.c.

title: #if arithmetic: negative shift counts and ?: usual arithmetic conversions
description:
`#if 17 << -2 != 17 >> 2` and `5 >> -2 != 20`: cpp defines a negative shift as a shift the other way. `#if (1 ? -2: 0 + 1U) < 0` must be false: the ?: result takes the common type of both arms (unsigned), even when the unchosen arm is unsigned.

Files: cpp/arith-1.c, cpp/if-shift.c, cpp/expr.c (arith-1 is long; re-run after the fix for further gaps). Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: #if: function-like macro name produced by an expansion is not invoked with the following ( ... )
description:
`#define glue(a,b) a##b` / `#define xglue(a,b) glue(a,b)`: `#if glue (xgl, ue) (1, 2) != 12` fails ('call to `glue` is not a constant expression'). The expansion yields `xglue`, which must be rescanned together with the rest of the line and invoked on (1, 2). Check whether the same gap exists outside #if.

Files: cpp/macro4.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.
close_reason: Fixed by ryfo.3: #if operands expand through the stream expander, so a function-like name produced by an expansion takes the following (...); migrated cpp/macro4.c

title: #if: defined produced by macro expansion
description:
With `#define Z`: `#define bad0 defined Z` + `#if !bad0` fails (Z is expanded away before `defined` sees it); `#define bad1 defined` + `#if !bad1 Z` / `#if !bad1 (Z)`, and `#define bad2 defined (Z` + `#if !bad2)` also fail. gcc (and clang) treat a `defined` that comes out of an expansion as the operator, with its operand taken unexpanded, possibly from tokens after the expansion; -Wexpansion-to-defined is only a warning.

Files: cpp/defined-Wextra.c (migrate: cpp__defined-Wextra.c, -std=gnu23), cpp/defined-Wexpansion-to-defined.c, cpp/defined-Wextra-Wno-expansion-to-defined.c, cpp/defined-Wno-expansion-to-defined.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.
close_reason: Fixed by ryfo.4: #if expands through the stream and defined takes its operand unexpanded, including after an expansion; migrated the four cpp/defined-* files

title: #if: comma operator
description:
`#if 1 ? 2 : 3 , 0` and `#if 2 , 3` (after `, ## __VA_ARGS__` keeps the comma) fail with 'unexpected tokens after expression'. gcc accepts the comma operator in #if (pedantic warning only in C90 / outside unevaluated operands).

Files: cpp/vararg3.c (migrate: cpp__vararg3.c, -std=c99), cpp/vararg4.c, cpp/if-oppr2.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: GNU named variadic macro parameters (name...)
description:
`#define gnu_count(y...) _gnu_count1 ( , ##y)` is not recognized: the macro ends up undefined (unresolved ordinary name `gnu_count`) or later expansions produce stray commas. Needs `name...` parameters, the name standing for __VA_ARGS__, and GNU , ## name comma elision. Verify with gcc -E: gnu_count(), (A), (,), (A..J) give 0, 1, 2, 10.

Files: cpp/vararg2.c (the file also exercises c99_* variants; re-check after the fix). Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.

title: Tokens from argument pre-expansion lose their painted-blue status and are re-expanded
description:
enum { a = 4, f = 3 }; #define a1(y) (y+2) / #define f a+f: `a1(f)` must be (a+f+2) with the inner f not replaceable (gcc: 9). slate re-expands the inner f on rescan after substitution, so the value is wrong and the static assertion in the test fails silently-wrong rather than rejected. C11 6.10.3.4p2: a nested self-reference is never again available for replacement, even when later (re)examined.

Files: cpp/19921210-1.c. Migrate on fix per the recipe in slate-parser-cxg.7.
close_reason: Fixed by ryfo.3 hide sets; migrated cpp/19921210-1.c to gcc-dg gcc and clang fixtures

title: gcc flavor: C23 auto deduced from a bit-field initializer (gcc.dg/c23-auto-1.c)
description: c23-auto-1.c (-std=c23) fails 'not implemented: deduced type of a bit-field initializer' at `auto bfa = bv.a;` (struct b { int a : 2; unsigned b : 3; }). The test requires _Generic (bv.a, typeof (bfa) : 1, default : 2) == 1, i.e. gcc deduces the bit-field's own special type, matching _Generic's handling. Split out of slate-parser-cxg.4, whose attribute part of this file now passes. Migrate on fix: c23-auto-1.c -> tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/c23-auto-1.c (-std=c23).

title: aligned attribute in a type name is dropped (gcc applies it to the type)
description: gcc treats __attribute__((aligned(16))) in a type name as a type attribute: _Alignof(__attribute__((aligned(16))) char) is 16 and (__attribute__((aligned(16))) char){3} is 16-aligned. clang ignores it with -Wignored-attributes (_Alignof is 1). slate drops it in both flavors. Per flavor: gcc should apply it, clang should warn and ignore. Found while fixing cxg.53.
close_reason: gcc applies type-name aligned as an anonymous aligned typedef; clang/msvc warn -Wignored-attributes and ignore

title: _Alignas in a compound literal type name (DR 444) rejected; gcc accepts, clang rejects
description: char *p = &(_Alignas (_Alignof (max_align_t)) char) { 1 }; gcc -std=c11 accepts (DR#444); clang rejects 'expected expression'; slate rejects at parse ('expected ), found char'). gcc flavor is too strict. File: gcc.dg/c11-align-7.c (-std=c11). Migrate on fix into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/.
close_reason: fixed; c11-align-7.c and Wmismatched-dealloc.c migrated to suites/gcc-dg

title: always_inline + noinline conflict: gcc warns and ignores, slate rejects
description:
Slate errors 'conflicting always_inline and noinline attributes'. gcc -Wattributes warns and ignores the conflicting one (pr18079.c same declaration; Wattributes-6.c: always_inline on declaration, noinline on definition). Check clang and which attribute gcc keeps (affects FunctionSemantics). Dedupe the check (Checker::inlining and record_function both do it; noted in attributes.md and sema-passes.md).

Files: pr18079.c, Wattributes-6.c (-std=gnu23).

Migrate on fix: copy into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/<name>.c, append // SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc, // SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES DEFAULT <defines>, // SLATE-FILECHECK-STD DEFAULT <std>, then python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place <fixture>. Reproduce: target/release/slate-parser parse <file> --flavor=gcc -std=<std> --dump-ir (file first). Split from slate-parser-cxg.2.

title: Remaining FileCheck slowdown from named IR variables: 263k regex lines
description: After -SAME splitting of long lines, the suite is 11.8s wall (summed test time 130s) versus ~6s before becf64da. Each check line with a [[VAR]] is a per-line regex compile in FileCheck. 20001226-1.c (16k lines, ~1.5s FileCheck) is the largest single case. Measure the pre-becf64da suite on the same machine to confirm the baseline, then decide whether cheaper per-line forms are worth it (e.g. a -SAME split of just the variable token on long files).
close_reason: Replaced FileCheck with an in-harness matcher; suite is faster than before named variables

title: Redundant diagnostics: one error reported twice or with an extra generic companion
description: Found regenerating fixtures on 2026-09-29: error fixtures were stale because extra diagnostics had appeared (plain PREFIX: lines don't require adjacency, so they still passed). Examples: c23_auto_inference.c reports "'auto' type inference is not allowed here" twice at the same span; malformed-attributes.c reports "invalid attribute" plus "invalid arguments for attribute visibility"; semantic_errors.c reports "void array element" plus "object cannot have type void" for void invalid_array[2]; gcc-torture 20010605-1.c adds "nonconstant or unknown identifier" over the whole typedef before the real error. Decide per case whether both come from checker and lowering paths and dedupe to the one clang reports.

title: Incomplete objects accepted: block-scope 'struct S s;' and file-scope tentative definitions never completed
description: Found during dvlq. With 'struct S;' never completed, clang rejects 'struct S s;' at file scope ('tentative definition has type struct S that is never completed', also for static) and 'void h(void) { struct S s; }' ('variable has incomplete type'). slate parse and ir --dump-ir accept both. Permissive, not too strict. Fix belongs in the checker (TypeResolver::is_incomplete_record exists): block-scope object definitions immediately, tentative definitions at the end of the unit.

title: gcc flavor: variably modified struct/union members (struct { char a[n]; }) rejected with 'nonconstant or unknown identifier'
description:
GNU C accepts a block-scope struct or union whose member is a VLA (gcc extension; clang rejects: 'fields must have a constant size'). slate --flavor=gcc rejects it in tag definition ('nonconstant or unknown identifier', types.rs array extent) in both the checker and lowering. Too strict for gcc only; clang-flavor rejection is correct.

Repro (gcc -fsyntax-only accepts):
  void f(int z) { struct { char a[z]; } x; }

Reproduces: gcc.dg/vla-2.c (-std=gnu99), gcc-torture 20030224-1.c (fixture now expects this error instead of the later 'unresolved foo'). Needs a record layout with runtime member offsets/size. Migrate vla-2.c to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/ and regenerate 20030224-1.c when fixed.

title: gcc flavor: accept a null pointer constant as a computed goto operand (goto *0)
description: gcc accepts 'goto *0;' (null pointer constant converts to void*); slate rejects 'nonpointer computed goto' in the checker. clang rejects it for other reasons. Low value.

title: Too strict: sizeof(call) in static assertion, negative offsetof index, return of a void expression from a void function
description:
Found while classifying ResolveError sites (yluq). clang 22 and gcc 16 accept all three; slate-parser rejects:
- _Static_assert(sizeof(f()) == 4, "") with extern int f(void): 'not implemented: nonconstant call expression' (TypeResolver::assertion_operand_type has no call case beyond builtins).
- __builtin_offsetof(struct s, a[-1]): 'not implemented: invalid offsetof index' (offsetof_member requires a non-negative u64 index; clang folds to a wrapped size_t).
- void g(void); void f(void) { return g(); }: 'value return from void function' (Rejected; C11 6.8.6.4 constraint, but both compilers accept, clang with only a pedantic warning).

title: (BUG) Wrong constant evaluation (remainder of cxg.37): __builtin_has_attribute + copy, _BitInt layout, tag composites, va_arg sizeof
description:
Split from slate-parser-cxg.37 on 2026-09-28 after clusters E (alignment) and G (C23 enums) were fixed. Each cluster is an independent root cause; reproduce with the sweep's options (tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py `one()`; note the module runs main() on import).

## Clusters

- C. __builtin_has_attribute (gcc only; clang rejects it): attr-copy-6.c, attr-copy-7.c, attr-copy-8.c. Not a constant-folding bug: it parses as a plain Call with the attribute as an Identifier. Needs an ExprKind variant (operand is a type or expression; attribute may take arguments like aligned(8)) plus a sema query of the attributes a function, variable, field or type ended up with, including ones inherited through `copy(expr)`, which is currently Attribute::Unknown with string args (so `copy` semantics are needed too: noreturn and returns_nonnull copy, leaf does not copy to a weakref, packed copies to fields).
- H. _BitInt struct layout: bitint-17.c (sizeof(struct S4) == 48 fails).
- I. alignof/sizeof through ?: composite of compatible tag types: c23-tag-composite-2.c ('nonconstant call' on sizeof(*((1 ? &x : &y)->i()))), c23-tag-composite-6.c (alignof(a.y) after extern typeof(*(1 ? &a : &b)) a: 'unknown or unsupported').
- J. sizeof(va_arg(ap, char[5])) is 'nonliteral': pr97986-1.c.

## Migrate on fix

Copy into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/ (and clang/ when clang also accepts), append // SLATE-FILECHECK-STD DEFAULT <std> and // SLATE-FILECHECK-DEFINES DEFAULT, then python3 tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place.

- attr-copy-6.c, attr-copy-7.c (gnu23), bitint-17.c (c23)

## Other reproducing files

attr-copy-8.c c23-tag-composite-2.c c23-tag-composite-6.c pr97986-1.c

title: slate-sysroots: no glibc sysroot for i686-unknown-linux-gnu or armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabi(hf)
description: slate-sysroots' Target enum only has x86_64/aarch64 Linux glibc. With per-family GCC headers installed (cxg.38), the gcc flavor on i686 and armv7 now fails at the libc boundary instead: arm/include/stdint.h's #include_next <stdint.h> and x86 mm_malloc.h's #include <stdlib.h> find no libc headers. Needs Debian i386 (multiarch i386-linux-gnu) and armel/armhf sysroots.
close_reason: slate-sysroots installs i686-unknown-linux-gnu (Debian i386 cross, glibc 2.43, usr/i686-linux-gnu), armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabi (armel, glibc 2.36 — armel dropped from sid) and armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf (armhf, glibc 2.43). slate-parser profiles now probe usr/i686-linux-gnu, usr/arm-linux-gnueabi(hf). stdio/pthread/signal/unwind/linux/version.h program parses on all three in gcc and clang flavors; float ABI selects stubs-soft/stubs-hard correctly.

title: GCC target builtins: __builtin_ia32_* functions and __builtin_aarch64_simd_* types used by GCC intrinsics headers
description: With cxg.38 the gcc flavor now finds GCC 16.2's x86/aarch64/arm intrinsics headers, but they depend on target builtins slate-parser doesn't model. x86: smmintrin.h/emmintrin.h call __builtin_ia32_pblendvb128, __builtin_ia32_pcmpistris128, ... -> 'unresolved ordinary name'. aarch64: arm_neon.h:5557 casts to (__builtin_aarch64_simd_hf *) and calls __builtin_aarch64_st2_lanev4hf -> parse error 'unexpected token RParen'. Repros (gcc.dg, -std=gnu23): torture/pr40470-1..4.c (nmmintrin.h); a one-line '#include <arm_neon.h>' with --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --flavor=gcc. The __m128 half of these failures is slate-parser-v74.1.13 (hardcoded is_target_builtin_name overrides the headers' typedefs); torture/stackalign/push-1.c, alloca-2.c, alloca-3.c, vararg-3.c fail only on that.

title: Empty initializer for an array of unknown size: GNU zero-length array unsupported in IR lowering
close_reason: static int a[] = {} is now a zero-length array<T, 0> in both flavors (sizeof 0), matching gcc and clang; covered by gcc-torture pr79286.c and clang/linux/x86_64/initializer_brace_rules.c. range-test-1.c needs other files, so the sweep tool skips migrating it.

title: IR lowering rejects excess initializer elements for a zero-length array member
close_reason: Fixed by cxg.21: excess braced elements are dropped like gcc/clang; 20000926-1.c migrated.

title: 0o octal prefix rejected in #if: lexed as a floating literal
description:
Repro, any -std, both flavors:

  #if 0o17 != 15
  #error
  #endif

slate: 'invalid #if expression: floating literal is not a constant expression'. gcc accepts 0o in every mode (C2Y feature, -Wpedantic warning only); clang 22 accepts too. Check the non-#if path as well ('int x = 0o17;'). Repro: gcc.dg/octal-constants-1.c (-std=gnu99). Found by re-sweeping slate-parser-cxg.13's files after GCC headers landed (limits.h used to mask it). Reproduces under --flavor=gcc and --flavor=clang; gcc and clang both accept. Migrate on fix: copy into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/ via python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate gcc, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place.

title: Leading vector_size attribute on a function definition's return type gives the wrong vector type
Model nullptr_t as a distinct type instead of void *
description: nullptr lowers as ValueKind::Null of type void * (sema/expression.rs) and the static-assertion type path matches that (sema/types.rs assertion_operand_type). C23 makes nullptr_t a distinct scalar type: gcc accepts _Generic(nullptr, void*: 1, typeof(nullptr): 2), which slate would call an ambiguous selection, and conversions/comparisons of nullptr_t objects differ from void *. Needs a CTypeKind variant; see wiki/concepts/type-family-touchpoints.md. Found while fixing cxg.6 (c23-nullptr-1/2.c pass with the void * approximation).
close_reason: Implemented in the cxg.6 nullptr commit: CTypeKind::NullPtr lowering to ptr<void>, C23 conversions, equality, classify_type -1.

title: Model x86-64 __vectorcall argument/result shapes where clang and rustc diverge
description:
slate records __vectorcall on x86_64 (1yuw) but prints the platform cdecl shapes (sysv64/win64). Verified 2026-09-28 with clang -emit-llvm and rustc --emit=llvm-ir (extern "vectorcall", #![feature(abi_vectorcall)]):
- clang x86_64-linux vectorcall uses SysV classification: struct{int a,b,c} -> (i64, i32); struct{double x4} -> byval; struct{double a,b} result -> {double,double}.
- clang x86_64-windows vectorcall passes HVAs inreg (struct{double x4} -> %struct inreg, struct{double a,b} returned as %struct), otherwise win64 (12-byte struct byref, i128 byref, returns <2 x i64>).
- rustc extern "vectorcall" on BOTH x86_64 OSes uses win64 rules without HVA registers: d2 returns sret, d4 byref, r3 byref, i128 byref returning <16 x i8>.
So under the native_c = trust-rustc rule nearly every record diverges; needs explicit shapes (and the i686 vectorcall HVA case probably too). Also: clang rejects vectorcall on a variadic function ('variadic function cannot use vectorcall calling convention'); slate silently drops the convention (permissive).

title: thumbv7a-pc-windows-msvc: homogeneous vector aggregates diverge from rustc but print native_c
description: rustc never uses VFP passing on thumbv7a-pc-windows-msvc (no hf suffix), and clang passes homogeneous vector aggregates (e.g. struct { float32x4_t v; }) in q registers (arm_aapcs_vfpcc [1 x <4 x float>]). The divergence check in sema/abi.rs only models float HFAs, so HVAs print native_c there. Needs an HVA-aware homogeneous walk (also missing for the explicit AAPCS shapes generally).

title: Model __vectorcall on x86-64 targets
description: clang honours __vectorcall on x86_64 (both -windows-msvc and -linux-gnu: 'define x86_vectorcallcc i32 @vc(...)', decorated vc@@N on windows), unlike stdcall/fastcall/thiscall which it ignores there. slate-parser-v910 models calling conventions only on 32-bit x86, so on x86_64 vectorcall is dropped from the function type and _Generic/compatibility differ from clang. Extend TypeResolver::calling_convention to keep X86Vectorcall when target.family is X86_64.
close_reason: x86_64 keeps __vectorcall in function types (linux and windows); ABI shapes filed as x74n

title: typeof(&f) in a static assertion fails after f's definition
description: After a function definition, __builtin_types_compatible_p(__typeof__(&f), int (*)(int)) inside _Static_assert fails with 'static assertion requires an integer constant expression: unknown or unsupported sizeof operand type'. The same assertion after a plain declaration of f passes. Clang accepts both. Repro: 'int f(int a) { return a; } _Static_assert(__builtin_types_compatible_p(__typeof__(&f), int (*)(int)), "");' on any target. Found while writing calling-convention fixtures (slate-parser-v910); reproduces on the tree before that change.
close_reason: Closed

title: clang flavor: small gaps from the gcc.dg clang pass (asm __imag__ lvalue, overloadable tgmath, noipa, _Fract without -ffixed-point, excess initializers)
description:
Code clang accepts that slate --flavor=clang rejects, each with a small cause of its own. The gcc column says what slate --flavor=gcc does on the same file.

- pr115426.c (-std=gnu11), torture/pr70370.c: 'invalid lvalue in asm output' for __asm__("" : "=rm" (__imag__ r)). --flavor=gcc passes, so the clang flavor's asm lvalue check is stricter.
- c99-tgmath-2.c, c99-tgmath-3.c, c99-tgmath-4.c (-std=iso9899:1999): clang's tgmath.h declares __tg_promote overloads with __attribute__((__overloadable__)); slate reports 'conflicting types for function redeclaration'. Needs C overloadable functions in the clang flavor. (--flavor=gcc fails on __builtin_tgmath, cxg.12.)
- guality/example.c, guality/guality.c, guality/inline-params.c, guality/inline-params-2.c, guality/pr41447-1.c, guality/pr41616-1.c (-fgnu89-inline), guality/pr42782.c: 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: nonliteral numeric expression', span on __attribute__((noipa)) in guality.h. clang ignores noipa with a warning. (--flavor=gcc fails on malloc(deallocator), cxg.2.)
- fixed-point/keywords-ignored-c99.c (-std=c99): 'cannot combine _Fract with previous declaration specifiers'. clang only makes _Fract/_Accum/_Sat keywords with -ffixed-point; without it they are ordinary identifiers. --flavor=gcc passes.
- 20000926-1.c, noncompile/init-1.c, noncompile/940227-1.c: 'excess elements in initializer'. clang warns (-Wexcess-initializers) and drops the extras; slate errors.
- range-test-1.c: 'empty initializer for array of unknown size'.
- tree-ssa/20030807-8.c (-std=gnu89), tree-ssa/builtin-sprintf-warn-3.c ('non-function callee'), vect/vect-pr124802.c.

Migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/clang/linux/x86_64/ when fixed (python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate clang, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place). Found by the clang pass of the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg.29).

title: clang flavor: triage gcc.dg tests gcc rejects but clang accepts
description:
gcc.dg tests that gcc -fsyntax-only rejects (dg-error / pedantic-error tests) but clang 22 accepts, and slate --flavor=clang rejects with the same error as --flavor=gcc. Rejecting them is right for the gcc flavor. For the clang flavor it is too strict, but these inputs are deliberately invalid and clang accepts them only with a warning, so triage each one against clang before fixing: some may be clang warnings slate treats as errors, and some may be slate bugs of their own.

bitfld-19.c, bitfld-20.c, bitfld-21.c (nonconstant or unknown identifier); c23-align-10.c (incomplete field type); attr-aligned.c (-Wno-pedantic, static assertion on incomplete field); c23-attr-reproducible-3.c, c23-attr-unsequenced-3.c (unexpected [); c23-enum-4.c (enum value outside i64 range); c23-tag-enum-5.c (duplicate ordinary name); cpp/macro8.c, cpp/vararg1.c (-std=c89, #if expressions); fixed-point/keywords-reserved.c (-std=gnu99); gnu89-const-expr-1.c, gnu90-const-expr-1.c, gnu99-const-expr-1.c (nonliteral numeric expression); gomp/attrs-13.c, gomp/attrs-14.c (-std=c23); large-size-array-6.c (array size overflow); redecl-5.c (-std=c89), redecl-16.c; vla-init-4.c; Wincompatible-pointer-types-5.c (conditional operands); gnu23-auto-1.c; analyzer/builtins-pr107565.c (__builtin_ia32_rdrand16_step); darwin-cfstring-2.c, torture/darwin-cfstring-3.c (__builtin___CFStringMakeConstantString).

Migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/clang/linux/x86_64/ when fixed (python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate clang, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place). Found by the clang pass of the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg.29).

title: mode(__unwind_word__) unsupported in IR lowering (unwind.h)
description:
clang's unwind.h declares 'typedef uintptr_t _Unwind_Word __attribute__((__mode__(__unwind_word__)))'; slate --flavor=clang fails with 'unsupported in numeric IR lowering: machine mode'. GCC's own unwind.h uses the same mode, so --flavor=gcc will hit it once cxg.13 supplies unwind.h. clang and gcc both map __unwind_word__ to word_mode (DI on x86_64).

Repros (gcc.dg, all include <unwind.h>): cleanup-5.c, cleanup-8.c, cleanup-9.c, cleanup-10.c, cleanup-11.c, cleanup-12.c, cleanup-13.c.

Migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/clang/linux/x86_64/ when fixed (python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate clang, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place). Found by the clang pass of the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg.29).
close_reason: Closed
