title: clang flavor: IR lowering reports incompatible pointer types on code clang accepts (integer-constant types, null pointer constants, strftime)
description:
clang 22 accepts all of these even with -Werror=incompatible-pointer-types; slate parse --flavor=clang --dump-ir fails in IR lowering with 'incompatible pointer types'. Plain parse (no --dump-ir) succeeds.

- c99-intconst-1.c (-std=iso9899:1999) at CHECK_DEC_CONST(1), c90-intconst-1.c (-std=iso9899:1990), binary-constants-1.c (-std=gnu99) at CHECK_BIN_CONST(1), c23-binary-constants-1.c (-std=c23): these check an integer constant's type through pointer assignments, so slate gives a constant or its u/l-suffixed form the wrong type. Under --flavor=gcc they stop earlier at <limits.h> (cxg.13), so gcc may share the bug.
- c90-const-expr-2.c (-std=iso9899:1990) at ASSERT_NOT_NPC((void *)(void *)0): null-pointer-constant classification. --flavor=gcc passes.
- format/c90-strftime-1.c, format/c90-strftime-2.c, format/ms_c90-strftime-1.c, format/ms_c90-strftime-2.c (-std=iso9899:1990): 'const struct tm *' passed to strftime's 'const struct tm *restrict' parameter. --flavor=gcc passes, so this is clang-flavor specific.

Migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/clang/linux/x86_64/ when fixed (python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate clang, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place). Found by the clang pass of the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg.29).
notes:
cc94.5.6 re-check: all seven samples still fail with 'incompatible pointer types', now from the checker's conversion classification rather than lowering. Separate bugs, not caused by check placement: clang-flavor integer-constant typing (intconst/binary-constants), (void *)(void *)0 null-pointer-constant classification (c90-const-expr-2), restrict pointee compatibility for strftime.
Correction to the previous note: plain parse still accepts these. 'incompatible pointer types' is the default-error incompatible-pointer-types warning that lowering emits from the checker's recorded conversion, not a ResolveError, so it is outside the no-Rejected audit (same class as cc94.5.7). The underlying bugs are still the three listed.
cc94.5.7: plain parse now rejects these too (default-error conversion warnings are emitted by the checker), so parse and --dump-ir agree; the underlying typing bugs remain.

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Confirmed that --flavor=gcc shares the integer-constant part: with <limits.h> available (cxg.13), binary-constants-1.c (-std=gnu99), c23-binary-constants-1.c (-std=c23) and c99-intconst-1.c (-std=iso9899:1999) fail with 'incompatible pointer types' under gcc too. When fixed, also migrate them with --migrate gcc.

title: clang flavor: __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__ undefined (clang builtin macro missing from -dM snapshots)
description:
clang defines __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__ as a builtin macro: it expands to 0 on x86_64, but clang -dM -E does not list it. So the clang predefines snapshots lack it, and slate --flavor=clang reports 'unresolved ordinary name __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__'. --flavor=gcc passes.

Repros (gcc.dg): fpermitted-flt-eval-methods_1.c (-std=c11), _2.c (-std=gnu23), _3.c (-std=c11), _4.c (-std=c11). Check how clang varies it (#pragma clang fp eval_method, -ffp-eval-method, i386 without SSE) before deciding where to define it.

Migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/clang/linux/x86_64/ when fixed (python3 tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py OUT --migrate clang, then tools/update_filecheck.py --in-place). Found by the clang pass of the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg.29).

title: MS __asm blocks: AVX-512 opmask operand syntax {k1} / {z} rejected
description:
__asm { vaddpd zmm8 {k1}, zmm27, zmm6 }

clang-cl accepts (x86_64); slate --flavor=clang: "expected instruction mnemonic in `__asm`" at `{`. The MS-asm tokenizer treats `{` as a block delimiter; inside an instruction it is an opmask/zeroing decorator. cl.exe x64 has no inline asm.

Migrate on fix:
- CodeGen/ms-inline-asm-avx512.c (x86_64)

title: Preprocessor: __is_target_arch/os/vendor/environment/variant_* unsupported
description:
clang supports the __is_target_* function-like builtins in #if (__is_target_arch, __is_target_vendor, __is_target_os, __is_target_environment, __is_target_variant_os, __is_target_variant_environment), and __has_builtin reports them. slate: "invalid #if expression: call to `__is_target_arch` is not a constant expression". Matching rules (from the triple, with arch sub-variants and the "unknown" vendor/OS cases) are in clang's PPMacroExpansion.cpp.

Migrate on fix:
- Preprocessor/is_target_environment_version.c (x86_64)

title: __builtin_ms_va_list / __builtin_ms_va_start / __builtin_ms_va_end unsupported
description:
clang accepts __builtin_ms_va_list (a type keyword) and __builtin_ms_va_start/_end/_copy on x86_64 and aarch64 (any OS; used for ms_abi functions on non-Windows targets). On *-windows-msvc it is the same as __builtin_va_list (char*). slate: "unexpected tokens after expression" at `__builtin_ms_va_list ap;`. cl.exe does not know these.

Migrate on fix:
- CodeGen/ms_abi.c (x86_64), CodeGen/ms_abi_aarch64.c (aarch64)

title: clang flavor defaults to gnu23; clang 22 defaults to gnu17
description:
clang 22.1.8 with no -std gives __STDC_VERSION__ 201710L on every target (checked x86_64-pc-windows-msvc); slate --flavor=clang gives 202311L because LanguageStandard::default() is Gnu23 for every flavor (decision in wiki/log/2026-09-17-22-17.md, which chose gnu over strict but did not consider per-flavor defaults). gcc 15 does default to gnu23, so the gcc flavor is right. cl.exe with no /std: is its legacy C mode (no __STDC_VERSION__), so the msvc flavor default deserves the same look.

Under gnu23, K&R definitions are errors and `T f()` means `(void)`, so these clang-accepted tests fail only on the default (they pass with explicit -std=gnu17):
- CodeGen/microsoft-call-conv-x64.c: `void __stdcall f7(foo) int foo; {}`
- CodeGen/variadic-null-win64.c: `void kr(); kr(f, 1, 2, 3, 0);` -> "call argument count"
- CodeGen/call-graph-section-noprototype.c: `void (*fp)() = foo; fp(1);`

Making the default per flavor will change predefines and parse results across the fixture corpus; fixtures without SLATE-FILECHECK-STD would need regenerating (or pinning gnu23). llvm_lit_sweep.py pins gnu17 for the clang flavor so the default does not mask other gaps.

Migrate on fix: the three files above.

title: MS layout: __declspec(align(N)) on a record type is not capped by #pragma pack
MS intrinsics are in the builtin registry but have no IR lowering (_Interlocked*, _bittest*, _setjmp)
description:
Both oracles accept calls to MS intrinsics without a declaration (clang registers them as LangBuiltin ALL_MS_LANGUAGES builtins); slate recognizes them via clang_builtins.rs and then fails in sema/expression.rs lower_expr with `unsupported Clang builtin `X`` in both flavors.

Seen in the sweep:
- _InterlockedAnd (and the rest of the _Interlocked* family: Or/Xor/Exchange/ExchangeAdd/CompareExchange/Increment/Decrement, 8/16/64 and _acq/_rel/_nf variants on aarch64)
- _bittest, _bittestandcomplement, _bittestandreset, _bittestandset, _bittest64..., _interlockedbittestandset/reset (+ _acq/_rel/_nf on aarch64)
- _setjmp, _setjmpex (returns_twice)

Decide per family whether to lower to IR ops (atomics / bit ops) or to an opaque call to the intrinsic name, the way library builtins are handled. The CRT's intrin.h declares these too, so real Windows code hits this through headers as well.

Migrate on fix:
- CodeGen/X86/mskernel-interlocked.c (x86_64), CodeGen/AArch64/mskernel-interlocked.c (aarch64)
- CodeGen/bittest-intrin.c (x86_64, aarch64)
- CodeGen/ms-setjmp.c (i686, x86_64, aarch64)

title: size_t is predeclared under MS compatibility (no #include needed)
description:
`size_t f(void);` with no include:
- clang --target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: accepts; with -fno-ms-compatibility: rejects
- clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu -fms-compatibility: accepts; -fms-extensions alone: rejects
- cl.exe /TC: accepts
- slate --flavor=clang/msvc -target=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: `unknown type name size_t`

So the gate is MS compatibility (implied by the windows-msvc target and by the msvc flavor), not MS extensions. Check what clang does exactly (Sema::Initialize) and whether anything else is predeclared the same way; the type is the target's size type.

Migrate on fix:
- CodeGen/X86/ms-secure-hotpatch-globals.c (x86_64; both oracles)

title: SEH statements __try/__except/__finally/__leave unsupported
description:
clang --target=*-windows-msvc and cl.exe accept structured exception handling in C; slate rejects `__try {` at parse time in both flavors ("expected `;`" / "unexpected tokens after expression").

Needed: parse __try compound-statement followed by __except(filter-expr) compound-statement or __finally compound-statement; __leave; inside a filter, the builtins _exception_code()/GetExceptionCode(), _exception_info()/GetExceptionInformation() (already in the builtin registry as __exception_code/__exception_info), and _abnormal_termination() in a __finally. AST + sema scoping (clang: __leave outside __try is an error; __except filter is a full expression of integral type) + an IR shape. Check ast-enum-touchpoints.md before adding the Stmt variant.

Migrate on fix (llvm_lit_sweep.py):
- CodeGen/exceptions-seh.c (x86_64, i686; both oracles)
- CodeGen/exceptions-seh-nested-finally.c (x86_64, i686; both oracles)
- CodeGen/exceptions-seh-finally.c (x86_64, i686; clang-cl only)
- CodeGen/exceptions-seh-leave.c (x86_64; clang-cl only)
- CodeGen/defer-ts-seh.c also needs -fdefer-ts / _Defer (clang TS, not MS) and -std=c2y, which slate does not accept yet

title: Preprocessor constant-factor costs on windows.h (0.8s vs clang 0.15s)
description: After fmzz the windows_h fixture profile is flat: expand_rescanning ~29% (eager argument pre-expansion for every function-like invocation even when the parameter is only used with #/##; macro_def.clone() of the whole definition per invocation just to restamp expansion/macro_origin), parse ~17%, Lexer::tokenize ~8.5%, SipHash on the String-keyed macro table ~7%. Candidates: FxHash-style hasher, stamp provenance while substituting instead of cloning the def, expand arguments lazily. Benchmark recipe: bd memory perf-benchmark-windows-h.
notes: b6e79ad7 (lazy arg expansion etc) 805->663ms; 4cf62318 (TokenText=Rc<str>) 653->602ms, libc share 50%->35%. Next: lexer (Vec<char> + Vec<usize> offsets per file, String-then-Rc double alloc per ident; emit 5.5%, with_offset 3.7%), pp::syntax::parse 3.8%.
close_reason: windows.h at 602ms vs clang 150ms (~4x), accepted. Reopen if a real-world benchmark is much worse. Remaining leads: lexer Vec<char>+offset table per file and String-then-Rc per ident (~11%), pp::syntax::parse (~4%), 144-byte Span<Token> copies.

title: Refresh MSVC predefines snapshot to match tools/cl.exe 19.51.36257
description: Split from slate-parser-v74.3's comment. src/predefines/msvc_19.51.36256_x86_windows.h pins _MSC_FULL_VER 195136256, but the local cl.exe oracle is 19.51.36257 (195136257). All other i686 predefines probed match. Re-snapshot from tools/cl.exe (and the other MSVC predefines files) so sweep comparisons don't differ on _MSC_FULL_VER.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give IR lowering errors the span of the failing expression
description: Follow-up to slate-parser-zs34. numeric::ResolveError variants other than Names carry no location, so resolve_module falls back to the enclosing top-level declaration's span: an error in a 200-line function underlines the whole function. Attach the span where the error is raised (e.g. InvalidOperands/Unsupported at the operand expression), via ResolveError::loc(), which item_error already prefers. Clang oracle: tests/fixtures/sema_poisoned_declaration.c should point at 's + 1' (2:24), not line 2 col 1.
close_reason: Lowering errors now carry the innermost failing expression/statement span via ResolveError::Located; poisoned fixture points at 2:24.

title: Finish the ast-spec Migration table
description: Leftover from slate-parser-lh7.3, closed with rows still open in wiki/concepts/ast-spec.md ## Migration. Still accurate as of 2026-09-27: FieldItem -> MemberItem/EnumItem; TypeSpecifier variant names/shapes; TranslationUnit.tags indexed by TagId instead of a gappy Vec; Designator::Array/ArrayRange -> Index/IndexRange; bare aligned reads __BIGGEST_ALIGNMENT__ in the parser (src/parser/declarator.rs) instead of an argument-less Aligned resolved by sema; parser calls name-based filter_translation_unit (src/parser/decl.rs) before resolution. The sema.rs row is stale (done via src/sema/validate.rs) and should be deleted. Acceptance: Migration table empty, fixtures regenerated.

title: File-scope extended asm with operands (GCC 15+) is rejected
description: gcc 16 accepts toplevel extended asm, e.g. asm("# %0" : : "i"(7)); at file scope, emitting '# $7'. slate-parser fails with 'expected )' in every flavor. clang also rejects it, so only the gcc flavor should accept. Reachability already marks DeclKind::Asm operands, so the gap is the file-scope parser and sema/lowering.
close_reason: Filed in error: file-scope extended asm already works under --flavor=gcc (slate-parser-25m.5, fixtures asm-file-scope-operands-gcc.c and sema/ir_asm_file_scope_operands_gcc.c); the probe that motivated it ran under the default clang flavor, which correctly rejects like clang. Every gcc-16-accepted form probed (named operands, %c/%cc, E/i floats, &g[2], =m outputs, matching constraints, empty sections, __asm__ in c99) passes. Remaining differences are permissive only: gcc rejects register-allowing constraints (r/g/X), '+' outputs, non-constant i inputs, and a clobber section at file scope; slate accepts them.

title: Model the implicit EAX/EDX:EAX return of functions ending in MSVC __asm
description: When a function's end is reachable, it contains MS asm, and its return type fits EAX or EDX:EAX (integer/pointer up to 8 bytes), add a synthetic return local: every MS asm in the function outputs explicit eax (and edx) into it, and falling off the end returns it. Mirrors clang's return-slot store. x87 st(0) returns are deferred. See wiki/concepts/msvc-asm.md.
acceptance_criteria: winnt.h Int64ShllMod32/ShraMod32/ShrlMod32 lower with a return built from EDX:EAX; fixture compared against clang -emit-llvm.
notes: Implemented i686 MS asm return captures using explicit eax/edx outputs and shared u32 temporaries. Fallthrough::Return(Box<Value>) reconstructs the value only at the function end; explicit returns and control flow need no rewriting, noreturn overrides the fallthrough, and naked functions have no captures. Clang 22.1.8 oracle confirms Int64ShllMod32/ShraMod32/ShrlMod32 return i64 asm =&A, every asm captures even with explicit returns, narrow results truncate, and x86_64 has no capture. Generated fixtures cover both flavors and exclusions. Validation complete: clippy/fmt clean; all 4343 release FileCheck tests passed. See wiki/log/2026-09-27-19-46.md.
close_reason: Implemented explicit eax/edx return captures and value fallthrough; both flavors covered by generated fixtures, compared with clang LLVM IR. Clippy/fmt clean; all 4343 release FileCheck tests passed.

title: Lower MSVC __asm to InlineAsm with Memory operands and Address pieces
description: Lower MsAsm into ir::InlineAsm (dialect Intel). New AsmOperandKind::Memory { place, access } (the asm gets the address; globals and functions as Symbol) and AsmPiece::Address { operand, displacement, base, index, size } at each C-object reference. Size set when explicit or when the instruction has no register operand, plus movzx/movsx, shifts by cl, shld/shrd. Asm-local labels become label pieces so Slate can renumber them. Immediates normalized to decimal. Options: volatile, memory Any, nostack false, preserves_flags false, may_unwind false. See wiki/concepts/msvc-asm.md.
acceptance_criteria: IR fixtures for the example file and winnt.h pattern; ir-spec and ir-grammar updated.
notes: Sema output from 25m.6.2: Lowerer::ms_asm (src/sema/ms_asm.rs) returns Vec<MsAsmLine>, with each operand classified as Register / Segment / St / Immediate / Reference{symbol: Object(Place) | Function(BindingId) | Label, displacement, base, index(reg, scale), size, segment, offset, short}. module.rs calls it and then returns Unsupported; replace that with the real lowering and drop the #[expect(dead_code)] attributes. The ms_asm_names_{msvc,clang}.c fixtures currently only check the unsupported error; they become the positive IR fixtures here.
close_reason: Closed

title: Infer MSVC __asm clobbers and access direction from an effects table
description: Hand-curated conservative table: operand 0 is read+write unless the mnemonic is read-only (cmp, test, bt, push, comis*/ucomis*, ptest, ...); xchg/xadd write both. Implicit defs for mul/div, cdq family, cpuid, rdtsc(p), xgetbv, rdmsr, string ops and rep forms, loop, xlat, cmpxchg(8b), in/out, fstsw ax, lahf, push/pop/pushad/popad/pushfd/popfd/enter/leave. f* mnemonics clobber the x87 stack. Written explicit registers are clobbered; esp writes are covered by nostack=false. Drives Memory access and register clobbers. See wiki/concepts/msvc-asm.md.
acceptance_criteria: Clobber sets match clang's ~{...} lists for the example file (modulo esp/dirflag, which Rust cannot express); fixtures for implicit-def instructions.
notes: From 25m.6.3: src/sema/ms_asm.rs lowers every C object to AsmOperandKind::Memory { access: AsmAccess::ReadWrite } and leaves InlineAsm::clobbers empty. This child refines access per operand and fills the clobbers, working from the classified MsAsmOperand list per instruction (Lowerer::ms_asm).
close_reason: Effects table in src/sema/ms_asm_effects.rs drives Memory access and register clobbers; clang lists equal or supersets on the example and ms_asm_effects.c

title: Resolve names and fold operand expressions in MSVC __asm
description: In sema, resolve each MsAsmExpr::Name to a local/param place, a global (sym), a function (sym), an enumerator, or an asm-local label; undeclared names are errors. Fold member and index byte displacements (arr[4] is byte 4), TYPE/LENGTH/SIZE from C types, and constant arithmetic. Referencing a local marks it used and address-taken. Until the lowering child lands, lowering fails with a clear unsupported error. See wiki/concepts/msvc-asm.md.
acceptance_criteria: Sema fixtures for each name kind, byte-offset indexing, s.b field offsets and TYPE/LENGTH/SIZE, checked against clang -emit-llvm and tools/cl.exe /FAs.
notes: Reachability (src/reachability.rs mark_stmt) treats StmtKind::MsAsm as a leaf today, so a header global or function referenced only from __asm is pruned. Resolve MsAsmExpr::Name there too, alongside src/sema/names.rs. Asm-local labels need a namespace decision against C labels (clang keeps them apart; MSVC-only cross jumps are 25m.6.6).
close_reason: Closed

title: Parse MSVC __asm statements into StmtKind::MsAsm
description: Recognize __asm/_asm (and asm under the Clang flavor) not followed by ( or a GNU qualifier as an MS asm statement. Gate: MSVC flavor x86 only (C4235 elsewhere); Clang flavor on every *-windows-msvc x86 triple, x86_64 included. Boundaries: end of expansion line (line tables; a macro expansion is one line), next __asm, or }; ; comments run to end of line and hide }; merge single-line __asm statements on consecutive lines. AST: MsAsm { instructions: label, prefixes, mnemonic, operands as MsAsmExpr } with MASM radix numbers folded, keyword tokens accepted as mnemonics, case-insensitive registers/PTR/operators, _emit kept as an instruction. See wiki/concepts/msvc-asm.md.
acceptance_criteria: todo/msvc-asm-example.c and the winnt.h Int64ShllMod32 pattern parse on i686-pc-windows-msvc in both flavors; parse fixtures cover boundaries, comments, macros, and flavor/target rejection; ast-spec, ast-grammar and ast-enum-touchpoints updated.
close_reason: MS asm parses into StmtKind::MsAsm: token pre-pass marks lines and strips ; comments, clang's merge rules, MASM operand expressions and radix numbers. Lowering reports unsupported until 25m.6.3. Error fixtures only, per user.

title: Sema inline definition=emitted ignores the windows-msvc GVA rules
description: finish_functions (src/sema/function.rs) decides [definition=emitted|inline_only] with the C99/gnu89 rules only. On a windows-msvc target clang (basicGVALinkageForFunction, isMSExternInline) treats a non-gnu_inline C inline definition as weak_odr when dllexport or any redeclaration is extern, otherwise linkonce_odr (discardable). Observed with tests/fixtures/reachable_inline_from_include_msvc.c: exported_inline prints definition=inline_only though clang emits weak_odr dllexport; with the declarations in the main file, predeclared_inline prints emitted though clang discards it. Reachability already applies the MSVC rule (emits_inline_definition in src/reachability.rs). The IR may also want a discardable (linkonce_odr) linkage for these, rather than only emitted/inline_only.
close_reason: Closed

title: Root emitted inline definitions from included files in reachability
description: defines_external_symbol (src/reachability.rs) skips every inline function definition. Definitions clang still emits — C99 'extern inline', or plain 'inline' under gnu89/gnu_inline — are pruned when they live in an included file and nothing in the main file uses them. Also: a file-scope 'fn_t f;' through a function typedef is rooted as if it were an object definition (harmless, but it keeps an unused declaration). Both would disappear once pruning moves after resolution (ir-spec: Validation and declaration pruning).
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin windows.h on i686-pc-windows-msvc in both flavors
description: Left over from slate-parser-9k8k. On i686, winnt.h's _M_IX86 branch defines Int64ShllMod32/Int64ShraMod32/Int64ShrlMod32 (and a few more) with MSVC __asm { } blocks (winnt.h:1064 in the xwin sysroot), so '#include <windows.h>' fails with 'expected ;' at the __asm in both --flavor=clang and --flavor=msvc until MSVC asm blocks parse (slate-parser-25m.6). Once they do, add tests/fixtures/sema/i686-pc-windows-msvc/windows_h_{clang,msvc}.c checking HANDLE/LONG_PTR are 4 bytes and LARGE_INTEGER is 8-aligned, diffed against clang --target=i686-pc-windows-msvc and tools/cl.exe (x86).
close_reason: windows.h fixtures for both flavors on i686-pc-windows-msvc; sizes and alignment match clang and cl.exe x86

title: Vectors of decimal floats rejected (vector element must be an integer or real)
description: gcc.dg/pr104511.c (gcc accepts with --flavor=gcc): typedef _Decimal32 __attribute__((__vector_size__(16))) D; is rejected by sema/types.rs vector element check (CTypeKind::Float(kind) => !kind.is_decimal()). Verify gcc's rules for DFP vector elements and __builtin_convertvector between _Float64 and _Decimal32 vectors, then migrate pr104511.c into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/. Found while fixing cxg.9.

title: gcc flavor: aarch64 -march/+ext predefines differ from gcc
description: src/target/aarch64_isa.rs models clang. The no-flag baseline matches gcc since 78x3.2, but across 85 -march=armv8.x/9.x(+ext) sets there are 332 macro differences vs aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 16.1: __FLT_EVAL_METHOD__/_C99/_TS_18661_3 = 16 on v9 (fp16), __ARM_FEATURE_SVE_BITS=0 and SVE_PREDICATE_OPERATORS=2, __GCC_DESTRUCTIVE_SIZE 64 (slate 256), FP16_FML on v9, no __ARM_BF16_FORMAT_ALTERNATIVE, no NUMERIC_MAXMIN/QRDMX with +nosimd, COMPLEX with +sve, no MOPS on 8.8 / CSSC on 8.9, +nofp drops FMA/FP16/IEC macros, FAMINMAX/LUT on 9.5, +crypto on 8.4 gives no SHA3/SHA512/SM3/SM4, +nosimd keeps no SVE2, +nofp removes JCVT/FRINT. Reproduce with the macro diff (tools/gcc_macro_diff.py).
close_reason: Closed

title: gcc flavor: x86 feature implications differ (-mavx512f does not imply FMA/F16C)
description: X86Feature::implies is clang's graph: avx512f => avx2+fma+f16c. gcc's avx512f implies only avx2, and -mno-fma does not drop avx512f. X86IsaRequest folds -m flags into masks at parse time, before the flavor is known, so fix by recording the ordered flags and folding at TargetIsa::resolve with the flavor. Only -mavx512* without -march=x86-64-v4 differs (checked with tools/gcc_macro_diff.py over 18 x86 flag sets).
close_reason: Closed

title: Linux targets seed clang predefines for the gcc and msvc flavors
description: Every linux-gnu registry entry (src/target_registry.rs, ALL_FLAVORS) gives --flavor=gcc and --flavor=msvc clang's predefines: gcc defines __clang__/__clang_major__, msvc defines no _MSC_VER (visible in tests/fixtures/sema/target_registry.c). Decide per flavor: gcc should get gcc -dM predefines (gcc is the native oracle); msvc on a non-Windows triple is used as a stand-in for 32-bit MS extensions (sema/ms_mixed_pointers_32_bit.c) until 9k8k lands, after which it could be rejected like gcc on windows-msvc.
close_reason: Closed

title: Keyword aliases lose their spelling when stringized (#__const gives "const")
description:
Keyword tokens don't record how they were spelled. Aliases (__const, __signed__, __inline__, __restrict, __volatile__, _Alignof..., and in MS mode __int8/__int16/__int32 → char/short/int, _int64 → __int64) are printed using the canonical spelling from `From<Keyword> for &str`. So stringizing and -E output are wrong:
  #define S(x) #x
  const char *p = S(__const __signed__);   // slate: "const signed" (13 bytes), clang: "__const __signed__" (19)

clang keeps the source text of every token, so an alias stringizes as it was spelled. The fix is to carry the original spelling on Token::Keyword, or to spell it from the source span when stringizing and printing. Probably the same fix as the keyword-named-macro bead: keep identifiers as identifiers through the preprocessor and turn them into keywords afterwards.
close_reason: Fixed by vp7: stringizing now sees identifiers with their source spelling.

title: clang-cl gaps: clang --target=*-windows-msvc accepts, slate --flavor=clang rejects
description: Gaps where clang --target=*-windows-msvc (clang-cl) accepts and slate-parser --flavor=clang -target=*-windows-msvc rejects. Fixes here are the priority: slate should compile MSVC-style C the way clang does. Children that also fail under --flavor=msvc where cl.exe accepts carry the msvc label too.

title: clang/test MS-mode sweep: clang-cl and MSVC gaps
description:
Three-way sweep of the MS-mode C tests in ~/llvm-project/clang/test (about 450 .c files; only the RUN lines with a *-windows-msvc / *-pc-win32 triple or %clang_cl count) against slate-parser, clang-cl and cl.exe. Same approach as the gcc.dg sweep (slate-parser-cxg).

Oracles:
- clang-cl: clang --target=<arch>-pc-windows-msvc -fsyntax-only, with the slate MSVC sysroot as -isystem. This is the primary target: slate should behave like clang compiling MSVC-style C. The slate side is --flavor=clang -target=<arch>-pc-windows-msvc.
- MSVC: tools/cl.exe /Zs /TC /std:c11|c17|clatest (msvc-wine). The slate side is --flavor=msvc.

Where each result goes:
- Both oracles accept and slate rejects: filed under .1 (clang-cl), labelled clang-cl and msvc.
- Only clang-cl accepts: filed under .1, labelled clang-cl.
- Only cl.exe accepts: filed under .2 (MSVC), labelled msvc.
- Only clang (not cl.exe) accepts in -fms-extensions mode on a non-Windows triple: not a gap. These are migrated as FLAVOR clang fixtures when slate accepts them.

Fixtures migrate to tests/fixtures/suites/clang-test/<dir>__<name>.c. The source is stripped of RUN:/CHECK*: lines, since clang's FileCheck lines would collide with ours.

The header check came first (2026-09-27). Probed as `#include <h.h>` + `int x;` for 33 standard and Windows headers against the x86_64 sysroot. Every CRT header fails in both slate flavors, while clang-cl and cl.exe accept them. The blockers, in the order the preprocessor reaches them:
1. vadefs.h:61 `unsigned __int64`
2. vcruntime.h:96 `__pragma(...)`
3. winnt.h: `__ptr64`, `__unaligned`, `__forceinline`

With those replaced by -D macros, all the CRT headers, intrin.h, windows.h and winsock2.h parse in both flavors. The children below are the real fixes.

title: Stack overflow in debug builds on long binary-operator chains (gcc.dg/inline-24.c)
description:
gcc.dg/inline-24.c expands nested macros B/C/D into a ~2,160-term left-associative `+` chain inside `return`. The release binary handles it; the debug binary (used by tools/update_filecheck.py via cargo run, and by debug cargo test/nextest) aborts with 'thread has overflowed its stack'. Recursion depth scales with chain length somewhere in parse/sema/lowering; make it iterative or bounded.

title: gcc.dg sweep: frontend gaps where gcc accepts and slate-parser rejects
description: Swept all 18,457 gcc.dg C tests (2026-09-27) with tools/gcc_dg_sweep.py: slate-parser parse --flavor=gcc --dump-ir vs gcc -fsyntax-only, using each test's -std/-D/-Wno- options and gcc.dg's -ansi default. Results: 13,875 both accept, 2,742 gcc-only accept (1,305 outside optimizer-only dirs vect/tree-ssa/graphite/ipa/guality/debug/analyzer/sanitizers/gomp/tm), 1,490 both reject, 346 slate-only accept (permissive, accepted cost), 4 hangs, 0 panics. Each child bead is one root-cause cluster and lists the gcc.dg files to migrate into tests/fixtures/suites/gcc-dg/gcc/linux/x86_64/ when it is fixed, plus every other reproducing file, so the sweep does not need redoing to find them.

title: Accept symbolic immediates ("i"(&global), "i"(func)) in asm alternative selection
description: Alternative selection (.15) only takes an immediate whose value is an integer constant, so "i"(&global) or "i"(func) rejects the alternative (not-constant). Both gcc and clang accept these as symbolic immediates (AT&T prints $sym). Recognize addr_of a global or function binding (plus a constant offset?) as a symbol-class choice in the IR. Emitting Rust sym operands (and the $ prefix they need under AT&T) is Slate's lowering, not this crate.
close_reason: Closed

title: gcc flavor skips asm operand validation (alternative count, invalid output lvalue)
description: check_function_asm in sema/validate.rs runs only under CompilerFlavor::Clang, so gcc-flavor sources with mismatched constraint alternative counts ("=r,m"(x) : "r"(x)) or invalid output lvalues get through. gcc rejects both too ('operand constraints for asm differ in number of alternatives', verified). Fixtures asm-sema-gcc.c and asm-hard-register-gcc.c currently contain mismatched counts. Alternative selection tolerates this via the 'missing' rejection reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: Emit Rust asm! from structured InlineAsm
description: Turn the selected InlineAsm (alternative, AsmOperand::selected, width, piece views) into a Rust asm! invocation. Pin reg_legacy (x86-64 R) and vreg_low8 (AArch64 y) to a free explicit register from their set, avoiding the asm's explicit operands, clobbers and reserved registers (rbx/rbp/rsp); no save/restore needed. InPlace inputs pass in(reg) &raw const place and wrap the reference site as ({x}); memory outputs likewise with &raw mut. Rust modifier per reference: the piece view, else the operand width, mapped by the selected class. x86 GPR: 8 l, 16 x, 32 e, 64 r, high8 h. x86 xmm/ymm/zmm: up to 128 x, 256 y, 512 z. AArch64 reg: 32 w, 64 x (an unmodified reference prints the full x register, like Rust). vreg 8-128: b/h/s/d/q. Explicit registers are named at that width in the template, since Rust forbids {n} for them. A view with no Rust mapping (%x0 on a GPR) must fall back. Reserved explicit registers (ebx/rbx, esi on i386) use push/pop.
close_reason: Out of scope: slate-parser stops at IR; Slate's lowering emits Rust asm!. The IR already carries the selected alternative, operand classes, widths and piece views it needs; the description is kept as design notes for Slate.

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Naked functions (25m.17): when FunctionSemantics::naked, emit #[unsafe(naked)] with one naked_asm! built by joining the body's asm templates in order (null statements skipped), renumbering operands across statements; 'i' operands become const (or sym per 25m.22). Their asm has options None. Reject a naked body containing non-asm statements (gcc accepts those).

title: Support -masm=att|intel for GNU asm dialect selection
description: GNU asm on x86 always lowers with AsmDialect::Att because -masm is not a recognized compiler arg. gcc and clang both select the second side of a bare {att|intel} template alternation and print operands in Intel syntax under -masm=intel. Add the arg (see wiki/concepts/compiler-arg-rules.md), thread it to sema/asm.rs where dialect is chosen, and cover it with a fixture that runs sema/ir_asm.c's dialects() cases under -masm=intel.
close_reason: Closed

title: MSVC flavor gives library builtins like exit noreturn, cl.exe does not
description:
Under --flavor=msvc, void exit(int); int h(int x){ if (x) exit(3); return x+1; } lowered exit as [noreturn] (clang_builtin treats Msvc like Clang). cl.exe /O2 keeps the code after call exit, for a compatible void exit(int) and an incompatible int exit(long); MSVC learns noreturn only from __declspec(noreturn). Seen during slate-parser-3vz.

Scope folded in: __declspec(noreturn) is the MSVC analogue of clang's inherited noreturn and already works (it lowers to Attribute::NoReturn, tracked per function, so it covers every declaration and calls lowered before it; cl agrees: a call before the declspec redeclaration is followed by int 3). The fix is subtractive: under MSVC, Library-kind builtins take neither noreturn nor Const/Pure from the registry, declared or implicit. cl /O2 calls isdigit/toupper (Pure) and cbrt (Const) twice in f(x)+f(x); labs is inlined only as an /Oi intrinsic. c_builtin stays (libc identity). Out of scope: MSVC flavor still accepts clang compiler builtins such as __builtin_trap with their semantics, which cl.exe treats as unknown external functions.
close_reason: Closed

title: Incompatible external redeclaration of a noreturn library builtin loses noreturn
description: int exit(long); int g(void){ return exit(2); } lowers exit without [noreturn]. Clang merges every external-linkage declaration of a library builtin's name with its implicit builtin decl; an incompatible type drops builtin status (no BuiltinAttr, no const/pure/nothrow: long abs(long) gets no memory(none)) but noreturn lives in the function type's ExtInfo and is inherited: clang -std=c89 emits declare i32 @exit(i64) #1 with #1 = noreturn. static definitions are not linked and stay plain. Our finish_functions (src/sema/function.rs) gates noreturn on declares_builtin (compatible type), so split: c_builtin/memory stay gated on compatibility, noreturn only on external linkage.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implicit library builtin call before its declaration lowers to two fn decls with the same name
description: int f(int x){ if (x) exit(1); return 0; } void exit(int); int g(void){ exit(2); } lowers to two 'fn @exit' declarations (the builtin_declarations one from the implicit call in f, and the user declaration used by g). They should be one entity, since the later declaration redeclares the implicit builtin. Same for GCC-flavor __builtin_exit followed by a later exit declaration. Seen while doing slate-parser-dyd.23 (src/sema/expression.rs builtin_declaration).
close_reason: Closed

title: Hoisting moves a later operand's side effect ahead of an earlier call
description: 'int plain(int *); int g; int f(int *p) { return plain(p) + (g = 1); }' lowers to 'write(g, 1); return add(call(plain, p), 1);'. Calls are indeterminately sequenced with sibling operands (C11 6.5.2.2p10), so this is allowed, but it contradicts the documented left-to-right (Clang) order: clang calls plain before storing g. An effectful call preceding a hoisted effect should itself be spilled first.

title: gcc flavor: fold const-qualified objects in static initializers
description: Found surveying slate-parser-wxs.5. 'static const int k = 5; int y = sizeof(char[k]);' is accepted by gcc 16 (it folds the const object's initializer), rejected by clang 22 ('initializer element is not a compile-time constant') and cl (C2057). slate rejects it under every flavor with 'nonconstant or unknown identifier', so it is too strict only for --flavor=gcc. Needs gcc-flavor folding of const-qualified objects with constant initializers in the contexts gcc accepts; measure which (enum values and case labels are errors in gcc too).

title: __has_c_attribute always evaluates to 0; answer it from attribute_support
description: const_expr.rs evaluates __has_c_attribute(x) to 0 unconditionally, so a header testing [[nodiscard]] / [[gnu::packed]] support takes its fallback branch where clang, gcc and cl (which defines only __has_c_attribute, not __has_attribute) take the attribute branch. clang returns the standard's date value for standard attributes (e.g. 202003 for nodiscard) and 1 for vendor scoped ones. Needs the scope table in attribute_support.rs (scope_registered / spelling_registered) plus per-standard-attribute values, measured against clang 22.1.8, gcc 16.2.1 and tools/cl.exe.
close_reason: __has_c_attribute answers from attribute_support (per-flavor standard dates, generated per-name scoped lists); __has_* operators visible to #ifdef per flavor

title: Libc identity: recognize libc functions by header provenance + builtin signature
description: Separate from builtin semantics (dyd.45). For the Rust-conversion handoff, a function is libc's when its declaration's outermost-header provenance is a libc header AND its signature matches the builtin registry's library prototype. A user-declared matching strlen keeps builtin semantics but is not libc identity; a header declaration with a mismatched signature is neither. Decide how the IR exposes it (metadata on the function decl?) and update ir-spec.

title: Accept enum constants in aligned and vector_size operands
description: validate.rs is_integer_constant_expression is syntactic and rejects every Identifier, so 'enum { N = 16 }; int x __attribute__((vector_size(N)));' (and aligned(N)) fails with 'layout attribute requires an integer constant expression'. clang and gcc accept enum constants there.

title: Apply declarator-position vector_size and mode to only their own declarator
description: The parser folds type attributes (vector_size, ext_vector_type, mode) from every declarator of a declaration into the shared specifier (src/parser/decl.rs parse_declarator_list), so in 'int x, y __attribute__((vector_size(16)));' or '... mode(QI)' both x and y change type. clang applies a declarator-position type attribute only to that declarator: x stays int.
close_reason: Closed

title: Carry access alignment on IR loads and stores
description: IR loads, stores, and member accesses carry no alignment, so an access through a pointer to an under-aligned type (typedef struct {...} P __attribute__((aligned(1))); P *p; p->b = x;) or into a packed record lowers as if naturally aligned. clang emits align 1 there. Object, field, and _Alignof alignment are modeled (dyd.30); access alignment is not. Repros: gcc-dg/torture__pr52419.c, gcc-dg/torture__pr57748-1..4.c (foo(P *p)). Matters for Rust conversion: an under-aligned place needs read_unaligned/write_unaligned.

title: Support -ffp-contract= and -fcx-limited-range/-fcomplex-arithmetic= compiler args
description: dyd.28 added contract= and range= to float arithmetic with flavor/standard defaults only (clang on; gcc fast for gnu*, off for c*; range full). The command-line flags that change those defaults are not parsed. See wiki/concepts/compiler-arg-rules.md.

title: Represent fast-math permissions from float_control(precise, off) and -ffast-math in the IR
description: dyd.28 records float_control(precise, off) only as contract=fast. Clang also grants reassoc, nnan, ninf, nsz, arcp and afn there (IR shows 'fmul fast'). Per the revised compiler-flags.md rule, permissions a consumer can use belong on the op. Add them to ArithSema::Floating and set them from precise(off) and the -ffast-math family.

title: Lower GNU nested functions under --flavor=gcc
description:
Since slate-parser-dyd.26, StmtKind::NestedFunction is Invalid("function definition is not allowed here") under the clang and msvc flavors, matching clang. Under --flavor=gcc it is Unsupported("GNU nested function"), which is too strict: gcc accepts nested functions. Affected fixtures: nested-function-definition.c, function_definition_declarators.c, and gcc-torture 20010226-1, 20020309-1, 20021204-1, 20030418-1, 20030716-1 and 20031011-1 (gcc-torture fixtures run under the clang flavor today, so they error correctly there).

Needs IR surface that does not exist yet: a nested function captures the enclosing frame by reference (static chain), and taking its address needs a trampoline or an equivalent closure value that stays valid only while the parent frame is live. Decide the IR shape (for example a nested fn with explicit captures plus a closure value, which suits Rust conversion) before lowering. Oracle: gcc -fdump-tree-original / gimple; clang has no support.
acceptance_criteria: Under --flavor=gcc, nested function definitions lower to IR that expresses captured enclosing locals and address-taken nested functions, and the listed fixtures lower under a gcc-flavor configuration. The ir-spec documents the shape.
notes:
Also covers gcc-torture 20010605-1 (folded in from dyd.36): a struct member array sized by a runtime variable (GNU variable-size record member). gcc-only: clang rejects it ('fields must have a constant size: variable length array in structure extension will never be supported'), so it stays an error under every flavor for now. Under gcc such a record has runtime sizeof and runtime offsets for members after the VLA, which needs the same IR design work as nested functions. The repro also needs a nested function.
See slate-parser-dyd.56 (Lower GNU nested functions under --flavor=gcc). These gcc.dg files fail with `unsupported in numeric IR lowering: GNU nested function`.

title: 'defined' is parsed as the preprocessor operator outside #if
description: src/const_expr.rs:1844 treats the identifier 'defined' as the defined-operator in every expression, not only in #if/#elif conditions. 'int defined; int b = defined;' fails with 'unexpected token Semi'; 'typeof(defined)' fails with 'expected integer expression'. clang accepts both. Found while writing the fixture for slate-parser-rdj.
close_reason: Closed

title: Block-scope 'struct T;' must declare a new incomplete type
description: C 6.7.2.3p7: 'struct T;' alone in a block declares a new, distinct struct T that hides the outer one. slate reuses the outer tag: 'struct T; struct T *gt; void f(void) { struct T; _Static_assert(!__builtin_types_compatible_p(struct T*, typeof(gt))); }' fails in slate and passes under clang 22 -std=c23. Found while probing slate-parser-rhg; predates it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Point ignored-attribute warnings at the attribute spelling
description: Ignored-attribute warnings currently use the declaration or declarator span because AST attributes do not retain their own source locations. Preserve attribute spans through parsing and use the specific attribute span for diagnostics.
close_reason: Individual attribute spans are preserved through the AST and ignored-attribute warnings now underline the attribute spelling; fixture expectations match.

title: Named attribute diagnostics beyond applicability: gcc-compat, visibility, alloc-size, underlying-cv-qualifier-ignored
description:
slate-parser-dyd.15 covered the applied-vs-ignored half of the corpus sweep's attribute warning gap and the -Wignored-attributes identity that names it. The sweep also named four diagnostics that are not applicability questions and each need their own rule and measurement:

- gcc-compat: clang warning where its handling of an attribute differs from gcc's.
- visibility: a visibility attribute that conflicts with an earlier one, or with -fvisibility.
- alloc-size: argument indices out of range for the function's parameter list (overlaps slate-parser-dyd.37, invalid attribute arguments).
- underlying-cv-qualifier-ignored: a cv-qualifier on an enum's fixed underlying type.

Measure each against clang 22.1.8 / gcc 16.2.1 before adding an identity.

title: Route record and field attributes through check_attributes
description:
sema::attributes::Subject has Record, but only the declaration-without-declarators path passes it, and there is no Field subject at all. So an attribute written on a struct member or on a tag definition is never checked for applicability: clang drops e.g. visibility, section or malloc on a field under -Wignored-attributes, and applies packed/ms_struct/gcc_struct/scalar_storage_order there, which is the one place they do apply.

Until the field and tag lowering call Lowerer::check_attributes with the right subject, inapplicable(Attribute::Packed, Subject::Record) is dead in one direction: nothing ever asks. Follows slate-parser-dyd.15.
close_reason: Closed

title: Model naked asm functions as an IR function kind
description: naked_asm! selection belongs on the function, not the asm statement. The condition is: the function is __attribute__((naked)) and its body is a single basic asm. Record that as an IR function kind so the backend picks asm! vs naked_asm! from the function rather than sniffing the statement.
acceptance_criteria: A naked function whose body is a single basic asm is marked as such in the IR; fixture covers a naked function and a normal function containing asm.
close_reason: FunctionSemantics::naked from the attribute on any declaration, printed [naked]; fallthrough ub; asm inside has options None. Keyed on the attribute, not body shape, since clang accepts multiple/extended asm in naked bodies. Fixture sema/ir_naked.c.

title: Pick a constraint alternative during lowering
description: Rust asm! cannot express multi-alternative constraints ("r,m"). Something has to choose. Choose during lowering (first alternative that maps cleanly to a Rust register class) and keep the rejected alternatives for diagnostics, rather than pushing the choice onto the backend. Interacts with slate-parser-25m.10: whether an operand is addressed or held in a register depends on which alternative is picked.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-alternative constraints lower to one selected alternative plus the rejected ones; fixture covers "r,m" and "0,m".
notes:
Emission must pin reg_legacy (x86-64 R) and vreg_low8 (AArch64 y) operands to a free explicit register from their set, avoiding the asm's explicit operands/clobbers and reserved regs (rbx/rbp/rsp); no save/restore needed.
InPlace inputs (from .10): memory alternative -> in(reg) &raw const place and wrap the reference site as ({x}); register alternative -> read the place into in(reg).
Rust modifier per reference (from .14): take the piece view, else the operand width, and map it by the chosen class. x86 GPR 8 l, 16 x, 32 e, 64 r, high8 h. x86 xmm/ymm/zmm up to 128 x, 256 y, 512 z. AArch64 reg 32 w, 64 x (unmodified prints the full x register, like Rust). vreg 8-128 b/h/s/d/q. Explicit registers are named at that width in the template, since Rust forbids {n} for them. A view with no Rust mapping (%x0 on a GPR) must fall back.
close_reason: Lowering picks the first alternative every operand can use, records each operand's class and the rejected alternatives; ties and InPlace follow the selection. Emission notes moved to .21.

title: Compute Rust asm options from volatility and clobbers
description: Derive nomem / readonly / pure / nostack / preserves_flags once during lowering from the volatile qualifier and the clobber list, instead of leaving the backend to re-derive them. Per-target caveat: on x86 GCC treats flags as clobbered by extended asm whether or not "cc" was written, so preserves_flags can never be inferred there. The rule is per-target, which is why this depends on the target landing on the node.
acceptance_criteria: ir::InlineAsm exposes computed options; x86 never infers preserves_flags; fixtures cover volatile, non-volatile, with and without a memory clobber.
close_reason: InlineAsm::options (Some for statement asm, None at file scope) derives nomem/readonly/pure/nostack/preserves_flags/may_unwind per flavor and target; x86 never preserves_flags; clang drops memory options for side-effecting asm, gcc keeps them. Fixtures cover volatile, non-volatile, memory clobber, memory operands, goto, basic, aarch64 cc.

title: Carry asm operand width and Rust register modifier
description: Silent-miscompile hazard. In AT&T, %0 for an int operand prints %eax; the Rust equivalent {0} for in(reg) always prints the full-width register (rax). Every operand reference therefore needs an explicit Rust modifier (:e, :x, :r, ...) derived from the operand scalar width, or the emitted asm quietly uses the wrong register size. Place/Value carry types, but the width must be a first-class decision input on the operand, alongside the GCC modifier char (%w0 / %b0 / %k0 / %q0) that is already parsed.
acceptance_criteria: Each asm operand records its scalar width; the IR printer shows it; fixture covers 8/16/32/64-bit operands and an explicit GCC width modifier.
notes: x86 'x' currently resolves to xmm_reg regardless of width (see .13); upgrade to ymm_reg/zmm_reg from the operand's vector width here.
close_reason: Operands carry storage width; width modifiers and x86 tied-input widths resolve to register views on pieces; x widens to ymm/zmm by width

title: Floating literal suffixes accept mixed case; gcc requires one case
description: split_float_spelling in src/const_expr.rs lowercases the whole spelling before matching FLOAT_SUFFIXES, so every suffix is accepted in any case mix. gcc requires the suffix be uniformly one case: it rejects 1.5Df, 1.5dF, 1.5fF16 and 1.5bF16 while accepting 1.5df/1.5DF, 1.5f16/1.5F16 and 1.5bf16/1.5BF16. Affects df, dd, dl, f16, f32, f64, f128, f32x, f64x and now bf16. We accept all the mixed spellings, so a source gcc rejects lowers silently. Fixing it means matching the suffix case-sensitively against both spellings of each entry rather than lowercasing first. Noticed while adding the bf16 suffix (slate-parser-pue).
close_reason: Closed

title: Lex the bf16/BF16 floating literal suffix
description: GCC spells __bf16 limit macros with a BF16 suffix (__BFLT16_MAX__ 3.389...e+38BF16 in src/predefines/gcc-16.*.h). FLOAT_SUFFIXES in src/const_expr.rs has no bf16 entry, and the suffix search is a suffix-match over an ordered list, so 3.4e+38BF16 matches f16 first and leaves a trailing 'b' in the digits -> 'invalid floating literal'. Latent today because the gcc-*.h predefine files are reference data and are not wired into src/pp/mod.rs. Needs FloatSuffix::BF16, a FloatValue::BFloat16(u16) resolved via rustc_apfloat::ieee::BFloat (Token::float_value_bf16), and a numeric.rs arm mapping it to FloatType::BF16. Would also make the BF16 arm of fold.rs float_to_integer reachable. Follow-up from slate-parser-dyd.39.
close_reason: Closed

title: WinArm64 record classification abstains behind the flat gate
description:
record_abi (src/sema/abi.rs) checks the flat gate -- all fields Numeric/Bool/Pointer, non-recursive -- before the convention, so win_arm64 returns native_c for any record with an array or a nested struct in it. Measured against clang -target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc:

  struct { char a[3]; }        clang i64          us native_c
  struct { struct three t; }   clang i64          us native_c
  struct { char a[8]; }        clang i64          us native_c
  struct { char a[16]; }       clang [2 x i64]    us native_c
  struct { char a[20]; }       clang ptr (indirect) us native_c

Unlike win64 (fixed in slate-parser-57a, which classifies on size alone and so needs no field walk), aapcs64/win_arm64 cannot simply move ahead of the gate: the HFA check comes first and does need a field walk, and ours is non-recursive, so struct { struct hfa h; } would be classified as a non-HFA and coerced to [2 x i64] where clang gives [4 x float]. Moving the size rule ahead of the gate without fixing HFA detection would turn a safe abstention into a wrong answer.

Work: make the homogeneous-float check recursive (a record whose fields are all the same float format, at any depth, up to 4 members), then classify win_arm64 and aapcs64 by size ahead of the flat gate. Pin against clang for both aarch64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.

Also unblocks the atomic half: abi_pass still returns Unsupported("atomic aggregate Windows ABI") for atomic records under WinArm64. The cl.exe measurement is already done and recorded in wiki/log/2026-09-21-09-1*.md -- MSVC arm64 classifies the lock-prefixed layout the same way win64 does (struct { long long a, b; } is 16/8 plain and passes in x0+x1, 24/8 atomic and passes indirectly), so once the gate is sorted the rejection can go.
notes: Implemented recursive HFA classification and AArch64 size classification. Clang/MSVC atomic aggregates use qualified integer or indirect ABI; GCC uses ordinary aggregate ABI. Added Windows MSVC, Linux clang, and Linux GCC FileCheck fixtures. Verified clang 22 IR, aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 16.1 assembly, cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release.
close_reason: Implemented and verified AArch64 record and flavor-specific atomic ABI classification

title: Atomic aggregate arguments are rejected on the Windows ABIs
description:
abi_pass (src/sema/abi.rs) returns Unsupported("atomic aggregate Windows ABI") for an _Atomic record or complex argument under AbiConvention::Win64 or WinArm64. That hole was left deliberately by slate-parser-lh7.2.29, which settled only the clang (MEMORY) and gcc (classify as the unqualified record) answers.

slate-parser-rol has since modelled MSVC's _Atomic layout, so the question is now answerable: a lock-prefixed atomic aggregate has a real size (e.g. _Atomic struct { char a[3]; } is 8 bytes, align 4), and Win64 passes an aggregate in a register when its size is 1, 2, 4 or 8 and by reference otherwise. Whether MSVC applies that ordinary rule to the lock-prefixed object, or forces indirect passing the way clang does on SysV, has not been measured.

Measure with tools/cl.exe 19.51 /std:c17 /experimental:c11atomics on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (see wiki/concepts/msvc-oracle.md) across the sizes that straddle the register/reference boundary -- the post-lock sizes 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 -- then either implement the rule or keep the rejection with a measured justification recorded in ir-spec.md.

Note _Atomic is a non-standard experimental opt-in on MSVC, so a warned rejection may be the right answer; the point is to decide it from measurement rather than from absence.
close_reason: Win64 now classifies records by size ahead of the flat gate, which is the real fix: flat is a confidence proxy, not an ABI concept, and win64 needs no field walk. That corrected three plain-record abstentions against the clang oracle (char[3], nested struct, char[8]) and made the atomic case fall out for free, since layout() is already atomic-aware. Matches cl.exe 19.51 for arguments and returns, including the 12/32-byte copies that pin the parameter object as the lock-prefixed one. Fixtures ir_record_abi_shape.c and ir_atomic_aggregate_abi.c under tests/fixtures/sema/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/. WinArm64 still rejects atomic records, split out as slate-parser-o9q (blocked on non-recursive HFA detection). See wiki/log/2026-09-21-09-26.md.

title: Scope enum defined in an if/do condition per C99 condition scope
description: tests/fixtures/parser_control_bodies.c (C99 prefix) fails with 'unknown typedef'. An enum declared inside an if/while/do controlling expression (if (sizeof(enum { T = 1 })) ...) must not leak its enumerator over the file-scope typedef T for the rest of the function; the C89 prefix passes and C99 does not, so the condition's declaration scope is the difference. Split out of slate-parser-dyd.10, which found it but did not cover it.
close_reason: Lowerer scopes if/while/do/switch as a whole under C99+ (control_scoped); fixture updated

title: Lower __bf16 as its own float format
description: FloatingType::BFloat16 hits the 'floating type' Unsupported arm in sema/types.rs base(). Needs FloatKind::BFloat16 plus a new ir::FloatType::BF16 (size 2, align 2, 8 exact integer bits) rather than aliasing F16: bf16 is a truncated f32, so its exponent range differs and FloatType::widens_from's declaration-order Ord would wrongly call bf16 -> f16 a widening. Walk wiki/concepts/type-family-touchpoints.md: Display, storage_of, abi_pass, numeric(), layout.rs ir_type/numeric, render.rs name, and the emit_arithmetic_conversion pairs. Clang accepts bf16 arithmetic and implicit bf16 <-> _Float16 conversions, so both directions need arms. Repro: tests/fixtures/builtin-types.c. Split out of slate-parser-dyd.10.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lex and lower N1169 fixed-point literals
description: The lexer has no r/k suffixes, so a fixed-point value can only come from a conversion. Add the N1169 literal suffixes (r/R for _Fract, k/K for _Accum, with optional u and h/l/ll in either order) to the lexer and const_expr, resolve them to a scaled Number::Integer of the right ir::Type::FixedPoint, and fold them in constant initializers. Depends on the fixed-point type and arithmetic contract from slate-parser-lh7.2.17.4.
close_reason: Implemented N1169 fixed-point literal suffix parsing and IR constant lowering; AST/IR documentation and generated fixture added.

title: [BUG] Lower transparent_union parameter passing
description: `__attribute__((transparent_union))` on a union is refused with `transparent union attribute`. A parameter of a transparent union type is passed as its first member and accepts any member type at the call site, so dropping the attribute gives the wrong ABI for unions whose members do not classify identically. Repro: transparent_union_call.c.
acceptance_criteria: A transparent union parameter takes the ABI of its first member and calls passing any member type lower; transparent_union_call.c produces IR.
close_reason: Closed

title: [BUG] Lower scalar_storage_order and address_space attributes
description: `__attribute__((scalar_storage_order("big-endian")))` and `__attribute__((address_space(N)))` are refused with named diagnostics. Both change how a scalar is stored or addressed and cannot be dropped. Repros: target-type-attributes.c, clang-semantic-attributes.c (GNU).
acceptance_criteria: scalar_storage_order and address_space survive as c_attributes metadata on lowered declarations; expression-valued attribute arguments are folded to integer literals before generic metadata formatting. The focused IR fixture covers these attributes, and clang-semantic-attributes.c produces IR.
close_reason: The requested declaration attributes and resolved integer arguments now pass through existing IR metadata, with focused fixture coverage.

title: [BUG] Lower register asm labels on local and global variables
description: `register int x asm("eax");` and file-scope `register long sp asm("rsp");` are refused with `register asm label`. The register binding is observable through inline asm operands, so it cannot be dropped; the IR has no way to pin a variable to a register. Unrecognized register spellings parse as Register::Other and must behave the same. Repros: asm-labels.c, asm-label-unknown-register.c.
acceptance_criteria: Local and global register variables lower with the register recorded on the binding; both fixtures produce IR.
close_reason: Named register asm labels, including unknown spellings, are preserved on local and file-scope IR variable bindings; both fixtures produce IR.

title: [BUG] Lower the cleanup attribute on automatic variables
description: `__attribute__((cleanup(fn)))` on an automatic variable is refused with `cleanup attribute`. It calls fn with the variable's address on every exit from the enclosing scope, including through goto, break, continue, and return, which the IR has no scope-exit construct for. Repro: pruning-attribute-roots.c.
acceptance_criteria: An automatic variable with __attribute__((cleanup(fn))) lowers to an IR variable carrying the handler name fn; pruning-attribute-roots.c produces IR.
notes: Scope clarified: this bead preserves cleanup(fn) as a dedicated IR variable attribute carrying the handler name for the subsequent Rust lowerer; IR does not currently model scope-exit invocation. Verified pruning-attribute-roots.c now emits [cleanup=cleanup_fn]. cargo clippy --allow-dirty --fix, cargo fmt, and cargo nextest run --release pass.
close_reason: Cleanup handler name is preserved as an IR variable attribute for downstream Rust lowering; pruning-attribute-roots.c produces [cleanup=cleanup_fn].

title: Model memory-constrained asm operands as addresses, not loaded values
description: IR lowering reads an "m"-constrained input operand as a value (`in 2 "0,m" read<i32>(deref(read<ptr<i32>>(%4)))`), which implies a load happens before the asm. A memory operand means the assembler addresses the object itself; the asm may read or write it at any point. Slate needs the address (and the fact that the object is clobbered) to translate this, not a snapshot load. Multi-alternative constraints make this conditional on which alternative the register allocator picks, so the IR probably has to carry both forms or defer the choice.
acceptance_criteria: Memory-constrained asm operands lower to a form that identifies the addressed object rather than a pre-asm load; sema/ir_asm.c covers an "m" input and an "=m" output.
notes: Rust has no m constraint. The translation is in(reg) &raw mut x PLUS rewriting the reference site from {x} to ({x}), so the operand-reference piece must know its operand kind for the emitter to wrap it. This is a local transform at the reference site and needs far less than an instruction parser. Which form applies can depend on the alternative picked in slate-parser-25m.15.
close_reason: Memory-capable inputs lower to AsmOperandKind::InPlace(place) when addressable; outputs already places; memory-only non-lvalue/bit-field (and register var under gcc) rejected; fixtures sema/ir_asm.c memory(), sema/ir_asm_memory_gcc.c, error/asm-memory-*.c

title: Lower __builtin_shufflevector and __builtin_convertvector
description: tests/fixtures/vector_extension_ops.c fails IR lowering with 'unsupported Clang builtin __builtin_shufflevector'. Both builtins are CustomTypeChecking with generic vector operands and a result type derived from the mask length / target type, so neither fits the derived-signature shapes added in dyd.19: shufflevector takes a vector pair plus constant lane indices and yields a vector of the mask's length; convertvector takes a vector and a type. Needs an IR value for a lane permutation and for a per-lane conversion.
notes:
Done (2378 -> 2379 accepted; vector_extension_ops.c was the only corpus fixture, and it also exercises the swizzles from lh7.2.17.7).

__builtin_shufflevector is CustomBuiltin::Shuffle, lowering to ValueKind::Shuffle { left, right, mask }: the constant-index form takes two vectors of the same type and any number of ICE indices over their concatenation (-1 prints as an undef lane), and the result is a vector of the element type with one lane per index, so a narrowing or widening shuffle is fine. The two-argument form takes a runtime integer mask vector of the same lane count and prints mask=dynamic(..), mirroring the existing dynamic(..) spelling for atomic orders and weak.

__builtin_convertvector needed an AST node, since its second operand is a type: ExprKind::ConvertVector { ty, value }, parsed like __builtin_va_arg. It has the same shape as Cast/BitCast/VaArg, so it joined their existing or-patterns in visit.rs, reachability.rs, sema/names.rs and sema/assertion.rs without new arms; the touchpoints page now records that. Lowering reuses the scalar conversion policy rather than restating it: Context::elementwise_conversion runs emit_arithmetic_conversion over the element types and re-types the resulting chain onto vector operands, so int_to_float/float_to_int/widen/truncate/reinterpret all carry their usual exactness and exception metadata, and an int->int conversion that needs both a resize and a reinterpret keeps both steps.

Verified against clang -ast-dump for shuffle result types (3-, 4- and 6-index forms, the dynamic mask form, GNU vectors) and for each convertvector element pair. ast-spec.md, ast-grammar.md, ast-enum-touchpoints.md, ir-spec.md and ir-grammar.md updated; tests/fixtures/sema/ir_vector.c and vector_extension_ops.c pin the forms.
close_reason: Closed

title: GCC personality: __builtin_ prefix on library builtins
description: GCC accepts __builtin_<name> for any library builtin (__builtin_exit, __builtin_puts, ...). Clang 22 rejects these: 'use of unknown builtin __builtin_exit'. Builtins.td only generates a __builtin_-prefixed alias where AddBuiltinPrefixedAlias is set (5 defs), which is why the registry has no __builtin_exit. Since we default to the Clang personality, rejecting it is currently correct and matches the oracle. Repro: tests/fixtures/gcc/gcc-torture/20000105-1.c, a gcc-torture fixture running under the default (clang) flavor. Fix is a CompilerFlavor::Gcc rule in builtins::clang_builtin that strips the __builtin_ prefix and accepts a ClangBuiltinKind::Library match, plus SLATE-FILECHECK-FLAVOR gcc on that fixture. Note the fixture would then be a deliberate slate-accepts/clang-rejects divergence in the --tool both sweep. Also note the GCC semantics: the prefixed spelling bypasses -fno-builtin, which we do not model.
close_reason: --flavor=gcc accepts __builtin_<lib> for Clang Library builtins; binds to a compatible in-scope declaration, otherwise the builtin signature

title: Source-location builtins __builtin_FILE/FUNCTION/LINE/COLUMN
description: __builtin_FILE, __builtin_FILE_NAME, __builtin_FUNCTION, __builtin_LINE and __builtin_COLUMN are Clang keywords (TokenKinds.def), not Builtins.td records, so the generated registry does not contain them and sema reports an unresolved ordinary name. Repro: tests/fixtures/gnu_builtin_source.c (1 configuration). Two prerequisites are missing: the enclosing function's name during lowering (shared with slate-parser-dyd.21), and column information, which ast::Provenance does not carry at all (file, kind, line, system_header only) — __builtin_COLUMN cannot be implemented until the lexer/preprocessor tracks columns.
close_reason: All five source-location builtins implemented. Position comes from the callee token's Loc through the new Files source map (Files now carries the preprocessor's line table and a position() accessor) rather than Provenance, which is stamped per logical line and so cannot supply a column. Line and column verified equal to clang.

title: Propagate builtin NoReturn/Const attributes to call sites
description: The typed registry now carries BuiltinAttribute::NoReturn, Const, Pure and NoThrow, but a builtin call lowers to a plain Callee::Builtin with only c_builtin metadata. IR noreturn lives on FunctionSemantics, which a builtin has no declaration for, so __builtin_unreachable/__builtin_abort calls are not marked as terminating. Decide whether call values carry these attributes and update ir-spec/ir-grammar with them.
close_reason: Builtins lower as functions (implicit or source declaration); NoReturn becomes fn [noreturn]; Const/Pure/NoThrow intentionally not lowered

title: ir::Field has no is_const, so a const record member is invisible in the IR
description: ir::Field carries an Access (volatile + atomic) but no const bit, so 'struct s { const int a; }' prints 'field0 a: i32'. Sema itself is correct: assigning to a struct with a const-qualified member is rejected exactly as clang rejects it, through the C type layer. Only the printed IR loses the fact, which matters because the IR is the handoff to Rust conversion. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 entity audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md.
close_reason: ir::Field now preserves and prints const-qualified record members; fixtures and documentation updated

title: Linkage, storage duration and symbol attributes live on ir::Global, not on the entity
description: The entity record holds the declared QualType and the alignment/common request. Linkage, storage duration, definition state and symbol attributes are computed per declaration in src/sema/module.rs and merged in place on ir::Global / ir::Function by declare_global / declare_function, so module.globals is a second per-object store keyed by BindingId. The epic slate-parser-8lv listed those properties on the entity. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md.
close_reason: Declaration linkage, storage duration, definition state and symbol attributes now merge on entities and project onto IR globals/functions.

title: resolve_parameters duplicates parameter lowering outside the entity table
description: src/sema/types.rs::resolve_parameters lowers ir::Parameter for the standalone resolve_type_module/resolve_module path. It has no Lowerer and so no entity table, hands out BindingIds from a counter, and re-derives restrict/is_const/access from the resolved QualType with a copy of the logic in module.rs::parameters. Found by the slate-parser-8lv.5 entity audit; documented in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md. Either give that path an entity table or factor the projection QualType -> ir::Parameter into one function both call.
close_reason: Factored the QualType -> ir::Parameter projection into TypeResolver::parameter_shape; both module.rs::parameters and types.rs::resolve_parameters call it. This also fixed a live bug: the type-view path used the written (undecayed) type, so any array- or function-typed parameter failed --dump-ir-types with 'unadjusted ABI parameter type'. Entity-table unification for that path is out of scope (needs a Lowerer); noted in wiki/concepts/entity-model.md. Fixture: tests/fixtures/sema/ir_types_parameter_adjustment.c

title: Parameter attributes are blanket-rejected, including ones MSVC accepts
description:
src/sema lowering rejects any attribute on a function parameter with ResolveError::Unsupported("parameter attributes").

Measured 2026-09-19:
- '_Alignas(16) int p' as a parameter: clang errors ("'_Alignas' attribute cannot be applied to a function parameter"), gcc errors ("alignment specified for parameter 'p'"), MSVC 14.51 accepts it silently with /std:c17.
- 'int q __attribute__((aligned(16)))' as a parameter: clang accepts, gcc errors ("alignment may not be specified for 'q'").

By the project's three-compiler consensus rule neither case may be an error, since MSVC accepts the first and clang accepts the second. Both should lower with a named warning from src/diagnostics.rs instead, and the alignment should have no effect on the parameter.

Found while doing slate-parser-8lv.2, which relaxed the equivalent blanket rejection for automatic locals. Left out of that phase because it needs a new warning and its own oracle work, not just the entity's alignment request.
close_reason: Parameter attributes now classified by attributes::parameter_unsupported instead of blanket-rejected; alignment attributes lower with -Wparameter-alignment (new Warning, default on, not pedantic). Deviated from the bead on one point: it said the alignment should have no effect, but re-measurement shows every compiler that accepts a spelling applies it (clang _Alignof(q)=16 and a 16-aligned home slot; MSVC __alignof(p)=32), so the request goes on the parameter entity and _Alignof reads it via declared_alignment, matching clang and MSVC per flavor. Also fixed a quieter bug: trailing ParameterDeclarationKind.attributes were never inspected, so __attribute__((aligned)) after the declarator was silently dropped. Fixtures: ir_parameter_alignment.c, ir_parameter_alignment_msvc.c, ir_parameter_attribute_diagnostics.c. Documented in wiki/concepts/diagnostic-severity.md.

title: Brace elision decides aggregate initializer compatibility on ir::Type
description:
src/sema/initializer.rs:349 decides whether an initializer expression initializes an aggregate member whole (consuming one item) or is brace-elided into its fields by comparing unaliased ir::Type, not C types.

C23 6.7.11 makes this a compatibility question. Within one TU the two answers agree for every ordinary case, because distinct tags get distinct TypeIds and Defined(id) is nominal. They diverge for a compatible-but-separately-defined tag, e.g. a file-scope 'struct S { int x; }' and a block-scope 'struct S { int x; }': C23 says compatible (initialize whole), the IR comparison says Defined(id1) != Defined(id2) and wrongly brace-elides.

Fix: route through CTypes::compatible_unqualified. Blocked on the initializer walk being shaped over ir::Type Shape rather than QualType, which is why it was left out of slate-parser-9ve.6.

Found by the grep audit in slate-parser-9ve.6; recorded in wiki/concepts/c-type-layer.md under the invariant's residues.
close_reason: Closed

title: MSVC models non-lock-free _Atomic aggregates with a lock member
description:
Measured with tools/cl.exe 14.51 /std:c17 /experimental:c11atomics on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, as size/align of _Atomic struct { char a[N]; }:

N:      1    2    3    4    5    6    7    8    9   16   17
size:   1    2    8    4   12   12   12    8   16   20   24
align:  1    ?    4    ?    4    ?    ?    ?    ?    4    4

The rule: when sizeof(T) is already a lock-free width (1, 2, 4, 8) the layout is unchanged. Otherwise MSVC prepends a 4-byte lock, giving size = 4 + round_up(sizeof(T), 4) and align 4. Every padded case measured has align 4, consistent with an int lock member leading the object.

This differs from BOTH personalities modelled in slate-parser-9ve.5: clang promotes to the next power of two (char[3] -> 4/4), gcc does not promote at all (char[3] -> 3/1), MSVC adds a lock (char[3] -> 8/4).

It is also a bigger change than clang's: it alters the object REPRESENTATION, not just size and alignment, so member offsets and the ABI are affected too, and a faithful model needs a hidden field rather than a StorageLayout adjustment.

9ve.5 deliberately left --flavor=msvc on clang's promotion rule rather than invent a half-model; it is no more wrong than before that phase. Fix here, or decide to reject _Atomic aggregates under --flavor=msvc instead of reporting a size we know is wrong. Note _Atomic is an experimental non-standard opt-in on MSVC (/experimental:c11atomics).
close_reason: Modelled MSVC's /experimental:c11atomics layout: lock-free widths (1,2,4,8) keep their size and are aligned to it, everything else gets a leading four-byte lock (struct { int lock; T value; }). Size/align only, no hidden field -- C forbids reaching a member of an atomic aggregate, so interior offsets are not observable. Measured against cl.exe 19.51. Note: MSVC's lock-free-branch over-alignment is spelling-dependent (_Atomic struct S is 4/4, _Atomic T through a typedef is 4/1); not reproduced, we take the elaborated-specifier answer. See wiki/log/2026-09-21-09-09.md.

title: Reject taking the address of a register-qualified variable
description:
6.5.3.2p1 forbids & on an object declared with storage-class register; clang errors ('address of register variable requested'). slate-parser accepts it silently. The bit-field half of the same constraint is already rejected ('address of a bit-field').

Blocked on storage-class tracking: StorageClass::Register currently reaches sema only in validate.rs for asm labels; nothing records register-ness per BindingId. Needs a register set (or a storage class on the binding) threaded from declaration lowering, which fits the declared-entity model of slate-parser-8lv better than the conversion rules of 9ve.3.

Split out of slate-parser-9ve.3, where the rest of the 6.3.2.1/6.5.3.2 lvalue constraints landed.
close_reason: register storage is tracked per binding and address-taking now emits a semantic error for objects and parameters

title: Corpus-wide AST+IR FileCheck and one-shot clang -fsyntax-only sweep
description:
Final step after the structural epics. Today only ~140 of ~2660 fixtures produce IR (SLATE-FILECHECK-ARGS --dump-ir etc.); the rest, including 1637 gcc-torture and 176 gcc-dg fixtures, only check the AST. Gaps in sema/lowering are therefore found one at a time while working on something else.

1. Make every fixture render both the AST and the IR (FileCheck prefixes for each), so the existing suite exercises IR generation. Fixtures that fail lowering record the failure as an expected diagnostic rather than being excluded, so the count of lowering failures is visible and shrinks.
2. Run clang -fsyntax-only (pinned version, per fixture -std/-D/--target/flavor args; see slate-parser-2lv.1) once over the whole corpus and diff against slate-parser: accept vs reject, and which warnings fire. Output a report grouped by diagnostic kind.
3. File the resulting gaps by root cause (one bead per missing rule with the repros listed), not one bead per fixture.

This is the accept/reject oracle; it is much cheaper than the differential IR interpreter (2lv.5) and should surface wxs.4/wxs.5-class gaps in bulk.
acceptance_criteria: Every fixture's FileCheck covers AST and IR output; tools/update_filecheck.py generates both; a one-shot script runs clang -fsyntax-only over all fixtures and emits an accept/reject + warning diff report; the gaps are filed as root-cause beads; cargo nextest run --release passes.
notes:
Baseline update: slate-ir 2617/2693 accepted after dyd.10 (bit-precise literals, GNU omitted conditionals, complex conjugation, sizeof over member paths). Clang-accepted/slate-rejected: 58 -> 35 (clang 22.1.8 sweep, 2575/2689). History: 1861/2673 -> 2195/2674 -> 2324/2674 -> 2345/2674 -> 2347/2674 -> 2354/2674 -> 2363/2674 -> 2378/2674 -> 2379/2674 -> 2504/2687 -> 2554/2687 (dyd.5) -> 2569/2688 (dyd.6) -> 2574/2688 (dyd.7) -> 2582/2688 (dyd.8) -> 2588/2689 (dyd.9) -> 2617/2693 (dyd.10).
dyd.15-.17 rescoped 2026-09-21 under the rule: implement a diagnostic's underlying rule only when it decides acceptance or changes what we lower. dyd.15 -> attribute applicability (IR-observable). dyd.16 -> constant-expression arithmetic only. dyd.17 closed won't-do; the non-cosmetic parts are dyd.44/dyd.45. dyd.43 filed for the live accept/reject divergence found while scoping. The sweep's warning diff stays a gap-finding report, not a parity target.

title: Compound literals with variably modified types: (int (*)[n]){p}
description: lh7.2.24 captures VLA bounds for sizeof(type) and casts via ValueKind::Capture, but ExprKind::CompoundLiteral lowers to a Place (PlaceKind::CompoundLiteral), so the value-level wrapper does not reach it and '(int (*)[n]){p}' still fails with 'nonconstant or unknown identifier'. A VLA-typed compound literal itself is a constraint violation (C11 6.5.2.5p1); only pointer-to-VLA and similar variably modified element types are valid. Needs capture hoisting at the place level (or capturing in the literal's initializer).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture covers a compound literal of pointer-to-VLA type; bound evaluated once at the literal.
close_reason: Compound literals now capture variably modified bounds: type_name_extents runs before resolve_type_name (so layout sees VariableExtent::Captured instead of constant-folding), and the captures wrap the literal's initializer Value via a new captured() helper, which the effects pass hoists to Temporary statements ahead of the literal. with_extents is now a thin Operand wrapper over captured().
